where: Settings > Privacy (claude.ai/settings/data-privacy-controls); same path on mobile
what_it_does: Toggle deciding whether new chats and coding sessions, including Claude Code on these accounts, can be used to train models. Turning it off also stops future use of stored chats.
limits: Not retroactive for training already run; safety-flagged chats still used for safety models. Anthropic does not state the pre-set value; TechCrunch reported it pre-set On.

where: Privacy Center consumer retention article
what_it_does: When the setting is on, new or resumed chats and coding sessions may be kept de-identified in training pipelines for up to 5 years.
limits: Page gives no fixed period for kept chats when the setting is off. Deleted chats leave back-end systems within 30 days. Flagged chats: inputs/outputs up to 2 years.

where: Thumbs up/down buttons on a response
what_it_does: Optional rating. Sending it stores the whole related conversation, de-linked from your user ID, for up to 5 years for research and possible training.
limits: Page describes feedback use separately from the model-improvement setting. Raw connector content is excluded unless pasted into the chat.

where: New chat outside a project > ghost icon
what_it_does: Starts a temporary chat that is not saved to chat history or memory, not used for training, and skipped by past-chat search and the monthly recap.
limits: Still retained for 30 days by default. Not available in projects; cannot be reopened or converted; profile instructions still apply.

where: Settings > Memory
what_it_does: Stops Claude from searching and citing your earlier conversations when answering in new chats.
limits: On by default once rolled out. Incognito chats are never searched; project chats are searched only within that project.

control: Generate memory from chats (Pause memory / Reset memory)
where: Settings > Memory
what_it_does: Turns saved memory from chats on or off. Turning off offers 'Pause memory' (keep, stop using and adding) or 'Reset memory' (delete all, including project memory).
limits: Shared with Cowork when Cowork runs in the cloud. Deleting a chat does not remove memories made from it.

where: '+' menu in a new chat or Cowork task, before the first message
what_it_does: Turns memory off for one chat or task, so Claude neither uses nor adds to memory; the chat stays in history and remains searchable.
limits: Cannot be changed after the first message. Not shown if account memory is off or in incognito chats.

where: Project page > Memory
what_it_does: When turned off, keeps a project's memory fully separate from your account-level memory.

where: Settings > Memory
what_it_does: Opt-in letting memory store topics such as health, religion, politics or gender identity. Turning it off removes sensitive items already saved.
limits: Government ID numbers, criminal history, financial account numbers and immigration status are never saved.

where: Settings > Memory > Topics
what_it_does: View, edit or delete individual remembered topics; you can also tell Claude in chat to forget something. Deletion, not an opt-out.

control: Location data for product features (exact label not given)
where: Privacy dashboard (claude.ai/settings/data-privacy-controls)
what_it_does: Turns off use of IP-based city or region location to improve features such as local web search results.
limits: Country or region inference for security, abuse prevention and terms compliance cannot be turned off. Mobile app and browser extension location is managed in device settings.

control: Allow once / Always allow / Don't allow (iOS permission prompts)
where: In-app prompt; later iOS Settings > Claude, and Settings > Health > Data Access & Devices > Claude
what_it_does: Grant or refuse Claude access to location, calendar, reminders and Apple Health data, per request or later in device settings.
plans: All plans; Health: Pro, Max, US only, beta
limits: Claude suggests these app actions on its own when it judges them useful. Android article describes similar permission requests.

control: Revoke consent for health app integrations
where: Settings (per Consumer Health Data Privacy Policy)
what_it_does: Withdraw consent for third-party health integrations; you may also request to know, access or delete consumer health data.
plans: Residents of Washington or states with similar consumer health data laws
limits: Applies only to users who connect health apps and where these laws apply.

where: Voice mode controls
what_it_does: Makes Claude listen only while you hold the button instead of listening continuously in hands-free mode.
limits: Hands-free is the default. Voice transcripts are saved to chat history like text; microphone access is a device permission.

where: '+' in the chat box > Connectors
what_it_does: Turns a connected app off for one conversation so Claude will not use or proactively suggest it there.
limits: Connected apps can be brought into chats unprompted, using memory for context. Claude confirms before booking or buying; page says no paid placements.

where: Customize > Connectors
what_it_does: Removes a connected service so Claude stops accessing it; also lets you review each service's permissions and access.
limits: Connected services process data under their own terms. Custom connectors are not verified by Anthropic.

control: Connector tool permission: Always allow / Needs approval / Blocked
where: Connector settings (Customize > Connectors)
what_it_does: Per-tool rule deciding whether Claude may use a connector action freely, must ask first, or can never use it.
plans: Pro, Max (Cowork); Team/Enterprise owners can set org-wide
limits: 'Blocked' is denied in every mode. In Auto mode the page's table says 'Claude decides' for 'Needs approval' tools and for write/delete tools set to 'Always allow'. In Skip mode, 'Needs approval' tools are approved without asking.

control: Manually approve / Automatically approve / Skip all approvals (Cowork)
where: Mode selector in the chat box
what_it_does: Sets whether Claude asks before each action, screens each action itself with a safety check, or acts with no checks.
default: Manual in the new Claude experience; not stated for the classic three-mode selector
limits: New Claude experience offers only Auto and Manual, Manual by default. Auto uses more usage. Permanent file deletion always needs approval.

control: Manually approve (Manual) / Automatically approve (Auto) / Skip all approvals (Skip), Claude in Chrome
where: Drop-down on the chat input (Chrome side panel or Claude Desktop)
what_it_does: Chooses whether Claude asks before browser actions, screens its own actions, or acts without asking. Formerly 'Ask before acting' and 'Act without asking'.
default: Automatically approve in the Cowork side panel; not stated for the classic side panel
plans: Pro, Max (paid plans; beta in Chrome)
limits: Cowork side panel defaults to Automatically approve. Purchases, account creation, trades and permanent deletions are blocked in every mode.

control: Allow this action / Always allow actions on this site / Decline; Your approved sites
where: Permission prompt; Claude extension > Extension settings > Permissions
what_it_does: Approve a browser action once or for a whole site, or refuse it; later review approved sites, revoke them and view permission history.
limits: Even on always-allowed sites, downloads, sensitive input, authorizations and permission changes still need approval.

control: Claude in Chrome connector ('Configure' toggle plus per-chat Connectors switch)
where: Claude Desktop > Settings > Connectors > Claude in Chrome
what_it_does: Lets Claude in the desktop app drive your Chrome browser; it must also be switched on in each conversation.
limits: The extension takes screenshots while controlling the browser. Side panel sessions that run as Cowork sessions are saved to history.

control: Pause / Resume / Delete a scheduled task
where: 'Scheduled' page in the left sidebar
what_it_does: Stops or removes recurring tasks that Claude runs on its own in the cloud, even while your computer is asleep or the app is closed.
limits: Each scheduled task is set up with its own approval mode. Upcoming and past runs can be reviewed on the same page. On Pro and Max, scheduled tasks created before October 6 that run on your computer keep running there.

where: Claude Desktop > Settings > General (Desktop app)
what_it_does: Must be switched on before Claude can see your screen and control apps in Cowork or Claude Code on the desktop.
limits: No sandbox; Claude takes screenshots of apps it may use. Not available on Team or Enterprise.

control: Per-app permission prompt and app blocklist (computer use)
where: Prompt when an app is first needed; app blocklist (location not stated)
what_it_does: Claude asks before using each application; apps on your blocklist are refused automatically.
limits: Trading and crypto apps are blocked by default. A link clicked in one app may open in an app you never allowed.

where: Settings > Capabilities (web, desktop, mobile)
what_it_does: Turns Claude's sandboxed code execution and file creation on or off.

where: Settings > Capabilities, under Code execution and file creation
what_it_does: Controls whether Claude's code sandbox can make outside network requests, such as installing packages. When on, the page says it can reach a listed set of approved domains (package registries, GitHub, Anthropic services).
limits: Does not limit connectors (MCP), which can still send data out.

where: '+' menu in a chat
what_it_does: Turns web search, and fetching of linked pages, on or off for a chat.
limits: The new Claude experience has no toggle; Claude searches when it decides to. Image results come from Bing.

where: Formerly Claude Desktop > Settings > General
what_it_does: Former option to keep Cowork tasks running locally. Removed for Pro and Max; new tasks run on Anthropic's servers and users cannot switch back.
limits: Removed October 6, 2026. Local folders are reached only through the open desktop app; earlier local and scheduled tasks keep running locally.

where: Three-dot menu next to a task, or Tasks list > trash icon
what_it_does: Removes a Cowork task from task history at once; back-end copies are deleted within 30 days. Deletion, not an opt-out.

where: Sidebar or 'Chats and tasks' > three-dot menu > Delete; multi-select supported
what_it_does: Removes a chat from history immediately; back-end copies are deleted within 30 days. Deletion, not an opt-out.
limits: Projects and account data stay until you delete them or the account.

where: Settings > Account (web); Profile (iOS, Android)
what_it_does: Permanently deletes the account with its conversations and projects. Deletion, not an opt-out.
limits: Paid plans must cancel and let the subscription lapse first; some cases need support.

where: Settings > Privacy > Shared chats; or Share menu, Public to Private
what_it_does: Lists chats you shared by link and revokes access to a shared snapshot.
limits: Chats are private unless shared. Attached files and raw MCP tool data are not included in shared snapshots.

where: Settings > Privacy (web or desktop)
what_it_does: Emails a download link with your account data and chat history. Portability tool, not an opt-out.
limits: Not available on iOS or Android; the link expires 24 hours after delivery.

where: anthropic.com footer; claude.ai Learn More overflow menu
what_it_does: Lets visitors refuse analytics and marketing (targeted advertising) cookies; necessary cookies cannot be refused.
limits: Listed marketing cookies include Google, Facebook, Reddit, TikTok and Twitter; analytics include Google Analytics and LinkedIn.

where: Browser or extension setting; Privacy Policy Section 4
what_it_does: Anthropic states it honors GPC as an opt-out of sharing personal data for targeted advertising of its own products.
limits: Policy says Anthropic does not 'sell' personal data. No separate Do Not Sell or Share link or US state notice found.

where: Anthropic marketing emails
what_it_does: Opts you out of future direct marketing messages.

control: Privacy rights requests (know, access, deletion, correction, objection, restriction, withdraw consent)
where: Email privacy@anthropic.com (the 'contacting us' link in Section 4 is a mailto to this address); appeals to the same address
what_it_does: Ask Anthropic to act on legal privacy rights, including objecting to processing based on legitimate interests; authorized agents may file.
plans: All users, depending on local law
limits: Rights depend on where you live; Anthropic may decline with a lawful reason; requests about training data are limited.

control: Request no overseas transfer (Republic of Korea)
where: Email privacy@anthropic.com and contact the Data Protection Officer at dpo@anthropic.com
what_it_does: Korean users may ask that their personal data not be transferred overseas.
plans: Users in the Republic of Korea
limits: Anthropic may then be unable to provide some or all services.

control: Privacy rights requests relating to training data
where: Contact link in the Privacy Center article
what_it_does: Anyone can object to, or ask for erasure or correction of, personal data in material used to train models, under laws such as GDPR.
limits: Anthropic says it cannot easily find one person's data in training material; requests may be declined.

where: Claude Console > Settings > Privacy controls
what_it_does: Opt-in letting Anthropic train on the organization's Claude Code sessions sent via the first-party API; leaving stops new sharing.
plans: Prepaid API organizations; invoice-billed by request
limits: Without it, commercial data is not used for training by default. Shared data is kept up to two years. ZDR organizations are not eligible.

where: Arranged with Anthropic sales, enabled per organization
what_it_does: Anthropic does not store prompts or responses after returning the API response, for eligible endpoints and features.
plans: Claude API; Claude Platform on AWS on request; approval required
limits: Excludes Console, Batch, Files, code execution, MCP connector, Managed Agents. Covered Models need 30-day retention. Flagged content kept up to 2 years.

control: Standard data retention (30-day retention), per-workspace setting
where: Claude Console > Data retention page (platform.claude.com/settings/privacy), workspace selector
what_it_does: Lets a ZDR organization switch one workspace to standard retention so Covered Models work there, while other workspaces keep ZDR.
default: off (workspaces follow the organization's ZDR setting until 'Standard data retention (30-day retention)' is selected)
limits: The Default Workspace always follows the organization setting; enabling requires accepting retention terms.

where: Claude Console > Data retention page > HIPAA compliance card
what_it_does: Applies HIPAA safeguards to the organization and makes the API reject features not covered by the BAA.
limits: Permanent once enabled. Does not cover Console use, Claude Code, Bedrock, Google Cloud, or beta features unless listed.

where: Files API
what_it_does: Delete uploaded files, or set automatic expiry between 1 hour and 90 days at upload; otherwise files persist until deleted.
limits: Expiry is not guaranteed deletion; content may be kept briefly for safety review and metadata stays visible up to 30 days.

where: cache_control in Messages API requests
what_it_does: Optional 1-hour prompt-cache lifetime at extra cost; without it the cache has a 5-minute minimum lifetime that resets each time the cached content is used, and expired entries are deleted promptly but not immediately.
plans: Claude API (also cloud platforms listed in docs)
limits: Caches are isolated between organizations and per workspace on the Claude API.

where: Messages API parameter or workspace default; Workspace geo in Console
what_it_does: Restricts model inference to US infrastructure instead of the 'global' default; workspace geo sets where data is stored at rest.
limits: Supported on Claude 4.6 and later models; older models return an error.

where: Messages API request body
what_it_does: Optional opaque end-user ID; developers can omit it or send a hash. Anthropic may use it to detect abuse.
limits: Docs say not to include names, emails or phone numbers.

where: tools array when using the MCP connector
what_it_does: Choose which tools from a remote MCP server Claude may call, by allowlisting or denylisting individual tools.
plans: Claude API (beta, header mcp-client-2025-11-20); also Claude Platform on AWS and Microsoft Foundry (beta)
limits: MCP connector is not ZDR-eligible; data exchanged with MCP servers (tool definitions and results) is kept under Anthropic's standard retention policy.

control: permission_policy for MCP toolsets (always_ask / auto / always_allow)
where: Managed Agents agent tools configuration
what_it_does: Makes server-run MCP tools wait for your approval, be judged per call by the server, or run freely.
limits: MCP toolsets default to always_ask. Running sessions keep the policy they started with.

control: permission_policy for the agent toolset (always_ask / auto)
where: Managed Agents agent tools configuration (default_config.permission_policy)
what_it_does: Requires approval, or per-call server review, for built-in agent tools that otherwise run automatically.
limits: The agent toolset defaults to always_allow. Custom tools run by your app are outside these policies.

where: Managed Agents API
what_it_does: Session transcripts persist until the developer deletes them. Deletion, not an opt-out.
limits: Managed Agents are not ZDR-eligible.

control: Client-side tools (computer use, bash, text editor, memory tool)
where: Tool definitions in Messages API requests
what_it_does: These tools run in the developer's environment, so screenshots, files and memory stay there under the developer's control rather than stored by Anthropic.
limits: Memory tool storage and its retention are controlled by the developer.

where: Arranged with the Anthropic account team; events in the Compliance API Activity Feed
what_it_does: Records each human view of retained prompt or response content by Anthropic staff, under a published reason code.
plans: Eligible Claude API organizations, including Claude Code used with an API key and Claude Platform on AWS; not Batch or Files, claude.ai Enterprise seats, consumer plans, Microsoft Foundry, Bedrock or Google Cloud
limits: Not self-serve. Visibility only, not an opt-out of review; automated processing is not logged.

where: Contact Anthropic Support; individual Console users ask their owner
what_it_does: Deletes an API organization or member account on request. Deletion, not an opt-out.
limits: Organization deletion must be requested by the Primary Owner.

control: Privacy Choices / global privacy controls (Anthropic websites incl. Console)
where: Cookie settings on Anthropic sites; browser GPC
what_it_does: Refuse analytics and marketing cookies on Anthropic web properties (cookie domains include .anthropic.com) through cookie settings or GPC.
limits: Covers website cookies, not API traffic. No API-specific sale or sharing control found.

control: SDK OpenTelemetry trace-context propagation off (open_telemetry={'propagation': False} or ANTHROPIC_OPEN_TELEMETRY_PROPAGATION=false)
where: SDK option open_telemetry={'propagation': False} or ANTHROPIC_OPEN_TELEMETRY_PROPAGATION=false
what_it_does: Stops the SDK from sending your app's trace context (traceparent) and baggage headers to the API with each request.
limits: Beta. Spans go to your own exporter, not Anthropic. The page gives a non-privacy reason (avoiding duplicate headers). No opt-out was found for Anthropic's own logging of API traffic.

where: Shift+Tab in CLI; mode selector in VS Code or Desktop; --permission-mode; permissions.defaultMode
what_it_does: Claude asks before most file edits, shell commands and network requests; reads inside working directories run without asking.
default: off for interactive terminal and VS Code sessions on v2.1.283 or later; still the built-in start for claude -p and Agent SDK sessions that fetch feature flags, HIPAA-configured organizations (v2.1.285 or later), and sessions where auto mode is turned off or unavailable
limits: From v2.1.283, auto (not Manual) is the built-in starting mode only for interactive terminal and VS Code sessions; see default for the cases that still start in Manual.

where: Same mode controls
what_it_does: Auto-approves file edits and common filesystem commands such as mkdir or mv; other actions still prompt.

where: Same mode controls
what_it_does: Claude explores and proposes a plan; file edits are blocked until you approve it.
limits: When auto mode is available, the classifier reviews shell commands during planning instead of prompting (useAutoModeDuringPlan, on by default). In interactive terminal sessions with bypass permissions available, plan mode's edit block is not enforced.

where: Same mode controls
what_it_does: A separate classifier model reviews actions before they run instead of you (reads and working-directory edits skip it), blocking actions that go beyond the request, target unrecognized infrastructure, or seem driven by hostile content.
default: on for interactive terminal and VS Code sessions on v2.1.283 or later (earlier, only Pro, Max and Team); claude -p and Agent SDK sessions that fetch feature flags and HIPAA-configured organizations start in Manual
plans: All plans and providers, supported models only; Team and Enterprise admins can turn it off
limits: Not a safety guarantee; explicit ask rules still prompt. Organizations can disable it; unsupported models fall back to Manual.

where: --permission-mode dontAsk or permissions.defaultMode; never in the Shift+Tab cycle; cloud sessions ignore it from settings files
what_it_does: Denies any action that would normally prompt; only pre-approved tools and in-directory reads run. Meant for locked-down CI.

where: Mode cycle when enabled; CLI flag
what_it_does: Runs every action without prompts; intended only for isolated containers or VMs.
plans: Local sessions on all plans; Desktop needs the 'Allow bypass permissions mode' toggle on Pro and Max (organization policy on Team and Enterprise); VS Code needs its 'Allow dangerously skip permissions' toggle; not available in cloud sessions or from Remote Control
limits: Deny rules, explicit ask rules and critical-path removals such as rm -rf ~ still stop it.

where: /permissions dialog; permissions.allow, ask, deny in settings.json (user, project, managed)
what_it_does: Pre-approve, always prompt for, or block specific tools, commands, file paths or web domains.
limits: Rules apply deny, then ask, then allow. A Bash deny rule does not catch the same program by path or inside sh -c.

where: Managed settings (or any settings file)
what_it_does: Removes auto mode, so sessions cannot use classifier-based approval and start in Manual.
plans: Team, Enterprise and any deployment using managed settings
limits: A running session leaves auto mode when the setting arrives from an admin-deployed source.

where: Managed settings
what_it_does: Prevents anyone from entering bypassPermissions mode.

where: settings.json (any scope)
what_it_does: Makes file tools refuse reads outside your working directories in every mode, including bypass.
default: off (unset; reads outside the working directories then follow your permission mode)
limits: Shell commands are handled differently and may prompt instead. Requires v2.1.257 or later.

where: /sandbox command or settings files
what_it_does: Operating-system limits on which files and network domains Claude's shell commands can reach; allowed domains start empty.
limits: Does not govern built-in Read, Edit or WebFetch tools. If it cannot start, commands run unsandboxed unless failIfUnavailable is set.

where: Hooks in settings files (/hooks to view)
what_it_does: Custom scripts run before a tool call and can block it, for example destructive shell commands.

where: Any settings scope; enforce from managed settings (allowManagedMcpServersOnly: true makes the managed allowlist the only one)
what_it_does: Admins allow only approved MCP servers or block specific ones; users can block servers for themselves.
default: off (unset; by default any MCP server can be connected)
limits: Without allowManagedMcpServersOnly, allowlists from user, project and local settings merge in, so users can widen the allowlist; denylists merge from every scope.

control: Network access: None / Trusted / Full / Custom (cloud environments)
where: Cloud environment dialog (claude.ai/code, Desktop, mobile)
what_it_does: Limits outbound connections from cloud sessions: none, a default allowlist, any domain, or your own list.
plans: Pro, Max, Team; Enterprise premium or Chat + Claude Code seats
limits: Default level is Trusted. GitHub proxy, enabled connectors and the Anthropic API stay reachable even at None.

where: claude.ai/settings/data-privacy-controls
what_it_does: Consumer users choose whether Claude Code sessions may train future models; commercial accounts are not trained on by default.
plans: Free, Pro, Max (choice); Team, Enterprise, API (no training by default)
limits: Retention: 5-year if allowed, 30-day if not; commercial standard is 30-day.

where: Claude Code command
what_it_does: Opens your privacy settings from the CLI to view or change them.

where: Organization admin opt-in
what_it_does: Organization-level opt-in letting Anthropic train on Claude Code sessions sent through the first-party API.
plans: Commercial API organizations; not Bedrock or Google Cloud

control: Zero Data Retention (Claude Code on Claude for Enterprise)
where: Enabled by Anthropic per organization; not in admin settings
what_it_does: Claude Code prompts and responses are not stored by Anthropic after the response, except for legal or misuse reasons.
plans: Qualified Claude for Enterprise accounts (API-key route: see the ZDR row under the API product)
limits: Disables cloud sessions; excludes claude.ai chat, Cowork, analytics metadata and third-party MCP data.

where: Environment variable (or env in settings.json)
what_it_does: Stops usage metrics (latency, reliability, usage patterns) sent to Anthropic and third-party logging.
plans: Claude API connections; off by default on Bedrock, Google Cloud, Foundry, Claude Platform on AWS
limits: Metrics exclude code, prompts and file paths. Also stops feature-flag fetching, which can disable Remote Control.

where: Environment variable
what_it_does: Stops error messages and stack traces from being sent to a third-party error tracking service.
plans: On for Pro and Max sign-ins on v2.1.198 or later via the Claude API; otherwise off
limits: Known patterns of secrets, file paths, email addresses and other personal information are redacted before sending; off for ZDR or HIPAA organizations.

where: Environment variable
what_it_does: Disables /feedback (and /bug, /share), which send conversation history including code to Anthropic.
plans: Claude API connections; off by default on third-party providers
limits: Reports are kept 5 years; on Bedrock or Google Cloud they are saved locally instead.

where: Environment variable; settings file
what_it_does: Turns off, or lowers the frequency of, the 'How is Claude doing this session?' rating prompt.
limits: The rating alone sends no transcript. Also off when DISABLE_TELEMETRY, DO_NOT_TRACK or nonessential traffic is disabled.

control: No / Don't ask again (transcript sharing prompt)
where: Follow-up shown after the session rating
what_it_does: Declines uploading the session transcript and logs; 'Don't ask again' stops future requests.
plans: All; not shown to ZDR organizations
limits: If 'Yes', transcripts are uploaded as-is (known keys redacted), kept up to 6 months, and not used for training.

where: User or managed settings
what_it_does: Stops Claude from drafting feedback reports on its own for you to review; 'quiet' keeps drafting but hides the cards.
limits: Default value is 'notify'. Drafts are not sent until you choose to send them.

where: Environment variable
what_it_does: One switch that turns off telemetry, error reports, feedback reporting and surveys.
limits: Does not stop the WebFetch hostname check or official plugin marketplace auto-install.

where: settings.json
what_it_does: Stops WebFetch from sending each requested hostname to Anthropic for a safety blocklist check.
limits: Only the hostname is sent. Skipping removes the blocklist, so pair it with WebFetch permission rules.

where: settings.json (any scope)
what_it_does: Sets how many days local session transcripts and app data are kept before automatic deletion.
limits: Default 30, minimum 1. Transcripts are plaintext; Desktop and Cowork transcripts need desktopSessionCleanupPeriodDays.

where: Environment variable; flag with -p
what_it_does: Stops Claude Code from writing transcripts and prompt history to disk.
limits: The flag works only in non-interactive mode; the Python Agent SDK has no equivalent.

where: CLI command
what_it_does: Deletes one project's local transcripts, auto memory, task and debug files and matching history lines after showing a plan. Deletion, not an opt-out.
limits: Pasted images and session scratchpads in the temp directory are not removed.

where: Cloud session controls (see 'Delete sessions' docs)
what_it_does: Permanently removes a cloud session's event data. Deletion, not an opt-out.

where: /memory toggle or settings.json
what_it_does: Stops Claude from reading or writing the auto memory notes it keeps across sessions.
limits: CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_AUTO_MEMORY overrides it for one session.

where: /config
what_it_does: Turns off the one-line summary Claude generates in the background when you return to an idle terminal.

where: /config or user settings
what_it_does: Stops Claude from resuming a task unattended after a plan usage limit resets.
plans: Interactive sessions signed in with a claude.ai subscription
limits: '/config key=value' can turn it off but not back on.

where: Environment variables used with CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_TELEMETRY=1
what_it_does: OpenTelemetry export to your own collector is opt-in; prompt text, tool inputs and tool output stay redacted unless these gates are set.
limits: OTEL_LOG_RAW_API_BODIES exports full conversation bodies if enabled.

where: settings.json
what_it_does: Change or hide the AI attribution Claude adds to commits and pull requests, and omit claude.ai session links.
limits: Session links are added only for cloud and Remote Control sessions.

control: I agree to receive marketing communications (checkbox)
where: Dana page > "Request More Info" form
what_it_does: Optional checkbox on the Dana sign-up and demo request form that asks for consent to marketing email.
limits: Seen in the live form Oct 16, 2026 (box starts unchecked). The same form has a required privacy policy agreement box. Form not submitted.

where: General Privacy Notice > 13. Your Choices
what_it_does: Stop marketing email by using the unsubscribe instructions in any marketing email.
limits: Administrative and support messages continue after opting out.

where: General Privacy Notice > 9. Privacy Rights
what_it_does: Ask Applied Intuition to stop processing your data that relies on legitimate interests, or that is used for direct marketing.
limits: Applied can refuse for compelling grounds or legal claims. Keeps a suppression list. Request via privacy@applied.co or contact form.

where: General Privacy Notice > 9. Privacy Rights
what_it_does: Ask Applied Intuition to block processing in some cases, for example while you dispute accuracy or object.
limits: Only in certain circumstances. Rights listed as ones you 'may' have, so availability depends on local law.

where: General Privacy Notice > 9. Privacy Rights
what_it_does: Withdraw consent where Applied relies on it, which the notice says covers cookies and direct marketing where local law requires consent.
limits: Does not affect processing done before withdrawal.

control: Rights in relation to automated decision-making
where: General Privacy Notice > 9. Privacy Rights
what_it_does: Right not to be subject to decisions based only on automated processing, including profiling, that have legal or similarly significant effects.
limits: Does not apply when needed for a contract with you or when you gave explicit consent. Not tied to Dana in the text.

where: General Privacy Notice > 8. Notices to California Residents; 9. Privacy Rights
what_it_does: Ask Applied Intuition to delete your personal information. California residents also get a deletion right. This is deletion, not an opt-out.
limits: Applies where there is no good reason to keep processing it, or after a successful objection. For California requests, identity and residence may need checking.

control: Right to opt out of sharing (California)
where: General Privacy Notice > 8. Notices to California Residents
what_it_does: California residents can opt out of sharing personal data for third-party advertising by contacting Applied Intuition or an authorized agent.
limits: Contact method is privacy@applied.co or the contact form. Identity and residence may need checking.

where: General Privacy Notice > 8. Notices to California Residents
what_it_does: Notice tells users to turn on GPC in the browser to opt out of shares that use cookie identifiers.
limits: Test Oct 16, 2026 (US connection): consent tool config had respectGPC false; simulated GPC changed nothing, Google Analytics, DoubleClick and Hotjar still loaded.

control: Do not sell or share my personal information
where: Cookie banner on appliedintuition.com > "Opt-out preferences" > "Save my preferences"
what_it_does: Opts the browser out of the site's third-party analytics and advertising cookies.
plans: Website visitors shown the US banner
limits: Seen in live banner Oct 16, 2026 from a US connection. Before any choice, all cookie categories were set on. Website only, not Dana data.

where: Cookie Policy > 3. Disabling the use of Cookies; cookie banner; browser settings
what_it_does: Accept, reject or tailor non-necessary cookies (analytics, functional, advertising) through the banner, or block and delete cookies in the browser.
limits: Necessary cookies are placed without consent; the policy says they can only be blocked in browser settings, which may break parts of the site. On Oct 16, 2026 the US banner showed only an opt-out link, and footer 'Cookie Settings' linked to this policy page.

where: General Privacy Notice > 1. Personal Information Collection
what_it_does: Applied says that wherever it uses cookies it will not collect personal data without your permission.
limits: May conflict with what I saw Oct 16, 2026 (US connection): analytics and ad trackers loaded before any banner choice.

where: General Privacy Notice > 4. Personal Information Sharing; 8. Notices to California Residents
what_it_does: Applied states it does not sell, rent, license or lease personal information and does not sell under the CCPA.
limits: Does not say whether it 'shares' for ads. Cookie Policy says advertising cookie data may go to advertisers and agencies.

where: General Privacy Notice > 13. Your Choices
what_it_does: Applied states it does not respond to Do Not Track or similar signals.
limits: Same notice separately says GPC can be used for cookie-based shares.

where: General Privacy Notice > 1. Personal Information Collection
what_it_does: May automatically log device details, IP address, features used, actions taken and IP-based rough location when you use the website or software platform; uses Google Analytics.
limits: No product-level setting found. Cookie controls (APP-10, APP-11) cover the website only.

where: General Privacy Notice > 2. Personal Information Use
what_it_does: Personal information is used to improve the Service, build new features, personalize your experience and make de-identified or aggregated statistics.
limits: No opt-out named. Right to Object (APP-03) is the only stated route. AI model training is not mentioned.

where: General Privacy Notice > 4. Personal Information Sharing
what_it_does: May disclose data to service providers (including advertising, marketing and analytics), advisors, deal parties, government authorities and current or future affiliates.
limits: No control to limit this sharing is described, apart from the California sharing opt-out (APP-08).

where: General Privacy Notice > 6. International Transfers
what_it_does: Data may be moved to affiliates or providers in the US, Germany, Japan, Korea and Sweden, or anywhere Applied or its providers operate; for EEA, UK and Swiss data it uses EU standard clauses or the UK transfer agreement where required.
limits: No customer choice of data region is stated for Dana.

where: General Privacy Notice > 7. Retention
what_it_does: Keeps data only as long as needed for the stated purposes, generally while you interact with Applied, based on listed factors.
limits: No fixed period and no user or admin choice of retention, and no zero data retention option found.

control: 保有個人データに関する開示等の請求 (Requests for Disclosure of Retained Personal Data)
where: Privacy Policy for Japan > Section 5
what_it_does: Under Japan's APPI, ask Applied Intuition GK to stop using, erase, or stop giving your data to third parties; also access and correction.
limits: Hub page says this policy covers data collection vehicles in Japan, but its text covers service users generally. Affiliate sharing is consent-based.

where: Bystander Privacy Notice > Your rights
what_it_does: People filmed by Applied's data collection vehicles can ask to access, delete, restrict or object to processing of non-anonymized sensor data.
plans: Bystanders of data collection vehicles in EEA/UK
limits: Only non-anonymized data, which is kept up to 28 days. Depends on local law. Request via privacy@applied.co.

control: How we preserve your privacy with anonymization
where: Bystander Privacy Notice > anonymization; Data retention
what_it_does: Raw camera, plate and location data from data collection vehicles is anonymized within up to 28 days, then the raw copy is deleted. Raw EEA data is processed only on Applied systems in the EU; only anonymized data is sent to other countries.
limits: Applies only to EEA/UK data collection vehicles, not to customer vehicles or Dana.

control: To develop, train, test and improve our ADAS and AD systems
where: Bystander Privacy Notice > Why do we need this information?
what_it_does: Anonymized sensor data, including anonymized bystander images, is used to train and test Applied's driving systems, based on legitimate interests.
limits: No opt-out once anonymized. Objection (APP-21) only reaches data in the up to 28-day window before anonymization.

where: Products page > Tools for Vehicle Intelligence > Modular and Composable
what_it_does: The workflow SDK can run workflows in the cloud, on-premises or in air-gapped settings.
limits: Stated for the Tools for Vehicle Intelligence SDK, not for Dana agents. Whether this keeps data away from Applied is not stated.

where: Products page > Tools for Vehicle Intelligence > Built for Physical AI at Scale
what_it_does: Product page says access controls let teams scale usage without breaking compliance or slowing down.
limits: Marketing line only. No settings, roles or scope documented publicly.

where: Dana launch blog > Building the Flywheel Behind Autonomy
what_it_does: Dana keeps every workflow result traceable, with full lineage, so results can be traced back through each workflow step.
limits: No control found to limit, export or delete these records, and no retention period stated.

where: Blog: The Future of Vehicle Software Is Agentic
what_it_does: Applied says Dana for SDVs has engineering guardrails built in to meet high safety standards.
limits: Vague claim. No approval steps, autonomy levels or confirmations described.

where: Tanzu Operations Manager > AI Services tile (downloaded from Broadcom Support)
what_it_does: AI Services is a separate Tanzu Operations Manager tile, downloaded from Broadcom Support, that hosts LLMs on Elastic Application Runtime VMs managed through Ops Manager.
limits: Docs do not say whether the tile is off by default; it is a separate download. The MCP Gateway (release notes v10.4.0) and the agent buildpack and tile uninstall (Enable the Agent Buildpack page) are on other pages, not this one. Formerly GenAI on Tanzu Platform for Cloud Foundry (title of the 10.2 docs PDF).

where: AI Services tile > Errands > Post-Deploy Errands
what_it_does: Installs agent_buildpack so developers can cf push AI agents. Leaving it Off keeps the agent runtime out of the foundation.
limits: Technical preview, not for production. The Delete Agent Buildpack pre-delete errand removes it on tile uninstall by default.

where: VI admin installs it as a Supervisor Service; org admin enables it in a namespace of a VCF Automation organization
what_it_does: Model endpoints, agents, MCP and knowledge bases work only in namespaces where admins install and activate Private AI Services.
plans: Private AI Services on VMware Private AI Foundation with NVIDIA 9.1 (VCF 9.1)
limits: Scope is per namespace.

control: Model Runtime only / Enable Full Service
where: Private AI Services configuration wizard > Service Resources (full set of capabilities or Model Runtime only); to add the full set later: Service Configuration tab > Service Capabilities > Enable Full Service (separate page)
what_it_does: Admins can activate model serving only, leaving out MCP server integration, Data Indexing and Retrieval, and Agent Builder. The full set can be added later.
limits: The 'Service Capabilities' row and 'Enable Full Service' button are documented on https://techdocs.broadcom.com/us/en/vmware-cis/private-ai/foundation-with-nvidia/9-1/deploying-private-ai-foundation-with-nvidia/installing-and-configuring-private-ai-services/enable-the-full-set-of-private-ai-services-capabilities.html, not on the cited page.

control: Vendor statement: models and data stay in your network
where: AI Services > Quickstart Guide for vSphere > Before you begin (also Overview, 'Privacy' feature)
what_it_does: Broadcom says that after install, models and data stay inside the Elastic Application Runtime network and foundation VMs make no outbound calls to outside APIs or services.
limits: Internet access is needed during install unless Offline Model Support is used. Off-platform model integrations (BRC-08) send prompts to outside providers. The Network Communications reference also lists outbound 443 calls from worker VMs to the NVIDIA license server when a model needs vGPU (the license server can be cloud CLS or on-premises DLS).

control: VMware Tanzu Platform transparency notice: hosting and processing location
where: Product Privacy Transparency Notice
what_it_does: Lists Tanzu Platform as on-premise software; any data customers feed it, possibly sensitive, is hosted and processed on customer premises.
limits: Notice says it is non-contractual and may change. Links a sub-processor list.

control: VMware Private AI Foundation with NVIDIA transparency notice: hosting and processing location
where: Product Privacy Transparency Notice
what_it_does: Lists the product as on-premise software; customer data, possibly sensitive, is hosted and processed on customer premises.
plans: VMware Private AI Foundation with NVIDIA (on-premise)
limits: Non-contractual. Notice links 9.0 docs and predates Private AI Services 3.0 cloud model routing.

where: AI Services tile > Off-Platform Models (OpenAI Compatible, Anthropic, AWS Bedrock, Azure OpenAI, Google Vertex AI)
what_it_does: Operators decide whether to connect outside model providers. Requests to those models then go to the provider; removing the model stops it.
limits: Network Communications page lists outbound 443 calls to ChatGPT, Bedrock, Gemini only when external integration is enabled. No Broadcom statement on provider data use.

control: InferenceGatewayRoute (Connect to a Remote Model Running in the Cloud)
where: Private AI Services namespace via kubectl (InferenceGatewayRoute resource and API token Secret)
what_it_does: Org or VI admins can connect a namespace to cloud models (Google Gemini, Vertex, OpenAI-compatible); prompts for those models then go to that provider.
limits: New in Private AI Services 3.0 (page says 'Starting with Private AI Services 3.0'). The 3.0 release date, September 3, 2026, is in the Private AI Services release notes, not on this page. Provider data terms not described.

where: AI Services tile > model configuration > Model URL; Tutorials > Offline Model Support
what_it_does: Pulls models from an internal artifact store instead of the internet (Ollama registry, Hugging Face) during install, for air-gapped setups.
limits: Docs say models are pulled from the internet by default. Covers model downloads, not prompt data.

where: AI Services tile > Advanced Config
what_it_does: Sets request/response logging: OFF, Log to file only, Log to file and database (bodies redacted), Trace to file only, Trace to file and database (full bodies).
limits: OFF stops logging of model requests and responses. Per the AI Services release notes (not this page), v10.4.2 (June 18, 2026) added the file-only levels and renamed DEFAULT and TRACE.

where: AI Services tile > Advanced Config
what_it_does: Sets how many hours audit records stay in the AI Services database.
limits: Does not affect log files; BOSH Director log rotation controls those.

where: AI Services tile > Advanced Config > Active Profiles; per-request store parameter
what_it_does: Journaling (beta) saves prompts and responses only when an operator adds the journaling profile and a request sets store: true.
limits: Beta. Journal can be exported in OpenAI fine-tuning and Bedrock distillation formats for the customer's own use.

where: AI Services > Store and Retrieve Transactions with Journaling (Beta)
what_it_does: Journaled transactions are kept in the internal PostgreSQL database for 48 hours, then deleted.
limits: Broadcom says future versions might allow longer storage.

where: MCP Gateway app logs (Tanzu Hub > Workloads > Apps > Logs, cf CLI, or forwarded logs)
what_it_does: Each MCP Gateway instance writes start and stop records for every MCP call, with method, tool name and caller identity.
limits: Methods matching skip patterns (ping by default) are not logged. Caller field may contain PII such as email.

control: Request payload logging / response payload logging
where: MCP Gateway audit configuration
what_it_does: Optional logging that adds tool-call arguments and results to MCP audit records. When off, only metadata such as tool name is kept.
limits: Docs do not name the setting or say how to change it. Large responses may be omitted or truncated.

control: auth (mode: none, forward_token, oauth_passthrough; service-instance OIDC)
where: cf create-service / update-service mcp-gateway -c (mcp-servers[].auth); cf bind-service -c auth
what_it_does: Sets how the MCP Gateway authenticates users to on-platform and off-platform MCP servers, from no auth to token forwarding or OIDC through Tanzu SSO.
limits: Mode none (default) adds no auth; binding without -c registers a server with no auth. OAuth for off-platform servers is technical preview.

where: Agent app: user-provided service tagged mcp-server, then cf restage
what_it_does: Developers choose which MCP servers an agent can call by binding them. Unbinding and restaging removes the server and its tools.
limits: Agent loads all bound mcp-server services at startup. No per-tool approval documented for the buildpack.

where: Agent chat UI > MCP server panel
what_it_does: MCP servers that need a token make each user authenticate in the chat UI. Tokens stay in memory for that session and are not shared across users.
limits: Users must re-enter tokens after a restage or session expiry. Per the AI Services release notes (not this page), bearer-token MCP servers were added in v10.4.2.

where: cf set-env <agent> TANZU_AGENT_ENABLE_DEBUG_UI false, then restage (or manifest.yaml)
what_it_does: Hides the agent debug panel, which shows run stats, the system prompt, tool definitions and MCP server status.

control: Policy tab: Rate Limits, Quotas, Webhooks (technical preview), Custom (technical preview)
where: AI Services tile > Policy; assign under Plan Config > Policies
what_it_does: Operators cap requests or tokens per plan and can call webhooks on chat or embedding traffic, for example a content filter.
limits: Webhook and custom policies are technical previews, not for production. No built-in content filter documented.

where: AI Services tile > Plan Config
what_it_does: Models are usable by developers only after an operator adds them to a plan; service access controls whether the plan shows in the Cloud Foundry Marketplace.
limits: Per-org restrictions not described on these pages.

where: Tanzu Platform agent foundations
what_it_does: Agents reach models, tools, data or the network only through explicit grants and service bindings set by platform operators.
limits: From Broadcom blogs; no techdocs page found. The Aug 31, 2026 blog 'Tanzu Platform: The Agent Platform for VMware Private AI Cloud' adds disposable sandboxes destroyed after each session, and the Aug 31, 2026 press release lists hardened deny-by-default sandboxes among capabilities due for GA in Fall 2026.

control: Human-in-the-loop permission levels: "always deny", "always allow", "request before taking action"
where: Agent Buildpack (announced at VMware Explore 2026)
what_it_does: Will let organizations set each agent's autonomy: block actions, allow them, or require a request before acting.
plans: Tanzu Platform Agent Buildpack (announced Aug 31, 2026 at VMware Explore 2026)
limits: Announced only ('will also be adding'). Not in AI Services 10.4 docs as of Oct 16, 2026. GA in Fall 2026 is stated in the Aug 31, 2026 press release (https://www.broadcom.com/company/news/product-releases/64646), not in this blog.

where: Tanzu Platform AI gateway (announced at VMware Explore 2026)
what_it_does: Will let platform teams write regex rules to enable or disable an MCP server's tools; disabled tools are hidden from agents on that gateway endpoint.
plans: Tanzu Platform AI gateway (announced Aug 31, 2026 at VMware Explore 2026)
limits: Announced only. Not in AI Services 10.4 docs as of Oct 16, 2026. The Aug 31, 2026 press release says capabilities announced there reach GA in Fall 2026; neither the press release nor this blog gives a date for tool filtering itself.

where: Private AI Services UI > Agent Builder > MCP > MCP Servers
what_it_does: Admins review the tools a connected MCP server offers and approve only suitable ones; agents can use only approved tools from the tool gallery.
limits: Tool calling only; MCP prompts, sampling and resources are not supported.

control: Session management: Chat history max length, Truncation strategy, Session expiration
where: Agent Builder > Create Agent wizard
what_it_does: Developers cap how much chat history an agent keeps per session (oldest removed first) and set the days after which idle sessions are deleted.
limits: FIFO is the only truncation option. Defaults not stated.

where: Private AI Services > Configure Service > Observability, or activation wizard
what_it_does: Turns on Prometheus metrics collection in the namespace and sets how long metrics data is kept.
limits: Docs say turn on 'if required by your organization'; default not stated.

where: Private AI Services > Configure Service > LLM Traces
what_it_does: Sends traces of agent runs and knowledge base indexing to an OpenTelemetry Collector that the admin chooses.
limits: Collector endpoint is set by the customer; docs do not describe traces going to Broadcom.

control: Model sharing: entitled organizations for a provider instance
where: Private AI Services activation (provider instance settings)
what_it_does: In VCF 9.1.1, admins list which VCF Automation organizations may use a provider instance's shared models.
limits: In VCF 9.1.0, all organizations can access a provider instance. New in Private AI Services 3.0.

where: Data Indexing and Retrieval > Knowledge Bases
what_it_does: Unlinking a data source removes its chunks from the vector database at the next indexing run.
limits: Deletion, not opt-out. Must unlink from every knowledge base to fully remove the data.

control: Validate and Upload an ML Model to a Model Gallery
where: Deep learning VM sandbox, then vcf pais models push to a Harbor model gallery
what_it_does: MLOps engineers check models (hashes, malware and serialization scans, safety tests) before publishing them to a gallery that developers use.
limits: Described as a workflow; docs do not say unvetted uploads are blocked.

control: Customer Experience Improvement Program (CEIP) via Telemetry tile
where: Tanzu Operations Manager > Telemetry tile (install and accept terms; uninstall to leave)
what_it_does: Tanzu Platform product analytics go to Broadcom only if the Telemetry tile is installed and configured. Uninstalling the tile leaves CEIP.
limits: Docs call CEIP strictly opt-in and say the tile sends nothing until configured.

control: Telemetry Programs: Operational Data / CEIP Data
where: Telemetry tile > Telemetry Settings
what_it_does: Pick which streams to send: Operational Data (a limited set of Tanzu Platform usage data, required for app and service instance usage) and/or CEIP Data (broader configuration and user experience data).
limits: Checking only one stream sends only that stream. Operational Data is described as required for Tanzu Platform (BRC-36).

where: Telemetry tile > Telemetry Settings
what_it_does: Keeps telemetry data on disk without sending it to Broadcom.

control: Operational data required for Tanzu Platform
where: Telemetry documentation overview
what_it_does: Broadcom states Tanzu Platform requires Operational Data (usage data) to be shared with Broadcom.
limits: Cites KB article 371562. The tile still shows Operational Data as a checkbox.

where: VMware Usage Data Programs > Customer Experience Improvement Program
what_it_does: Standard sends configuration, feature use and performance data; Enhanced adds product logs. Customers can generally pick the level.
limits: Uses include product improvement, customer insights and sales outreach. Tanzu Platform and Private AI Services are not in the CEIP product table.

where: VCF Operations > global settings
what_it_does: Controls whether VCF Operations sends anonymous usage data to vmware.com.
limits: On by default for new installs and upgrades. Not AI-specific. A deactivation made in 8.14 carries forward.

where: VCF Fleet LCM Service API: PATCH /fleet-lcm/v1/components/<componentId>/config
what_it_does: Turns CEIP participation on or off for a VCF Automation cluster, where Private AI Services is managed.
limits: API only per docs; pods restart during the change.

where: broadcom.com cookie banner or Cookie Settings
what_it_does: Visitors can accept all cookie categories or allow only essential cookies.
limits: Website only. Live banner says continuing to use the site counts as agreement.

where: Cookie icon or 'Cookie Settings' link on broadcom.com
what_it_does: Lets visitors switch off Functional, Performance and Targeting cookies; targeting cookies let ad partners build interest profiles.
limits: Choices stored per browser. Essential cookies cannot be turned off. The notice also describes Social Media cookies, but the live Preference Center shows no separate Social Media toggle.

control: Do Not Sell or Share My Personal Information
where: Cookie banner for California visitors; Privacy Preference Center
what_it_does: California visitors can opt out of cookie-based 'selling' or 'sharing' under the CPRA by allowing only essential cookies.
limits: Broadcom says it does not sell personal data for money. Covers cookies only. No separate US state privacy notice found.

where: Cookie Notice > Using An Opt-out Signal; Privacy Policy
what_it_does: If the site detects a GPC signal, Broadcom opts that browser out of non-essential cookies. The privacy policy says the same for Do Not Track.
limits: Applies per device and browser, cookies only. Not tested live.

control: Network Advertising Initiative / Digital Advertising Alliance opt-out
where: Cookie Notice > How Are Third-Party Ad Networks Used?
what_it_does: Cookie Notice points visitors to NAI and DAA tools to stop targeted ads from member ad networks.
limits: Third-party tools; non-targeted ads may continue.

where: Supplemental VMware Products & Services Privacy Notice
what_it_does: Users of VMware-branded services can change cookie settings in the service and use Fullstory's opt-out link to stop session recording.
limits: Notice does not say which services use these tools. Also names Pendo and Google Analytics.

where: Marketing emails; Broadcom preference center
what_it_does: Stops marketing and other non-transactional emails.

where: Privacy Policy > Your Rights; California toll-free line
what_it_does: Request access, correction, erasure, restriction, objection to processing, or consent withdrawal.
plans: Broadcom as controller (not customer data under a DPA)
limits: Rights vary by location. Broadcom answers only requests validated through the form. Erasure is deletion, not opt-out.

control: Statement on automated decisions with AI
where: Privacy Policy > How Does Broadcom Use Your Information?
what_it_does: Broadcom says it does not use AI tools for solely automated decisions with legal or similar effects, or for EU AI Act high-risk purposes.
limits: Covers Broadcom's processing of personal data, not customer AI deployments.

control: Private AI tenet 'Data privacy and control'
where: Broadcom news: VMware's Approach to Private AI
what_it_does: Says an organization's data stays private and is not used to train, tune or augment commercial or open-source models without its consent.
limits: A 2023 architectural principle, not product docs or contract terms for AI Services 10.4 or Private AI Services 3.0.

where: Workspace: username > Settings > Workspace admin > Advanced > Partner-powered AI features toggle; Settings API (the page does not name an API key)
what_it_does: Controls whether AI assistive features use partner-hosted models (Azure OpenAI, OpenAI on Databricks, Anthropic on Databricks). When off, some features switch to Databricks-hosted models and others become unavailable.
plans: Default on for workspaces without the compliance security profile; off for CSP workspaces
limits: Where the setting is on, the account and workspace toggles are already disabled, so the UI can only turn it on. The Settings API can still turn it on or off until Nov 1, 2026, when the setting is removed; after that, contact the account team.

where: Account console > Settings > Feature enablement > Enable partner-powered AI features + Enforce (the page does not name an API key)
what_it_does: Account admins set the partner-powered value for all workspaces and can enforce it so workspace admins cannot override it.
limits: Default shown is for the partner-powered value; Enforce default not stated. Removed Nov 1, 2026. Changes are recorded as account audit log events.

control: Compliance security profile (effect on AI features)
where: Enhanced security and compliance settings (account or workspace)
what_it_does: On CSP workspaces, partner-powered AI features start disabled and some AI assistive features, including Genie Code, are also disabled unless admins enable partner-powered features.
limits: Conflicts with a July 2026 release note on Genie Code for HIPAA CSP workspaces; see other_observations.

control: Enforce data processing within workspace Geography for Designated Services
where: Account console > Workspaces > [workspace] > Security and compliance tab
what_it_does: When on, Designated Services (AI assistive features, Foundation Model APIs and others) process content only in the workspace Geo. Turning it off allows cross-Geo processing.
default: off (cross-Geo on) for non-CSP workspaces in Geos outside the US and EU; not stated for others
plans: Cross-Geo processing is on by default for non-CSP workspaces in Geos outside the US and EU
limits: Databricks says data is not stored outside the workspace Geo either way. Per-feature Geo availability is on the Designated Services page.

where: Account console > Settings > Feature enablement > toggle to disable Genie
what_it_does: Turns off account-level Genie One for all users, which stops it sending extra Databricks-generated metadata (asset IDs, usage signals, audit events) to US-based services.
limits: Does not affect workspace-level Genie One. Its managed databricks-system-workspace can only be removed by contacting Databricks support.

where: Account console > Previews; workspace username menu > Previews
what_it_does: Account admins (account console > Previews) and workspace admins (username menu > Previews) use toggles to turn individual preview features on or off. Account-level previews apply to all workspaces.
limits: Default state depends on release type. Several AI Beta pages say an admin must turn the preview on.

where: Manage Databricks previews page (notice)
what_it_does: During Private Preview, Databricks may collect and use data about the feature, such as inputs and outputs, to develop and test it.
limits: No separate opt-out described; applies only to features in Private Preview.

control: Web search in Genie Code and Genie One
where: Workspace Previews page
what_it_does: Lets Genie Code and Genie One search the public web and cite sources. An admin must turn the Beta preview on.
plans: Needs partner-powered on and Americas/Europe Geo or cross-Geo; on CSP only HIPAA
limits: Beta.

where: Account console > Usage > Budgets > Create budget (Unity Gateway resource, tag databricks-product: genie)
what_it_does: Account admins set shared and per-user monthly spend thresholds that send alerts or block Genie usage once reached.
plans: Pay-as-you-go Genie usage (charges for Genie Code usage beyond the free monthly allowance began Jul 8, 2026)
limits: Cannot remove a user's free monthly usage, so it cannot fully stop Genie. Blocking is approximate.

where: Catalog Explorer, per object
what_it_does: Comments are generated only when a user requests one for an object, then reviewed before saving. There is no workspace or catalog toggle to disable the feature.
limits: Partner-powered setting only changes the host (Azure OpenAI or Databricks).

where: Genie Code settings > Actions (Ask first / Auto-approve); per request: Allow, Skip, Ask every time, Allow in current chat, Always allow
what_it_does: Sets whether Genie Code asks before using tools (running code, editing notebooks, querying tables) or lets an AI classifier approve actions that match the request.
limits: Default for every chat is Auto-approve. Databricks says it is not a security boundary and advises keeping it off for production data. Added Jun 4, 2026.

where: Genie Code scheduled tasks
what_it_does: Scheduled Genie Code runs always auto-approve tool actions, with an AI classifier blocking risky ones. Users cannot turn this off for scheduled runs.
limits: Runs use the creator's Unity Catalog permissions.

control: Genie Code scheduled tasks: pause, edit, delete
where: Full page Genie Code > Schedules > task details (toggle off, Edit, kebab > Delete)
what_it_does: Users can pause, edit, or delete recurring Genie Code tasks that run prompts in the background as full sessions.
limits: Each run creates a new chat. Runs count toward Genie usage.

control: Genie One scheduled tasks and code execution
where: Genie One sidebar > Schedules / Scheduled tasks > task
what_it_does: Users can edit or delete scheduled chat tasks that run automatically and email results. Before running sandboxed code, Genie One checks it matches the request or task instructions.
limits: In scheduled tasks, code execution is allowed by default; Genie One declines code it cannot match to the instructions.

control: Service policy ASK (approval before MCP tool call)
where: Unity Gateway > MCPs > [MCP] > Policies > New policy
what_it_does: Admins attach policies that allow, deny, or pause an MCP tool call for user approval before it runs, based on request content and caller.
plans: Beta (account admin enables on Previews page)
limits: On model services an ASK result blocks instead. Policies fail closed; Log mode records without blocking. Not supported for Agent Services.

control: Agent pause for human input (resume / interrupted)
where: Agent Bricks CLI agents: invocation API input field resume
what_it_does: Agents built from Agent Bricks CLI templates can pause for human input, such as approving a tool call; the client sends resume in the same session to continue.
limits: Developer must build the pause into the agent; no platform-wide approval setting described.

where: Workspace admin enablement; MLflow UserAuthPolicy api_scopes when logging the agent
what_it_does: Lets a Model Serving agent act as the querying user with tokens limited to declared API scopes.
limits: Disabled by default; a workspace admin must enable it. Agents may reach sensitive resources the user can access.

control: Unity Catalog permissions limit AI data access
where: Built into AI assistive features
what_it_does: Data sent to AI assistive feature models follows each user's Unity Catalog permissions. Genie Agents and Genie One chat run only read-only SQL.
limits: Genie Code can run code and write to data the user can access.

where: Ask in the Genie Code chat (no separate settings page)
what_it_does: Genie Code saves durable facts about you, your data and projects on its own. You can ask what it remembers, or ask it to update, forget, or delete memories.
limits: Page says there is no separate settings page; no off switch or admin control described.

where: Ask in a Genie One conversation
what_it_does: Genie One saves a memory when you ask, or after you approve a suggested one, and applies it to later chats. Ask in chat to update or delete it.
limits: Memories are private to the user. No global off switch described.

where: Genie One chat
what_it_does: Genie One draws on your own past conversations to shape answers and cites them. Databricks describes it as always available with no setup.
limits: No off switch described.

where: Workspace Previews page
what_it_does: Shows suggested questions built from your recent activity, favorites and asset metadata. An admin must turn the Beta on; otherwise generic questions appear.
limits: Uses only metadata and the user's own permissions.

where: Agent code (Lakebase-backed session store, memory store, memory pipelines; actor field)
what_it_does: Developers decide whether a custom agent keeps session history (Lakebase-backed session store) and long-term memory (memory store, memory pipelines), group sessions by actor_id, and can delete sessions (a force option cascades to child sessions).
limits: Deleting a session or session store does not delete memories already derived from it.

control: Reviewable by agent managers (Genie Agent conversation sharing)
where: Genie Agent > chat history > kebab > Share: Private / Reviewable by agent managers / All account users
what_it_does: Sets who can view a Genie Agent conversation. Private hides results from agent managers.
limits: Default for new conversations is Reviewable by agent managers. Under Private, managers still see your prompts in the monitoring tab.

where: Genie Agent > history > trash icon > Confirm and Delete Chat
what_it_does: Deletes a chat thread from your history and from managers' history pages. Otherwise chats are kept until the agent is deleted.
limits: Deletion, not opt-out. Query results persist for seven days.

where: Full page Genie Code > chat list > kebab menu > Delete
what_it_does: Users can delete, rename, copy, or share their Genie Code chats.
limits: Deletion, not opt-out. Chat history is stored with notebook content; admins can view a chat with a direct link. Post-deletion retention not stated.

where: Genie One chat > Uploaded files
what_it_does: Files uploaded to a chat are stored in a Unity Catalog managed volume with no fixed retention or lifecycle policy, until you remove them or delete the conversation.
plans: Beta; admin enables Genie One File Upload preview
limits: Files are private to the conversation and the uploader.

control: No training of third-party GenAI models (Service Specific Terms 5(c))
where: Service Specific Terms, Databricks AI Commitments
what_it_does: Databricks will not use Customer Content, Inputs, or Outputs to train, re-train, or fine-tune GenAI models it makes available to third parties.
limits: Wording covers models offered to third parties only.

control: Product improvement use of Inputs and Outputs (Service Specific Terms 5(b))
where: Service Specific Terms, Databricks AI Commitments
what_it_does: Databricks may collect and use Inputs and Outputs to develop, improve, operate and support its services, but only if the use is solely for the customer's benefit or does not identify the customer or disclose its confidential information to third parties.
limits: Subject to restrictions in the Documentation. No opt-out described.

where: Databricks AI assistive features trust and safety
what_it_does: Databricks does not use data, prompts, or responses from AI assistive features to train generative foundation models it makes available to third parties.
limits: Same third-party-model scope as the Service Specific Terms.

control: Model Serving no training or service improvement
where: Model Serving > Data protection
what_it_does: For paid accounts, Model Serving does not use inputs or outputs to train any models or improve any Databricks services.
limits: Free accounts not addressed on this page.

control: Free Edition content license (includes AI training)
where: Databricks Free Edition Terms
what_it_does: Free Edition users give Databricks a perpetual license to their content and usage data, including to train and improve AI models.
limits: No opt-out described. No date shown on page.

control: Partner zero data retention (AI assistive features)
where: Databricks AI assistive features trust and safety
what_it_does: Partner model providers do not store prompts or responses sent through AI assistive features, even for abuse monitoring; zero data retention endpoints are used.
limits: Covers AI assistive features, not Foundation Model APIs.

where: Model Serving > Data retention
what_it_does: Databricks may store Foundation Model API inputs and outputs for up to 30 days in the workspace region, only accessible for security or abuse response.
limits: No opt-out described on this page. Container build logs kept up to 30 days, metrics up to 14 days.

control: Opt out of data retention (Foundation Model APIs)
where: Not documented; referenced on supported models page
what_it_does: Page says customers who opt out of data retention cannot use Claude Fable 5 or 5.1, implying a retention opt-out exists.
limits: No setting, form, or process found in the docs opened.

control: Partner provider safety retention and human review
where: Model Serving > Partner model provider data retention; supported models page
what_it_does: Partner providers may keep data for safety via automated scans before limited human review. Fable 5/5.1 prompts and responses kept 30 days and may be flagged for human review.
plans: OpenAI: classifier-flagged GPT-5.5+ traffic from coding and routing customers; Anthropic: all Fable 5 and Mythos-class traffic
limits: No opt-out described other than not using these models.

where: Settings > Advanced > Access Control; Settings API key customerApprovedWSLoginExpirationTime
what_it_does: Workspace admins allow or block temporary Databricks staff logins (up to 48 hours, or always) for outages, security events, or support.
limits: Staff access is approval-gated, time-limited and audit-logged.

where: AI Gateway > model service > Inference tables > Set Up / edit > Disable inference tables
what_it_does: Logs raw request and response payloads of a model service to a Unity Catalog Delta table; owners can disable logging.
limits: Must be enabled per endpoint (unified trace page). Payloads over 10 MiB are not logged.

control: Enable usage tracking / Enable inference tables (AI Gateway legacy)
where: Serving endpoint page > Gateway section > Edit AI Gateway
what_it_does: On legacy model serving endpoints, endpoint managers turn on token-usage tracking in system tables and payload logging to inference tables.
limits: Unity Gateway is now GA and recommended. Legacy payloads over 1 MiB are not logged.

where: System table
what_it_does: Unity Gateway logs per-request usage (tokens, latency, requester, MCP call metadata) for model and MCP services to a system table.
plans: Billed feature; usage table is Public Preview
limits: No disable option described. By default, viewing or querying the table needs both the account admin and metastore admin roles. 365-day free retention.

where: AI Gateway > Govern > Traces > Set up tracing
what_it_does: A metastore admin creates one table that then logs every request and response across Unity Gateway services, including requester identity and full payload.
limits: Databricks does not manage the table lifecycle; it grows until you set Auto-TTL or delete rows. Only the creator can read it by default.

where: Agent code (MLflow)
what_it_does: Developers turn off automatic tracing of agent steps, inputs and outputs for one library or all libraries.
default: off on serverless compute (autolog must be called explicitly); not stated for other compute

where: databricks-agents deploy() for Model Serving
what_it_does: By default, deploying an agent turns on real-time MLflow tracing, production monitoring, Review App feedback collection, and inference-table logging.
limits: Real-time tracing does not work by default for notebooks in Git folders.

where: mlflow.tracing.configure(span_processors=...); Lakeflow pipeline with ai_mask
what_it_does: Developers redact PII from traces before export, or mask traces already stored in Unity Catalog and restrict access to raw tables.
limits: Redaction changes only the trace, not what the agent receives or returns.

control: Delete traces stored in Unity Catalog
where: SQL on underlying Unity Catalog tables; MLflow UI or API for experiment traces
what_it_does: Traces stored in Unity Catalog cannot be deleted one at a time; rows must be deleted with SQL. Experiment traces can be deleted in the MLflow UI or API.
limits: Deletion, not opt-out.

where: Account console > Settings > Account settings; Account Settings API key st_retention
what_it_does: Account admins set one retention period of 30 to 3,650 days for most system tables, including audit logs, Genie Code events and Unity Gateway usage.
limits: When enabled, free retention becomes 395 days; otherwise these tables have 365-day free retention. Added Sep 9, 2026.

where: System table
what_it_does: Records each message a user sends to Genie Code, with user agent and time, for admin adoption tracking.
limits: No opt-out described. Since May 7, 2026 background requests (autocomplete, quick fix) are not logged. 365-day free retention.

where: Model service or MCP service configuration > Rate limits
what_it_does: Admins cap requests or tokens per minute for a whole service, per user, or per group; excess calls get HTTP 429.
limits: By default no rate limits are configured. Limits are approximate during bursts.

control: Set rate limits to 0 to disable an endpoint
where: Serving endpoint settings
what_it_does: Workspace admins can block a Foundation Model API endpoint by setting its rate limits to zero; queries then return a permission error.
limits: Knowledge Base article (Last published Mar 2, 2026) written for Mosaic AI Model Serving; says users can query these models by default.

control: Revoke default EXECUTE on system.ai (model and MCP access)
where: SQL: REVOKE EXECUTE ON SCHEMA system.ai FROM account users; Catalog Explorer > system.ai > Policies > New policy (GRANT policies)
what_it_does: All account users can call system-provided model services by default. Admins can revoke that grant and allow only approved models or MCPs.
limits: Revoking also removes AI Functions access, which must be re-granted directly. If you were in the Foundation Model Unity Catalog Permissions preview, grants on individual models do not carry over to model services.

where: Workspace: Settings > Advanced > Enforce Unity Gateway; Settings API key enforce_ai_gateway_v3_only (listed at both account and workspace scope)
what_it_does: Requires all foundation model traffic to go through Unity Gateway so permissions, AI budgets and policies apply. Databricks-provided pay-per-token endpoints are disabled and new provisioned throughput or external model endpoints cannot be created outside the gateway.
default: on for new workspaces (setting hidden); off in workspaces with legacy AI Gateway endpoints until a workspace admin turns it on
plans: New workspaces: on by default and hidden
limits: Shown only in workspaces that have legacy AI Gateway endpoints. Docs conflict: the Settings API page says legacy endpoints that bypass the gateway reject traffic, while the migration page says existing provisioned throughput and external model endpoints stay queryable.

control: Built-in guardrail policies (block_unsafe_content, block_jailbreak, block_hallucination, detect_sensitive_data)
where: Unity Gateway > service > Policies > New policy
what_it_does: Admins attach Databricks-managed checks that deny unsafe, jailbreak or hallucinated content, or block or redact structured sensitive data such as card and Social Security numbers.
limits: Fail closed. Not supported on Agent Services. The three LLM-judge checks are each billed as a call to the evaluator model; detect_sensitive_data is pattern-based and uses no evaluator model. Redaction works only on model services.

control: AI Guardrails: Safety and PII detection (Block / Mask / None)
where: Serving endpoint > Edit AI Gateway > AI Guardrails (legacy)
what_it_does: On legacy endpoints, admins turn on safety filtering and choose to block or mask PII (names, addresses, card numbers) in requests and responses.
limits: Databricks says automated PII detection may not find all sensitive data. Output guardrails not supported for embeddings or streaming.

where: Register MCP > Tools: Select manually / Advanced; Automatically include tools added to this server in the future
what_it_does: Admins expose only chosen tools of a registered MCP server and can keep newly added tools out until reviewed.
limits: Registered MCPs expose all tools by default. Exclusion patterns are not supported.

control: Connectors and MCP servers for Genie Code and Genie One
where: Genie Code prompt bar + > Connect; Genie Code settings > MCP Servers; Genie One + > data source
what_it_does: Users connect Google Drive, Gmail, Microsoft 365, Slack, GitHub and others with their own OAuth. Admins control which MCP servers are available; connection owners can revoke user permissions.
limits: Connectors can take write actions (send Slack messages, update Jira or GitHub, draft email) within consented OAuth scopes.

where: Genie Code settings; Genie Agent connector configuration
what_it_does: Users choose which MCP tools and servers Genie Code may use; Genie Agent authors enable or disable individual tools per connector.
plans: Genie Agent MCP tools are Beta (preview)

control: Allowed collaboration platforms / Allow public messages in collaboration platforms
