where: Settings API keys collaboration_platform_connectivity, collaboration_platform_message_visibility
what_it_does: Admins choose whether Slack and Microsoft Teams can connect to the workspace and whether Databricks app replies can be posted to channels or stay private.
limits: Connectivity defaults to ALLOW_ALL; message visibility default not stated.

control: Restrict OAuth scopes for apps to selected values
where: Settings API key allowedAppsUserApiScopes
what_it_does: Limits which OAuth scopes Databricks Apps can request to act for users; an empty list disables user authorization for apps.

where: Account console > Settings > App connections
what_it_does: Account admins remove published OAuth apps (dbt Core, Power BI, Tableau Desktop, Tableau Cloud) or custom apps that connect to Databricks.
limits: Published apps are enabled by default. Changes can take 30 minutes.

where: Catalog Explorer > Data Classification > Enable; automatic tagging at metastore or catalog level
what_it_does: A background job uses an LLM to scan and classify tables in enabled catalogs. Owners pick catalogs and schemas; tagging can be set Inactive.
limits: Default schema scope includes future schemas. Disabling tagging keeps existing tags. Designated Service.

where: User settings (notebook editor)
what_it_does: Turns off automatic autocomplete suggestions in notebooks, which are personalized using Unity Catalog metadata and usage; Ctrl + Space still shows them.
limits: Page does not say whether this also covers Genie Code AI-based autocomplete.

control: Inline suggestion, auto quick fix and auto diagnose preferences
where: Settings API user preference keys enableInlineSuggestionAsYouTypeOptOut, enableAutoInlineQuickFix(OptOut), enableAutoTriggerDiagnose(OptOut)
what_it_does: User preferences that control automatic inline suggestions as you type, automatically suggested inline quick fixes, and automatically triggered diagnostics.
limits: Reference lists keys only; it does not name UI labels or confirm these cover Genie Code AI features.

where: Settings > Advanced > Usage Analytics toggle
what_it_does: Workspace admins opt out of Databricks collecting product usage data through third-party analytics tools.
limits: Databricks says these tools do not collect notebooks or customer data. Page last updated May 3, 2024.

where: Privacy Notice > Information We Collect
what_it_does: Databricks automatically collects Usage Data such as pages and features used, search terms, commands run, and file types and sizes, to run, secure and improve services.
limits: No opt-out offered in the notice; the Usage Analytics toggle covers only third-party tools.

where: databricks.com footer > Your Privacy Choices (Privacy Preference Center); banner Reject All / Manage Preferences
what_it_does: Visitors turn off Performance, Functional and Targeting cookies; Databricks treats this as opting out of cookie-based sale, sharing and targeted advertising.
plans: Applies to databricks.com; banner shown depending on location
limits: In this session the preference center showed non-essential groups pre-checked before any choice. Cookie Notice dated Jan 3, 2023.

where: Browser setting; Supplemental Privacy Notice for California Residents
what_it_does: Databricks says it recognizes opt-out preference signals such as GPC as an opt-out of cookie-based sale or sharing, as the CCPA requires.
plans: California residents; general notice says other US states where legally required
limits: Covers cookie and online identifiers only. The cookie tool has a hidden 'Opt-Out Preference Signal Honored' label.

control: Do Not Sell or Share / Targeted Advertising (request)
where: Privacy Request Center (privacypreferences.databricks.com) > Start Opt-out Request
what_it_does: Request to opt out of sale, sharing, or targeted advertising based on non-cookie identifiers such as email address.
plans: US residents in states with these rights
limits: Databricks says it does not sell data for money but treats some ad partner disclosures as sale or sharing.

control: Privacy rights requests (access, deletion, correction, transfer, object to processing)
where: Privacy Request Center; toll-free hotline in the Privacy Notice
what_it_does: Individuals request access, deletion, correction, or transfer of personal data, or object to processing for purposes such as direct marketing; appeals possible in some places.
limits: Deletion is not an opt-out. Requests about data a Customer put into the Platform go to that Customer, not Databricks.

where: Unsubscribe link in emails; databricks.com/legal/unsubscribe
what_it_does: Stops Databricks marketing emails; service-related messages continue.

where: Gemini web: Settings & help > Activity > On > Turn off / Turn off and delete activity (or myactivity.google.com/product/gemini)
what_it_does: Stops saving your future Gemini chats to Gemini Apps Activity in your Google Account.
plans: Personal accounts; on by default if 18 or over. Work/school settings are controlled by the Workspace admin.
limits: Chats are still kept with your account for up to 72 hours. Only Device assistance, Gemini Notebook, Messages, Phone and WhatsApp stay available.

where: Privacy Hub > What does the Keep Activity setting control? / Who has access to my chats
what_it_does: When off, future chats are not used to train Google's AI models or reviewed by people to improve services, unless you send feedback.
limits: Chats still used for safety, including human review; reviewed chats are not deleted when you delete activity and are kept up to 3 years; anonymized-data processing not covered. Live transcripts and screen automation screenshots follow this setting.

where: Settings & help > Activity > Deleting activity older than … months / Choose an auto-delete option
what_it_does: Sets how long saved Gemini activity is kept before automatic deletion: 3, 18 or 36 months, or Don't auto-delete activity.
limits: Default period is 18 months. Work/school retention may be set by the admin.

where: gemini.google.com: next to New chat > Temporary chat (web and mobile apps)
what_it_does: Starts a chat that does not appear in Gemini Apps Activity or recent chats and is not used to personalize later responses.
plans: Signed-in personal accounts only; not work or school accounts
limits: Not available in Gemini in Chrome or Google Messages. No Gems, feedback, personalized responses, or Connected Apps that need Keep Activity.

where: Privacy Hub > How long does Google retain my temporary chats and chats I have when Keep Activity is off
what_it_does: Temporary chats are kept with your account for 72 hours (last 24 hours used as context) and are not used to train AI models or improve AI with human reviewers.
limits: Still used to respond and to protect Google and users, including human review. The same 72-hour retention applies when Keep Activity is off.

control: Improve Google services with your audio and Gemini Live videos & screenshares
where: Settings & help > Activity (checkbox)
what_it_does: Allows Google to use your audio and Gemini Live video and screenshare recordings to improve services, including training AI models. Can be turned off anytime.
limits: Can only be turned on when Keep Activity is on.

control: Hold / Mute / End; Camera; Turn off screen sharing
where: Gemini mobile app > Live
what_it_does: Pauses or mutes the microphone, ends the Live session, and starts or stops camera and screen sharing.
limits: Muting keeps video or screen sharing active. Camera and screen sharing stop automatically when Live is on hold or the screen locks.

where: Settings & help > Personal Intelligence > Memory
what_it_does: Stops Gemini from using your past chats to personalize responses and suggest topics or tools.
plans: 18 or over; personal accounts with Keep Activity on; mobile, web, Gemini in Chrome, smartwatch
limits: Not used in Gems or Live chats. After you delete a chat there may be a short delay before Gemini stops using it.

where: Settings & help > Personal Intelligence > Instructions for Gemini (toggle, Edit, Delete)
what_it_does: Turns off, edits, or deletes the saved instructions that Gemini applies across chats.
plans: All users can add instructions; remembering specific facts needs a Google AI plan, over 18, US only
limits: Telling Gemini to forget a topic may not fully work; delete related chats in Gemini Apps Activity.

where: Opt-in card > Get started > Connect all / Choose apps / Don't connect; Settings & help > Personal Intelligence > Connected Apps
what_it_does: Chooses which Google apps (Contacts, Photos, Wallet, Workspace, Search services, YouTube) Gemini may use to personalize answers and act; each can be disconnected.
plans: 18 or over; personal accounts with Keep Activity on; gradual rollout
limits: Not in EEA, Nigeria, Switzerland or UK. Disconnecting alone does not remove info already in past chats; Gemini still uses public Search and YouTube info.

where: About personalization with Connected Apps > Common questions
what_it_does: If you connect apps and Keep Activity is on, summaries, excerpts and inferences from them can train Google's models and be human reviewed; not connecting avoids this.
limits: Google says it does not train directly on Gmail, Drive, Contacts, Wallet or Photos library media. Disconnecting does not delete saved activity, which can still be used.

control: Personal Intelligence (per chat) / Try without personalization
where: Text box > Tools > Personal Intelligence off; Try without personalization on a response
what_it_does: Stops one chat from being personalized with memory, instructions or connected app data, or regenerates a response without personalization.
limits: The chat is still saved to Gemini Apps Activity and can personalize other chats; use a temporary chat to avoid saving.

where: Sidebar > Customize > Connectors > Add / More options > Disconnect
what_it_does: Connects or disconnects Google and third-party apps, including custom apps added through MCP servers, that Gemini can use and act in.
plans: Signed-in users; apps vary by device, country and account
limits: Some apps work with Gemini automatically. Unavailable on web, iOS and watches when Keep Activity is off. Gemini can always use public Google Search info.

where: Settings & help > Personal Intelligence > Daily brief
what_it_does: Turns off the proactive daily summary Gemini builds from Gmail, Calendar and your Gemini chats.
plans: 18 or over, US, personal accounts eligible for Personal Intelligence with Workspace connected and Memory on
limits: Page says it works automatically for eligible users. Chats started from brief items are saved to Gemini Apps Activity.

where: Sidebar > Scheduled > More > Pause or Resume; edit or delete a schedule
what_it_does: Pauses or deletes recurring actions that Gemini prepares in the background at set times.
plans: Personal accounts and qualifying Workspace accounts; Keep Activity required
limits: Up to 10 active schedules. Notifications are managed in device settings.

control: Use task mode to hand off work
where: Settings > Task settings > Turn off (Mac app: Gemini > Settings > Tasks)
what_it_does: Turns off agent tasks; deletes remote browser and remote code execution data and stops schedules from running.
plans: 18 or over; personal accounts; Google AI Pro or Ultra; Keep Activity on; Personal Intelligence opt-in
limits: Not in EEA, Nigeria, Switzerland or UK. Tasks, threads, schedules and files are kept; local Chrome data is not erased.

control: Delete remote browser data / Delete remote code execution
where: Settings > Task settings
what_it_does: Deletes saved cookies and sign-in data from Gemini's cloud browser, and all files and data saved on the remote computer used for tasks.
limits: You may need to sign in to sites again. Gemini may also delete saved browser data automatically.

where: Task thread; View live > Take over task; Stop
what_it_does: Gemini is designed to ask for your review and confirmation before sending communications, modifying your data, making purchases, submitting web forms or signing in with Sign in with Google; you can stop it or take over its browser.
limits: Google says safeguards do not guarantee protection. If a schedule runs while you are offline, you may not be able to stop an unintended action. Gemini can perform bulk actions on private tasks in Google Tasks without your confirmation.

control: Screen automation (Always allow / Ask every time / Do not allow)
where: Gemini app > Settings > Screen automation > choose app
what_it_does: Sets per app whether Gemini may read and operate that Android app's screen to complete tasks like booking rides or ordering food.
plans: 18 or over; personal accounts; India, Japan, South Korea, UK, US; select Pixel and Samsung devices
limits: Beta. You can view, stop or take control (not on some devices). Gemini asks you to complete final steps like placing orders.

control: Call for me / Cancel / Take over
where: Gemini mobile app: calling task summary
what_it_does: Gemini shows the number and details it will share and calls only after you tap Call for me; you can cancel before it connects or take over.
plans: 18 or over, US, Pixel 11 with US SIM, Google AI subscription
limits: Gemini says it cannot make payments or share card numbers, passwords or health info. Calls are recorded and say they come from Google's AI.

control: Block calls from Gemini users (opt out)
where: g.co/gemini/opt-out (linked from the calling help page)
what_it_does: Lets people opt out of receiving automated calls that Gemini places for other users, and opt back in later.

where: Gemini web app: product listing
what_it_does: A purchase is placed only after you select Buy, review the prefilled order, and select Pay with GPay.
plans: 18 or over; personal accounts; Keep Activity on; listed countries; eligible merchants
limits: Linking retailer accounts lets Google see loyalty info and manage orders; review links at myaccount.google.com/connections.

control: Use Wallet to personalize Google Ads
where: wallet.google.com > Settings > Data & Privacy > Use Wallet to personalize Google Ads (sends you to My Ad Center); separate settings on the same page: Google Wallet personalization, Use Wallet to personalize experiences across Google, Google Wallet history
what_it_does: Controls whether Wallet and payments info and activity are used to show you more personalized ads. Personalization across Google is a separate Wallet setting (Use Wallet to personalize experiences across Google).
plans: Google Wallet users; rolling out gradually
limits: Wallet page does not mention Gemini. The Gemini Privacy Hub says Gemini shopping cart and order data is saved to Google Wallet, and Google Pay purchases from Gemini are saved to Google Pay My Activity; both may be used for ads depending on settings.

control: Do you use my Gemini Apps chats to show me ads? (statement)
where: Privacy Hub > Privacy questions
what_it_does: Google states Gemini chats are not used to show you ads and says it will clearly tell users if this changes.
plans: Gemini Apps users covered by the notice
limits: No ads toggle inside Gemini. The Hub also says Google does not sell personal info and that Wallet/Google Pay shopping data may be used for ads.

where: myadcenter.google.com > Personalized ads > On / Off
what_it_does: Turns off ad personalization for the signed-in account on Google services and Google ads on partner sites; ads become contextual.
plans: Signed-in Google Accounts; separate device settings when signed out
limits: Page does not mention Gemini. Personalized ads may already be off for accounts shown as under 18.

control: U.S. state law requirements (no sale, no CCPA "share")
where: Google Privacy Policy > U.S. state law requirements
what_it_does: Google says it does not sell personal info or "share" it as CCPA defines; it notes state opt-out rights for targeted ads and profiling. Ad controls: My Ad Center.
plans: US residents of states with privacy laws
limits: No mention of Global Privacy Control or opt-out preference signals found. Rights are exercised through Google's account tools (privacy controls, Takeout, My Ad Center), with requests checked by sign-in, or by contacting Google, including through an authorized agent; appeal by replying to Google's email.

control: Requests to opt out of sale / limit sensitive data
where: California Privacy Rights Report
what_it_does: Google says it answers opt-out-of-sale and limit-sensitive-data requests by explaining it does not sell data and uses sensitive data only as CCPA permits.
limits: No separate opt-out mechanism is offered and GPC is not mentioned.

where: Google Ads Help > Helping advertisers comply with the U.S. states' privacy laws
what_it_does: Google says that where state law applies, a GPC signal turns off ads targeting and triggers restricted data processing for those Google ad requests.
plans: Users in applicable US states; Google ad requests
limits: Advertiser-facing Google Ads page; it does not mention Gemini. No GPC statement found in the Privacy Policy or the Gemini Privacy Hub.

where: Device, browser and Google app location permissions (Privacy Hub location section)
what_it_does: Gemini uses precise device location only with your permission; otherwise it uses a general area from your IP address or Home/Work addresses.
limits: Location is always collected; precise location may come from Maps or other Google services even with the Google app setting off. Stored location is coarsened (3+ sq km, 1000+ users).

where: Android: touch and hold Google app > App Info > Permissions
what_it_does: Controls which device features, such as camera, microphone, contacts and location, Gemini (hosted by the Google app) can use.

control: Hey Google / Use Gemini without unlocking / Switch to Google Assistant / Default digital assistant app
where: Gemini app > Settings > Talk to Gemini hands-free; Gemini on lock screen; Menu > Switch to Google Assistant; Android Settings > Default apps
what_it_does: Stops Gemini opening by voice, on the lock screen or from the power button, switches back to Google Assistant, removes it as default assistant, or deletes the app.
limits: Deleting the app does not remove Gemini as default assistant. Switching to Assistant does not delete Gemini Apps Activity.

where: Family Link > select child > Controls > Gemini > Gemini Apps
what_it_does: Parents turn a supervised child's access to Gemini Apps on or off.
limits: Keep Activity is not available to these users. Not available for supervised accounts in EEA, Switzerland or UK.

control: Delete (All time / Last hour / Last day / Custom range)
where: Settings & help > Activity > Delete; also per day or per item
what_it_does: Deletes saved Gemini activity, including related Live audio, transcripts, video and screenshares. This is deletion, not an opt-out.
limits: Deleting a Gem chat keeps the Gem; deleting a shared chat keeps its public link.

control: Report legal issue (objection and correction request)
where: Help Center legal request form; in app: More > Report legal issue below a response
what_it_does: Where laws like the GDPR apply, lets users object to processing of their personal data or ask to correct inaccurate personal data in responses.
plans: Where privacy laws such as the GDPR grant these rights

control: Turn on smart features in Gmail, Chat, and Meet
where: Gmail > Settings > See all settings > General > Smart features (checkbox)
what_it_does: Stops Gmail, Chat and Meet from using your content and activity for in-app features like Smart Compose, Smart Reply, summary cards and inbox categories.
plans: Personal and work accounts; applies across signed-in devices
limits: Off by default in EEA, Japan, Switzerland, UK. Some features with their own toggles, like Chat summaries and Smart Reply in Chat, stay available.

where: Gmail > Settings > General > Google Workspace smart features > Manage Workspace smart feature settings (also Calendar, Chat, Drive, Meet)
what_it_does: Turning off stops Workspace data being used for cross-app features, including Gemini summaries and drafts and Gmail events in Calendar.
limits: Off by default in EEA, Japan, Switzerland, UK. When on, your data may be used to improve these features.

control: Smart features in other Google products
where: Same Workspace smart feature settings panel
what_it_does: Turning off stops Workspace data from personalizing other Google products, including Personal Intelligence in the Gemini app and Search, Maps reservations and Wallet passes.
plans: Listed examples are for personal accounts
limits: Off by default in EEA, Japan, Switzerland, UK. Workspace data you share through Gemini screen actions or screenshots can still be used.

control: AI Overview conversation summaries (via smart features)
where: Gmail settings: smart features
what_it_does: Gmail can add AI summaries at the top of email threads; Google says turning off smart features is how to stop them.
plans: All Gmail users globally, supported languages
limits: Turning off smart features also disables AI writing and proofreading across Gmail and other Workspace apps.

where: Gmail > Settings > See all settings > Inbox
what_it_does: Shows or hides AI Inbox, which lists AI-suggested to-dos and topics from your email.
plans: US, English; personal accounts with Google AI Plus, Pro or Ultra
limits: Beta. Needs both Workspace smart feature settings on.

control: Delete after (3 months / 18 months / 36 months / Manual deletion only)
where: Workspace app > Ask Gemini > More options > Settings > History; or delete single conversations
what_it_does: Sets auto-deletion of Gemini side panel conversation history in Docs, Drive, Gmail, Sheets and Slides; conversations can also be deleted one by one.
plans: Personal accounts with Google AI Pro, Ultra or Workspace Experiments
limits: Only inactive conversations auto-delete. Deletion is permanent.

control: Your instructions for Gemini in Workspace
where: Ask Gemini > Menu > Settings > Personalization (Chat: /settings > Have Gemini in Workspace use your instructions)
what_it_does: Turns off use of your saved instructions to tailor Gemini responses across Workspace apps; instructions can also be deleted.
plans: Personal accounts with Google AI Plus, Pro, Ultra or Workspace Experiments
limits: Separate from Gemini app instructions. Turned-off instructions stay saved until deleted.

where: Gmail Help: how Gemini in Gmail, Docs and other apps protects your data
what_it_does: For Google AI plan users, Gemini in Workspace apps uses your content to respond but not to train models, and does not store prompts or outputs without permission.
plans: Personal accounts with Google AI plans
limits: Workspace content is not used for ads. Data shared with the Gemini app (Personal Intelligence, screen actions) follows Gemini terms and may train models.

where: Chrome toolbar > Ask Gemini > on-screen opt-in
what_it_does: Gemini in Chrome works only after a one-time opt-in; it is not available in Incognito mode or signed-out profiles.
plans: 13 or older (or local age), supported regions, signed-in Chrome on Mac, Windows, Chromebook Plus
limits: Once opted in, it uses current tab content by default.

control: Show Gemini at the top of the browser / Show Gemini in Mac menu bar (or system tray on Windows) and turn on keyboard shortcut / Unpin Gemini
where: Chrome Settings > AI innovations > Gemini in Chrome > Preferences; or right-click the toolbar
what_it_does: Separate Preferences toggles: one hides Gemini's toolbar button (right-click > Unpin Gemini does the same); the others remove Gemini from the Mac menu bar or Windows system tray and turn off its keyboard shortcut.

control: Share current tab by default / Remove tab
where: Chrome Settings > AI innovations > Gemini in Chrome > Permissions; chat: Show shared tabs > Remove tab
what_it_does: Stops new Gemini chats from automatically using the current tab's page content, or stops sharing a specific tab.
limits: You can share up to 10 tabs. For shared Workspace pages, Gemini may access the full document from your Workspace account.

where: chrome://settings/ai/gemini
what_it_does: Stops Gemini in Chrome from answering questions about audio and video you already played on media sites.

where: Chrome Settings > AI innovations > Gemini in Chrome > Permissions
what_it_does: Blocks Gemini in Chrome from using your precise location (it then estimates from your IP address) or your microphone.
limits: Users under 18 cannot turn on the microphone and cannot use Live.

where: Chrome Settings > AI innovations > Gemini in Chrome > Permissions
what_it_does: Turns off auto browse, Gemini's ability to navigate and act on websites in Chrome for you on that device.
plans: 18 or over, US, English, personal account with Google AI Pro or Ultra
limits: Chrome asks permission the first time; after that, Gemini asks for confirmation before each task that browses the web.

control: Start Task / Take over task / Stop
where: Gemini in Chrome side panel and task tab
what_it_does: Gemini shows its plan before you click Start Task and aims to ask for confirmation before certain actions, such as starting a task, sending messages, changing data, submitting forms, scheduling events, or visiting sites with highly sensitive financial or health data. Take over task and Stop let you take control or end a task at any time.
limits: Gemini picks sites and may share your info with them. Google warns it can make unintended purchases and that you are responsible for its actions.

control: Sites Gemini can sign you in to
where: Chrome Settings > AI innovations > Gemini in Chrome > Permissions
what_it_does: Removes Gemini in Chrome's permission to sign you in to sites using Google Password Manager or Sign in with Google.
limits: Removing a site does not unlink your Google Account or delete saved passwords.

where: Chrome Settings > AI Innovations
what_it_does: Turning off deletes Chrome's on-device generative AI models, stops re-downloads, and disables features that rely on them.
plans: Eligible devices; set per user and per device
limits: Chrome may download models in the background. AI features that do not use these models may keep running. Enterprise policy can govern this.

where: Chrome Settings > AI Innovations > History search, powered by AI
what_it_does: Turns off AI search of your browsing history, which stores page contents of visited sites locally on your device.
limits: Organizations may disable it on managed profiles.

where: Family Link (linked from Gemini in Chrome help)
what_it_does: Parents who keep supervision for children 13 or older can turn off the child's access to Gemini in Chrome.

where: Admin console > Devices > Chrome > Settings > Generative AI > Gemini integrations
what_it_does: Admins can make Gemini in Chrome unavailable (GeminiSettings set to 1, or GenAiDefaultSettings set to 2); Gemini app access must also be enabled for it to work.
limits: Changes can take up to 24 hours to apply.

where: Chrome Enterprise policies (Admin console)
what_it_does: Admins can turn auto browse on or off and allow or block it for specific URLs on managed browsers.
plans: Managed users with listed Workspace editions
limits: Admin page says off by default for managed users; Chrome's policy list entry says unset allows actions. GeminiSparkSettings separately controls Spark using auto browse.

where: Gemini API Additional Terms > Unpaid Services / Paid Services > How Google Uses Your Data
what_it_does: With a billing-enabled Cloud project, Google does not use prompts, files, cached content or responses to improve products; free AI Studio and unpaid API content is used.
plans: Gemini API and AI Studio; unpaid vs paid
limits: Unpaid data may be read by human reviewers. Paid usage details stay under Google's Privacy Policy. In EEA, Switzerland, UK paid-tier data terms apply to all services.

where: AI Studio > Logs and Datasets > Settings; per-request store
what_it_does: Turns storing of API request and response logs on or off per project; generateContent does not store unless enabled, while the Interactions API stores by default.
default: off for generateContent; on for the Interactions API (store=true)
limits: Turning Interactions API logging off stops automatic storing and retrieval of conversation history unless overridden per request.

where: AI Studio > Logs > retention settings
what_it_does: Sets when a project's logs are marked for deletion: after 7, 14, 28 or 55 days.
limits: Default is 55 days. Logs saved to datasets do not expire.

where: API request parameter; AI Studio retention and deletion
what_it_does: Opts an interaction out of Google's server-side storage, which otherwise keeps interactions 55 days on the paid tier or 1 day on the free tier.
limits: store=false prevents background execution and previous_interaction_id. Paid projects can shorten retention to 7, 14, 28 or 55 days; stored items can be deleted by ID.

where: AI Studio > Logs and Datasets
what_it_does: Sharing a dataset of your logs lets Google use it under Unpaid Services terms, including model training and human review.
limits: Page says contribution happens through datasets with an option to opt out during dataset creation; the default state is unclear. Options vary by location.

where: AI Studio (invite-only private preview)
what_it_does: Opt-in tier with up to 50% off token costs on select models in exchange for Google using that project's data under Unpaid Services terms.
limits: Data may be used to improve Google products and machine learning; Google advises not sending sensitive or personal info.

where: Gemini API docs > Abuse monitoring
what_it_does: Google keeps prompts, context and outputs for 55 days to detect policy violations; flagged content may be reviewed by authorized Google employees.
limits: No opt-out is described. Data is used only for policy enforcement, not to train models other than enforcement ones.

control: Zero data retention steps (Gemini Developer API)
where: Gemini API docs > Zero data retention
what_it_does: No ZDR switch; developers reduce retention by avoiding Search/Maps grounding, setting store=false, not enabling Live session resumption, deleting files and skipping explicit caching.
limits: Abuse-monitoring logging remains; Google points to Vertex AI for guaranteed ZDR. Grounding storage (30 days) cannot be disabled; implicit in-memory cache has a 24-hour TTL.

where: Gemini API Additional Terms > Grounding with Google Search
what_it_does: When used, Google stores prompts, context and output for 30 days to create grounded results and for debugging and testing.
limits: Only avoidable by not using the feature. Under paid quota, debugging use follows the Data Processing Addendum. Grounding with Google Maps also stores data 30 days.

where: Gemini API docs > Context caching
what_it_does: Implicit caching is enabled by default for Gemini 2.5 and newer models; the page describes no way to turn it off.
limits: Explicit caching is optional and not supported by the Interactions API or newer models.

where: Gemini API docs > Computer Use > Safety and security
what_it_does: The model flags risky actions as needing confirmation; the app must get user approval and return a safety acknowledgement. Developers can exclude actions or adjust policy categories.
limits: Overrides only express a preference; the model may still require confirmation. Categories cover payments, messaging, account creation, consent banners and legal terms.

control: delete (Interactions API) / AI Studio log deletion
where: API delete method; AI Studio Logs page
what_it_does: Deletes stored interactions by ID, or removes logs from project storage in AI Studio. This is deletion, not an opt-out.
plans: API delete method: free and paid tiers; AI Studio log deletion: paid tier projects only

where: Gemini API Additional Terms > Unpaid Services
what_it_does: Tuning data is used only for tuning; deleting a tuned model also deletes its tuning content.
limits: Tuning content may be kept with the tuned model for re-tuning until you delete it.

control: EEA, Switzerland and UK data terms
where: Gemini API Additional Terms
what_it_does: For users in these regions, the paid-tier data terms (no use to improve products) apply to all services, including free AI Studio and unpaid quota.
limits: Apps made available to users in these regions must use Paid Services.

where: Service Specific Terms, summarized in the Agent Platform ZDR doc
what_it_does: Google will not use customer data to train or fine-tune any AI/ML models without prior permission or instruction, for all managed models including pre-GA ones.
plans: Vertex AI / Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform

where: Agent Platform ZDR doc > Prompt logging for abuse monitoring
what_it_does: Customers under the Google Cloud Platform Terms who want zero data retention can request an exception to prompt logging for abuse monitoring.
plans: Customers on Google Cloud online terms
limits: Zero data retention may not be possible with some Advanced AI features; Google says to contact your account team.

control: Prompt logging and human review (abuse monitoring)
where: Agent Platform docs > Abuse monitoring
what_it_does: If safety classifiers flag activity, Google may log prompts for up to 90 days for policy review by authorized staff; not used for training.
plans: Google Cloud online terms; Cloud Master Agreement customers exempt by default
limits: Frontier and Advanced AI models log prompts and responses for up to 30 days; some Anthropic models require enabling data sharing with Anthropic for abuse monitoring.

where: Per-model, per-project configuration (BigQuery)
what_it_does: If enabled, writes certain requests and responses to a BigQuery table you designate; leave it off for zero data retention.
plans: Vertex AI / Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform

where: API request
what_it_does: Stops Google storing prompts, responses and conversation state for the Interactions API; store defaults to true for all models.
plans: Vertex AI / Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform

where: cacheConfig API (needs roles/aiplatform.admin)
what_it_does: Turns off all implicit caching, or only durable at-rest caching while keeping in-memory caching, for a project across all regions.
plans: Vertex AI / Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform
limits: Cached data is project-scoped, deleted within 24 hours, and not used for training. Turning off durable caching org-wide requires the account team.

where: Per-request API field
what_it_does: Off unless enabled per request; when on, stores text, audio and video prompts and outputs for up to 24 hours so a session can reconnect.
plans: Vertex AI / Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform

control: Grounding with Google Search / Web Grounding for Enterprise
where: Agent Platform ZDR doc
what_it_does: Search grounding stores derived queries and context, not tied to the customer, for up to 3 days with no way to disable; Google recommends Web Grounding for Enterprise for ZDR.
plans: Vertex AI / Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform
limits: Grounding with Google Maps stores prompts, context and output for 30 days, also with no way to disable.

control: Agent session data (CodeMender, Deep Research, Sandbox Snapshots)
where: Agent Platform ZDR doc > Agent products
what_it_does: CodeMender and Deep Research keep session data for up to 7 days and sessions can be deleted earlier; Sandbox snapshots last for the sandbox TTL.
plans: Vertex AI / Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform
limits: Deep Research storage cannot be disabled. For zero data retention, do not use the Sandbox API.

control: Consent to the Advanced AI Safety Addendum
where: Model Garden consent; IAM permission aiplatform.consents.update
what_it_does: Each project must consent once, in Model Garden, before Advanced AI models can be enabled; those models log all prompts and responses for up to 30 days for abuse monitoring. Admins can block consent by limiting the aiplatform.consents.update permission in IAM or by disabling access to those models.
plans: Vertex AI / Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform
limits: Opting out of prompt-response logging may not be possible for some Advanced AI features.

control: CM_TELEMETRY_OPT_OUT environment variable set to 1 or true (CodeMender CLI)
where: Environment variable CM_TELEMETRY_OPT_OUT set to 1 or true
what_it_does: Turns off CodeMender CLI telemetry (anonymized usage metrics and performance diagnostics, no source code or user identities).
limits: Covers only the CodeMender CLI.

control: gcloud config set disable_usage_reporting true (Google Cloud CLI usage statistics)
where: gcloud config set disable_usage_reporting true
what_it_does: Turns off Google Cloud CLI usage statistics.
default: off unless you opt in at install
limits: General Google Cloud CLI setting, not specific to Vertex AI. No opt-out was found for the usage data the Gemini API or Vertex AI collect on the server side (token counts, errors, device IDs, IP addresses).

control: Statement, no toggle: Google does not sell Service Data and does not 'share' it as defined in the CCPA
where: Google Cloud Privacy Notice
what_it_does: Google says it does not sell Service Data and does not 'share' it as the CCPA defines.
limits: Covers Google Cloud Platform (Vertex AI and the Agent Platform) and only Service Data; Customer Data such as prompts falls under the Cloud Data Processing Addendum. For the Gemini API, paid-tier usage details stay under the Google Privacy Policy and the Controller-Controller Data Protection Terms.

where: WhatsApp: chat > View contact > Restricted chat; group > Restricted chat
what_it_does: Per-chat setting that blocks Meta AI features, chat export, auto-saving media, and linked devices (to stop unofficial clients or AI agents) for everyone in the chat.
who: user (either person in 1:1 chats; group admins in groups)
limits: Set per chat on the primary device. Older app versions may still use linked clients. Chats with Advanced chat privacy do not upgrade automatically.

control: "Remove from group" (Meta AI as a group member)
where: WhatsApp: group name > member list > Meta AI > Remove from group
what_it_does: Removes Meta AI from a group so it stops reading and replying to new group messages.
limits: While Meta AI is a member, Meta can read new group messages and may use prompts, shared messages and feedback to improve AI.

where: WhatsApp Settings > Chats > Private Processing
what_it_does: Turns message summaries and writing help on or off; when off, those options no longer appear in chats.
plans: WhatsApp; English, Indonesian, Portuguese and Spanish only
limits: Limited countries and languages. Covers summaries and writing help only, not other Meta AI chats.

where: WhatsApp Settings > Chats > Private Processing
what_it_does: Turns Meta AI web search off or on. When off, Meta AI no longer searches the web and its answers are based on when the model was last trained. Web search is on by default in Incognito chats, side chats, and groups where Meta AI with Private Processing is a member; this page says you can switch it for Incognito chats.
limits: When off, answers rely on training data only. No similar toggle documented for regular Meta AI chats.

control: Incognito chat with Meta AI; history: "When I exit" / "1 hour after I exit" / "Never"
where: WhatsApp: Meta AI chat > Incognito icon; Incognito chat > Settings
what_it_does: One-off Meta AI chat using Private Processing that Meta and WhatsApp cannot access. History disappears on exit by default, or after 1 hour, or stays on device.
limits: The /reset-ai command does not work here. Using Meta AI on WhatsApp is always optional.

where: WhatsApp: individual or group chat > side chat with Meta AI
what_it_does: Private Meta AI help using a chat's context; only you see it, prompts go encrypted to a secure enclave, and no messages are stored after the session.
limits: Web search is on by default in side chats.

where: Typed in an individual chat with an AI on Messenger, Instagram or WhatsApp
what_it_does: Deletes the AI's copy of your messages and saved details for one chat, or for all AI chats on that app including groups. Your own copy stays.
limits: Deletion, not opt-out. Deleting a WhatsApp AI chat in the app removes it only from WhatsApp, not from Meta.

where: Messenger: chat > Information > Privacy & support > Message permissions
what_it_does: When off, no one in the chat can use AI features that share its messages with Meta AI (such as summaries); auto-save photos also turns off.
plans: Messenger; not in some chats such as Marketplace
who: user (either person in 1:1 chats; admins in groups)
limits: People can still forward messages to Meta AI or report them to Meta.

where: Messenger: Menu > Settings > Underlined words
what_it_does: Turns off underlined topics in chats (such as restaurants or movies) that you can tap to look up with Meta AI.
limits: Underlining is processed on the device. Phone numbers or emails underlined by device settings are not affected.

where: Facebook group (admin) > group AI settings
what_it_does: Lets group admins turn off, or turn back on, the group's AI that people chat with one-to-one for answers drawn from group content.
plans: Eligible Facebook groups; not all regions
limits: Enabled by default for eligible groups. In public groups anyone on Facebook can chat with it.

where: Meta AI app: Menu > Settings > Data & privacy > Manage your information
what_it_does: Deletes all your Meta AI chats, prompts and generated media from History and Media.
limits: Deletion, not opt-out. Public vibes, and others' vibes that include you, are not deleted this way.

where: Meta AI app: Settings > Data & privacy > Manage your information; or vibe > Menu > Remove from feed
what_it_does: Takes your posted AI videos off the public Meta AI and Vibes feeds and off your public profile.
plans: Meta AI and Vibes apps and websites
limits: Removed vibes stay in your Media section and can be reposted.

control: "Suggesting your vibes on other apps" (Facebook, Instagram)
where: Meta AI app: Menu > Settings > Data & privacy
what_it_does: Stops Meta from suggesting your posted vibes to people on Facebook or Instagram.
plans: Meta AI and Vibes apps and websites
limits: The choice applies across all Meta AI and Vibes apps and websites.

where: Meta AI app: Menu > chat > Menu > Delete link (videos: Media > Creations)
what_it_does: Removes a shared link to a Meta AI conversation or video so people with the link can no longer see it.
limits: Links do not expire on their own and can be reshared until deleted.

control: "Create AI images of yourself with Meta AI"
where: Meta AI app: profile > Meta AI settings > create image of me
what_it_does: Turns off AI images of you and deletes your setup photos.
plans: Meta AI app, gradual US rollout
limits: Feature in development. Turning it back on requires new setup photos.

where: Connect: Meta AI app > Settings > Apps. Disconnect: Settings > Accounts Center > Your information and permissions > App Connections
what_it_does: Connects or disconnects third-party apps (calendar, email) that Meta AI can read and act on. After disconnecting, Meta AI loses access.
limits: Personalized information may be sent to connected apps. A connection made on one account is usable by other accounts in the same Accounts Center.

control: Remove profiles from Meta Account (formerly Accounts Center)
where: Settings > Meta Account or Accounts Center > profiles
what_it_does: Stops Meta combining your info across removed profiles for ads, content and suggestions, within 7 days of removal.
plans: All Meta apps; WhatsApp only if added
limits: Previously combined info stays combined. Safety, measurement and same-app uses continue.
page_date: Updated Oct 15, 2026 (shown as 'about a minute ago' at re-check)

control: Ask Meta AI to change what it remembers (e.g., "Remember that I no longer enjoy canoeing.")
where: Any Meta AI chat (Facebook, Messenger)
what_it_does: Corrects details Meta AI remembers from your chats and activity across accounts in the same Accounts Center.
limits: Correction only. No memory on/off switch is documented on this page.

where: Facebook: Settings & privacy > Settings > Meta Account > Your information and permissions > Activity from other businesses
what_it_does: Controls whether Meta uses activity that other businesses share about you (purchases, site visits) to show more relevant ads and content.
plans: Profiles in the same Meta Account; EU/UK choices differ
limits: Businesses still send the data. Content can still use your Meta activity and apps you connect, including for AI at Meta features.

control: "Ads Preferences" and feed controls (no AI-chat-specific setting)
where: Ad preferences; feed controls
what_it_does: The only tools Meta names for adjusting ads and content after it began using voice and text AI chats as a personalization signal on December 16, 2025.
limits: No opt-out of the AI-chat signal described. Sensitive topics (e.g., religion, health) not used for ads. WhatsApp counts only if in the same Accounts Center.

control: Global Privacy Control signal; "Right to Opt Out of Targeted Advertising"
where: US Regional Privacy Notice: GPC-enabled browser on Meta websites; webform; Ad Preferences ("Activity from other businesses", "Ads about Meta")
what_it_does: Where state law gives the right, Meta treats a GPC signal, received when you visit and log in to its websites, as an opt-out of targeted advertising.
plans: US residents in states that grant the right
limits: Logged out, GPC applies only to that browser. Meta says it does not sell or 'share' (CCPA). Other Do Not Track signals are ignored.

control: Objection form (right to object to AI training)
where: Form linked from in-app and email notices sent to people based in the EU
what_it_does: Lets people based in the EU who use Meta's platforms object, at any time, to their data (public content shared by adults and their interactions with AI at Meta) being used to train Meta's AI models.
limits: Private messages with friends and family are not used unless someone in the chat shares them with Meta's AI features; per the March 27, 2026 update, Meta may train on messages shared that way. Public data from EU accounts under 18 is not used. Meta honors objections already received. A US-facing help link to the form (meta.com/help/contact/6359191084165019) shows 'This page isn't available'.

control: "Data Subject Rights for Third Party Information Used for AI at Meta" (form)
where: Contact form linked from the Privacy Center generative AI page
what_it_does: Lets people in the countries listed on the form report a concern that their personal information from third-party sources (internet or licensed data) appeared in a response from an AI at Meta model, feature or experience.
plans: Countries in the form's menu (149 as served to a US connection, including the US); no EU or EEA country, the UK, Switzerland, Brazil, South Africa or Thailand is listed
limits: Not automatically fulfilled. Meta says it cannot access, correct or delete third-party training data because it is not linked to accounts.

where: Phone or tablet settings
what_it_does: Stops Meta Products covered by the Meta Privacy Policy from receiving GPS and other device location signals, which Meta uses for features including Meta AI responses.
plans: Meta Products covered by the Meta Privacy Policy (Facebook, Instagram, Messenger, AI at Meta; Meta Quest when logged in with a Meta account)
limits: Meta still estimates location from IP address, your activity (check-ins, events) and info you provide.

where: Meta AI app: glasses Settings > Meta AI (Experiences)
what_it_does: When off, images and video from live AI and other multimodal glasses features are not stored, not human-reviewed, and not used for training or product improvement.
limits: Not retroactive. Excludes voice, media shared on Messenger or Instagram, and metadata such as AI image descriptions. Visual reminders may stop working.

control: Voice recordings: view and delete ("Voice activity log")
where: Meta AI app; path in help article meta.com/help/ai-glasses/1129552064459382 (Glasses privacy > Voice activity log)
what_it_does: Lets you view and delete stored glasses voice recordings and transcripts; deleted items are no longer used to improve Meta products.
plans: Ray-Ban Meta and Oakley Meta AI glasses
limits: Stored by default up to one year; false wakes deleted within 90 days; trained reviewers may review them. Notice offers a storage off switch only for Ray-Ban Stories.

where: Meta AI app glasses settings (exact path not given)
what_it_does: Turning off the "Hey Meta" wake word also turns off "Meta AI with camera", which may capture an image when you ask about what you see.
limits: Same FAQ says the option to turn off voice recording storage is no longer available; recordings can be deleted in Settings.

where: Meta AI app: Glasses > Device settings > your glasses > Glasses privacy
what_it_does: Lets you decline sharing device usage data (how and how often you use glasses and wrist devices) for product improvement and personalization.
limits: Essential data is always used. One choice covers all paired devices. Companion app data falls under the Meta Privacy Policy.

where: Meta AI app: Glasses > Device settings > your glasses > Glasses privacy > Cloud media
what_it_does: Turns off sending glasses photos and videos to Meta's cloud for features like voice sharing ("Hey Meta, send a photo").
limits: When on, media stays in the cloud for 30 days, then is deleted. First activation asks for confirmation.

where: Meta AI app: Menu > Settings > Notifications
what_it_does: Pauses all Meta AI app push notifications or turns off individual types.
limits: Applies only to the app or website where you change it.

where: Facebook and Instagram settings (delete your information or account)
what_it_does: Permanently deletes your account and posted information unless Meta must keep it.
limits: Deletion, not opt-out. May take up to 90 days, plus up to 90 more days to clear backups.

control: Permission prompt before Meta AI works with business assets; revoke by asking Meta AI in chat
where: Meta AI chat
what_it_does: Meta AI asks for permission before working with your Instagram, Facebook or ad profile business assets; you can ask it in chat to revoke permission to read that data.
limits: Narrow: business assets only. No general approval or autonomy setting for Meta AI actions was found. Muse, Meta's separate agent, has its own approval settings, outside this product's scope.

vendor_entity: xAI (SpaceXAI LLC, branded 'SpaceXSI'); Grok in X via X Corp.
where: Grok app: Settings > Data Controls; grok.com: Settings > Data
what_it_does: Stops your new logged-in Grok conversations from being used to train xAI models.
plans: Grok apps and grok.com, logged in
limits: New chats only. Feedback you give may still be used for training. Logged-out use has no opt-out in some regions (not EU/UK).

vendor_entity: xAI (SpaceXAI LLC, branded 'SpaceXSI'); Grok in X via X Corp.
where: grok.com and Grok apps: ghost icon, top right
what_it_does: Chat is not shown in your history, is deleted from xAI systems within 30 days, and is not used for model training.
plans: Grok apps and grok.com, where available
limits: May be kept longer for safety, security or legal reasons.

vendor_entity: xAI (SpaceXAI LLC, branded 'SpaceXSI'); Grok in X via X Corp.
where: Grok app: Settings > Data Controls; grok.com: Settings > Data
what_it_does: Turns off use of your X data and interactions to personalize Grok on grok.com and the apps.
limits: Grok inside X uses a separate X setting (XAI-16).

vendor_entity: xAI (SpaceXAI LLC, branded 'SpaceXSI'); Grok in X via X Corp.
control: Memory summary: view, edit, delete memories
where: grok.com: Settings > memory summary
what_it_does: Lets you view, edit and delete saved memories; you can select text in the memory summary to correct or remove what Grok remembers.
limits: Release notes only (Dec 22, 2025; Jun 13, 2026; Aug 15, 2026). No memory on/off switch found in official docs.

vendor_entity: xAI (SpaceXAI LLC, branded 'SpaceXSI'); Grok in X via X Corp.
control: Background-tasks tray (stop task, delete scheduled loop); Automations
where: grok.com: background-tasks tray; Automations
what_it_does: Stops running background tasks and deletes scheduled loops. Automations run your instructions on a schedule or on matching emails, using connected apps.
limits: Release notes only (Jul 16, Aug 15, Aug 22, 2026). No help article on managing automations found.

vendor_entity: xAI (SpaceXAI LLC, branded 'SpaceXSI'); Grok in X via X Corp.
where: Grok app: history (press and hold) and Settings > Data Controls; grok.com: history trash icon and Settings
what_it_does: Deletes selected chats, all chat history, or the account.
limits: Deletion, not opt-out. Takes up to 30 days; de-identified copies or data needed for safety or legal reasons may be kept.

vendor_entity: xAI (SpaceXAI LLC, branded 'SpaceXSI'); Grok in X via X Corp.
where: grok.com/share-links

control: Personalization or notifications opt-out (label not given)

limits: The Transparency Note gives no setting name or path.

control: Location (in-product setting, label not given; OS location permissions)

limits: No Copilot-specific location setting name or default found in Copilot support pages.

where: Thumbs up or thumbs down feedback pane

limits: Feedback is used to improve Copilot, not to train foundation models.

control: Microsoft Family Safety and device parental controls
where: Microsoft Family Safety; Google or Apple device settings
what_it_does: Parents can block the Copilot app or browser access, set usage hours, and choose features such as image generation, voice mode, group chat or AI companions.
plans: Teens; minimum age 13, higher in some regions
limits: For young people Copilot does not personalize from conversation history or show personalized ads.

control: Delete my health data (Copilot Health); Connectors disconnect
where: Copilot settings > Health; settings > Connectors
what_it_does: Deletes all Copilot Health conversations, Health Profile and connected sources and withdraws consent. Wearables and health records can be disconnected anytime.
plans: Preview for Microsoft 365 Personal, Family, Premium subscribers aged 18+ in the US; temporarily unavailable for some users
limits: Health conversations are kept 18 months by default unless deleted. Microsoft says health data is not used for training or advertising.

where: Windows 11: Settings > Apps > Installed apps > Copilot > More options > Uninstall; Windows 10: Settings > Apps
what_it_does: Removes the Copilot app from Windows.
limits: Covers Windows only. Copilot in Edge and in Microsoft 365 apps has separate controls.

where: Microsoft account website
what_it_does: Close your Microsoft account; the same site lets you view, edit or remove profile and payment information.
limits: The Privacy Statement does not say how closure affects stored Copilot data.

control: Privacy support and requests page (data protection rights)
where: Privacy Statement > How to access and control your personal data
what_it_does: Request access, deletion, correction or portability; withdraw consent; object to or restrict use, such as direct marketing or legitimate-interest processing.
limits: Microsoft says some data cannot be controlled through its tools and rights may be limited by law.

where: Edge > Settings > Privacy, search, and services > Privacy > Global Privacy Control
what_it_does: Makes Edge send the GPC signal to every site you visit, asking that your data not be sold or shared for targeted advertising.
plans: Microsoft Edge; setting available in the US
limits: Sites may or may not honor the signal. It is a browser setting, not a Copilot app setting.

control: Training on conversation activity / Training on voice conversations
where: Older app: copilot.com profile > Privacy; Windows or macOS: Settings > Privacy; mobile: Account > Privacy
what_it_does: Opts your future text and voice conversations out of training Microsoft's generative AI models.
plans: Personal Microsoft account; older Copilot app version only; not used for users under 18, signed-out users, Microsoft 365 consumer app users, or users in Brazil, China (not Hong Kong), Israel, Nigeria, South Korea, Vietnam
limits: Applies to future conversations only. Does not stop use for product improvement, ads, safety or compliance. Labels 'Model training on text/voice' not found on current pages. The page does not state a default; its opt-out wording implies training is on until you opt out.

where: Older app: profile > Memory > Personalization and memory (also Edge sidebar)

plans: Personal Microsoft account; older Copilot app version only; not available in Brazil, China (not Hong Kong), Israel, Nigeria, South Korea, Vietnam, or when signed out

page_date: no date shown; ms.date metadata 2026-08-18 ; no date shown; ms.date metadata 2026-08-31

where: Older app: profile > Memory > Microsoft usage data
what_it_does: Stops Copilot from using your data from Bing, MSN, Edge and other Microsoft products to personalize your experience.

where: Older app: profile > Memory > Delete all Memory; or ask Copilot to forget an item

where: Older app conversation history

plans: Personal Microsoft account; older Copilot app version only
limits: Uploaded files are kept no longer than 18 months, then deleted automatically.

control: Microsoft 365 Copilot conversations visibility (older app; label not given)

plans: Personal Microsoft account; older Copilot app version only
limits: Setting name not given. The FAQ says those conversations are not used to train Copilot models.

default: not stated, except Edge site data import, which works only if you choose to allow it (opt-in)

where: Windows: File > Options > Copilot; Mac: app menu > Preferences > Authoring and Proofing Tools > Copilot

what_it_does: Turns Copilot off in Outlook; the choice applies on all your devices signed in with the same account.
plans: Personal account; Outlook for Mac needs Version 16.95.3 or later
limits: Not available in classic Outlook for Windows, with no estimated date.

control: Turn on experiences that analyze your content

where: Account privacy settings in Microsoft 365 apps
what_it_does: Turning off all connected experiences also makes Copilot unavailable in Excel, OneNote, Outlook, PowerPoint and Word.
plans: Microsoft 365 Personal, Family, Premium, Pro (personal Microsoft account)
limits: Also turns off other features you may want.

where: Office ribbon customization
what_it_does: Removes the Copilot icon from the ribbon.
limits: Does not turn Copilot off; it stays reachable through other routes such as the shortcut menu.

control: Cancel subscription (switch to a plan with fewer features)

control: Export all Copilot in Microsoft 365 apps activity history / Delete all activity history
where: Privacy dashboard > Privacy > Empower your productivity > Copilot > Your Copilot app activity history > Copilot in Microsoft 365 apps
what_it_does: Exports as CSV, or deletes, all Copilot activity history from Excel, OneNote, Outlook, PowerPoint, Teams and Word.
limits: Deletion, not an opt-out.

where: Account Privacy settings in any Microsoft 365 app, or during Microsoft 365 install and setup
what_it_does: Choose whether to send optional diagnostic data, which helps Microsoft improve products and may also be used, in aggregate, to train and improve machine-learning features such as text predictions.
plans: Microsoft 365 apps, including the Microsoft Copilot app (formerly Microsoft 365 Copilot app)
limits: Required diagnostic data is always collected.

control: Windows Family Safety controls; account birth date

limits: Users cannot turn off Copilot features in Designer, Notepad or Paint.

where: Settings > Privacy & security > Recall & snapshots

limits: Snapshots stay on the device; some diagnostic data may still be sent depending on Windows privacy settings.

where: Recall icon in the system tray
what_it_does: Pauses saving snapshots until they resume automatically at 12:00 AM, or until you resume them manually.
plans: Windows 11 Copilot+ PCs; Recall in preview
limits: Resuming manually requires Windows Hello.

where: Settings > Privacy & security > Recall & snapshots
what_it_does: Excludes chosen apps and websites from snapshots; private browsing in supported browsers is not saved.
plans: Windows 11 Copilot+ PCs; Recall in preview
limits: Website filtering works only in supported browsers such as Edge, Firefox, Opera and Chrome. Embedded content, history or background tabs can still appear.

where: Settings > Privacy & security > Recall & snapshots
what_it_does: Helps reduce passwords, national ID numbers and credit card numbers being stored in snapshots.
plans: Windows 11 Copilot+ PCs; Recall in preview
limits: Users can turn it off. Described as reducing, not guaranteeing, removal.

control: Recall shows a customized experience using your snapshots

plans: Windows 11 Copilot+ PCs; Recall in preview

control: Snapshot storage size and duration (labels not given)
where: Settings > Privacy & security > Recall & snapshots
what_it_does: Change the maximum disk space for snapshots and choose how long they are kept; the oldest snapshots are deleted when the maximum is reached.
plans: Windows 11 Copilot+ PCs; Recall in preview
limits: Consumer page gives no setting names or values.

control: Delete snapshots / Delete all (by app or website)
where: Settings > Privacy & security > Recall & snapshots; Recall search results or snapshot view
what_it_does: Deletes snapshots, including all snapshots that contain a chosen app or website.
plans: Windows 11 Copilot+ PCs; Recall in preview
limits: Deletion, not an opt-out.

where: Settings > Privacy & security > Recall & snapshots > Advanced settings > Reset Recall
what_it_does: Deletes all snapshots and resets Recall settings after Windows Hello authorization.
plans: Windows 11 Copilot+ PCs; Recall in preview
limits: Does not delete snapshots already exported or shared with apps or websites.

control: Turn Windows features on or off (remove Recall)
where: Taskbar search > Turn Windows features on or off > uncheck Recall
what_it_does: Removes the Recall optional feature after a restart; previously saved snapshots are deleted.
plans: Windows 11 Copilot+ PCs; Recall in preview; available by default on unmanaged devices, removed by default on managed commercial and education devices
limits: Can be re-enabled the same way.

control: Allow Recall to be enabled / Turn off saving snapshots for use with Recall (plus deny lists, storage limits)
where: Group Policy: Windows Components > Windows AI; WindowsAI Policy CSP
what_it_does: Admins can remove or disable Recall, block snapshot saving, set app and URI deny lists and storage limits; they cannot turn on snapshots for users.
plans: Managed devices, where Recall is disabled by default; enablement policies on Pro, Enterprise, Education; deny lists and storage limits Enterprise and Education only
limits: Duration policy offers 30, 60, 90 or 180 days; if not configured, the maximum is 90 days unless the user sets another value.

where: Settings > Privacy & security > Click to Do; actions: Settings > Apps > Actions
what_it_does: Turns off Click to Do, which screenshots and analyzes your screen on the device when invoked; individual actions can also be disabled.
limits: An admin policy (DisableClickToDo) also exists; the page says that policy does not affect Click to Do inside Recall. Content leaves the device only when the user picks an online action such as Search the web.

where: Settings > System > AI Components > Experimental agentic features
what_it_does: Turning it on creates agent accounts and an agent workspace for agents like Copilot Actions, which can request six known user folders. Turning it off limits that folder access.
plans: Windows 11 preview; Copilot Actions for Windows Insiders in Copilot Labs
limits: Only a device administrator can turn it on, and it then applies to all users. Another Microsoft page gives the path via 'Agent tools'.

control: Files: Allow Always / Ask every time / Never allow (per agent)

page_date: Editor's note says last updated December 5th, 2025 (shown); ms.date 2025-10-15

what_it_does: Admins can force agent connectors on or off, allow-list MCP server connections, and set how long agent consent lasts before Windows asks again.

where: WindowsAI Policy CSP; Group Policy
what_it_does: Uninstalls the Microsoft Copilot app on managed devices that meet set conditions; the deprecated older policy turned off Windows Copilot.

control: Deployment type (e.g. Global Standard, Data Zone Standard, Standard, Regional Provisioned)

where: Limited Access registration form linked from Learn
what_it_does: If approved, Microsoft stops storing prompts and completions for abuse review and stops human review. Customers can confirm via 'ContentLogging' showing false.
plans: Only customers and partners managed by a Microsoft account team or in an eligible program; stricter for some advanced models
limits: Automated review may still run. Severe or recurring abuse can lead to access limits or a request to turn human review back on.

plans: Approval limited to customers and partners managed by a Microsoft account team or in an eligible program
limits: A safety control, not a privacy control; listed because it changes what the service filters.

control: NVIDIA Accounts / Guest Purchasers and Email Subscribers (exercise data subject rights)
where: Privacy Center (privacy.nvidia.com)
what_it_does: Lets users ask NVIDIA to erase or export their personal data. Deletion, not an opt-out.
plans: NVIDIA account holders and people signed up with an email address; others email privacy@nvidia.com
limits: Policy says identity is verified through the NVIDIA account or registered email.

where: Privacy Policy > Data Retention
what_it_does: NVIDIA keeps personal data while engagement continues and erases customer data after more than five years without engagement.
limits: No shorter retention choice for app or assistant data was found.

where: ChatRTX GitHub README
what_it_does: README says ChatRTX was deprecated as of 1/21/2026 and is no longer maintained.
limits: Repo is archived and the old ChatRTX page URL redirects to /en-us/ai-on-rtx/. NVIDIA app FAQ (Feb 24, 2026) still lists ChatRTX. No successor named.

where: ChatRTX GitHub README
what_it_does: ChatRTX ran fully on the user's Windows RTX PC, answering over the user's own files, with voice input through local Whisper or Parakeet models.
limits: No privacy settings, history controls or telemetry statements were documented.

where: NVIDIA API Trial Terms of Service
what_it_does: NVIDIA collects session metrics, error and execution logs, feedback, and prompts and outputs, without identifying users, to improve products including AI models.
limits: No opt-out found. Conflicts with Section 2.3, which says content is not stored or used after the session.

control: Before You Use AI Models (Acknowledge & Continue)
where: build.nvidia.com model playground pop-up
what_it_does: Notice says inputs and outputs are recorded for the trial and to improve NVIDIA products and AI models. Users must accept to continue.
limits: Says product-development logging is turned off when a demo needs personal data. Tells users not to upload confidential or personal data.

where: NVIDIA API Trial Terms of Service
what_it_does: NVIDIA promises not to store or use prompts or outputs after each session ends, unless Section 2.4 applies or it is disclosed for a service.
limits: Section 3.3 and the playground notice describe use for product and model improvement.

where: NVIDIA API Trial Terms of Service
what_it_does: For some services such as Fine Tuning, NVIDIA keeps uploaded content 30 days and fine-tuning output 90 days.
plans: API trial; differs with a paid Subscription
limits: Does not apply if the user buys a Subscription from the Service Provider. Security and abuse logs may be kept separately.

where: NVIDIA API Trial Terms Section 3.3
what_it_does: All API use is logged for security, fraud or abuse monitoring and shared with third-party service providers for that purpose.
limits: Retention period for these logs is not stated.

control: Voice input and other permitted personal data (Section 3.2)
where: NVIDIA API Trial Terms of Service
what_it_does: For services that allow personal data such as voice, NVIDIA and providers collect and record it to run the service, with consent where law requires.

where: NVIDIA API Trial Terms of Service
what_it_does: When users get third-party software through NVIDIA, NVIDIA may share their registration details and usage, but not payment method, with that provider.

where: Download NIM container from API catalog and run on own infrastructure
what_it_does: Developers can move from NVIDIA-hosted endpoints to running models in their own cloud or data center, which the FAQ says reduces the risk of data IP leakage.
plans: Developer Program (dev/test, up to 16 GPUs); NVIDIA AI Enterprise license for production
limits: Needs NVIDIA GPUs; production needs a paid license.

control: Prompts not collected from enterprise software
where: NVIDIA Software Licensing FAQ > Security, Data Privacy & Compliance
what_it_does: NVIDIA says data collection from its enterprise software excludes customer and end-user prompts, inputs and outputs, which stay in customer environments.
limits: Applies to self-hosted software, not the hosted API catalog.

where: NIM container environment variable
what_it_does: Set to 0 to turn off NIM telemetry, which sends hardware and NIM version metadata. NIM_TELEMETRY_ENABLE_ON_RTX must also be true on RTX GPUs.
limits: Experimental. The latest NIM for LLM and VLM variable reference (Oct 15, 2026) lists no telemetry variables.

where: Product Specific Terms for NVIDIA AI Products
what_it_does: Terms say NIM containers that collect telemetry do so to configure products and improve NVIDIA products, and NIM_TELEMETRY_MODE=0 disables it.
plans: NVIDIA AI Enterprise and other NIMs licensed under the AI Product Terms (including Developer Program licenses, Section F)
limits: Telemetry covers microservice settings, usage data and hardware environment.

where: NIM container environment variables
what_it_does: Set how much NIM logs and whether logs are JSON Lines. Logs go to stderr in the developer's own environment.
limits: Defaults: NIM_LOG_LEVEL WARNING, NIM_JSONL_LOGGING false. Page does not say whether prompts appear at DEBUG level.

where: NIM container arguments
what_it_does: Inference request trace spans are created only when the developer sets a trace endpoint, sending them to the developer's own collector.

where: NeMo Agent Toolkit CLI; first-run consent prompt
what_it_does: Turns off toolkit CLI usage telemetry sent to NVIDIA. Choice is saved in ~/.config/nat/telemetry.toml.
limits: First-run prompt answers yes if the user just presses Enter. Off in non-interactive runs. Added in v1.7.0 (GitHub release notes, May 21, 2026; not stated in the README).

where: Environment variable
what_it_does: Master switch that overrides the saved choice. NAT_TELEMETRY_ENDPOINT set to empty or NAT_TELEMETRY_DRY_RUN builds events without sending them.
limits: Only 1, true or yes enable telemetry; any other value disables it.

where: Toolkit README > Telemetry
what_it_does: NVIDIA says toolkit telemetry never includes command arguments, workflow, function or model names, config contents, file paths, hostnames, usernames, IP addresses or outputs.
limits: Events include command name, outcome, duration, exit code, exception class and Python version.

where: Workflow config YAML
what_it_does: Developer chooses log and trace exporters (console, file, Phoenix, Weave, LangSmith and others), deciding where agent traces are sent.
limits: Toolkit security page warns traces can capture prompts and responses and advises log scrubbing and access control.

where: Weave tracing exporter config
what_it_does: Removes personal data such as emails, phone numbers, card numbers and named keys from traces sent to W&B Weave.
limits: Only documented for the Weave exporter.

where: auto_memory_agent wrapper config
what_it_does: Flags controlling whether the memory wrapper stores user messages and agent replies and injects past memory into each response.
limits: Defaults apply once a developer adds the optional memory wrapper and a memory plugin (Mem0, Redis, Zep and others).

where: Interactive workflows (UserInteractionManager)
what_it_does: Lets a workflow pause and wait for a person's input before continuing.
limits: nat run supports only text prompts; other prompt types need nat serve.

where: Workflow middleware
what_it_does: Shows a human prompt before a function runs, after it returns, or both. Developer code decides what to do with the answer.
limits: Abstract class; developer must write the decision logic. Added in v1.9.0 (GitHub release notes, Sep 10, 2026; not stated in the cited file).

where: Workflow middleware (nvidia-nat-security plugin)
what_it_does: Runs NeMo Guardrails input and output rails on chosen functions. A BLOCK result skips the call or replaces output with a refusal.
limits: Works on strings only; needs a guardrails policy. Added in v1.8.0 (GitHub release notes, June 16, 2026; the docs page does not say when it was added).

where: Defense middleware config
what_it_does: Checks tool inputs or outputs with a model and blocks, replaces or only logs unsafe content. fail_closed treats verifier failures as threats.
limits: Documented in an example README, not the main docs.

where: NeMo Guardrails config
what_it_does: Detects personal data in user input, model output or retrieved text and blocks or masks it.
limits: Can run on a local NIM or an NVIDIA-hosted endpoint; the hosted option sends the checked text to an NVIDIA endpoint.
page_date: not shown (docs Latest; newest version listed v0.24.1)

where: NeMo Guardrails config
what_it_does: Checks each model tool call against the declared tools and schemas, and checks tool results. Violations block the request.
limits: IORails engine is opt-in and experimental. It validates calls but does not ask a human.
page_date: not shown (docs Latest; newest version listed v0.24.1)

where: Environment variable or ~/.config/nemoguardrails/do_not_track
what_it_does: Stops the library's anonymous usage telemetry, heartbeats and local audit file.
limits: Must be set before the library starts. Telemetry is off automatically in CI and pytest. Documented from v0.22.0 (GitHub release notes, May 22, 2026; the v0.21.0 docs have no telemetry page).
page_date: not shown (docs Latest; newest version listed v0.24.1)

where: Guardrails telemetry page
what_it_does: NVIDIA says telemetry excludes prompts, completions, model names, rail configs, API keys, file paths, usernames and IP addresses.
limits: NVIDIA may share an aggregated subset publicly, such as adoption charts.
page_date: not shown (docs Latest; newest version listed v0.24.1)

where: NeMo Guardrails config.yml > tracing
what_it_does: Controls whether traces record user inputs and model outputs. Docs warn this can include personal data.
limits: Opt-in content capture for IORails added in v0.23.0 (GitHub release notes, July 1, 2026).
page_date: not shown (docs Latest; newest version listed v0.24.1)

control: Global Privacy Control and cookie settings (NVIDIA websites)
where: build.nvidia.com cookie banner; Privacy Policy > Preference Signal
what_it_does: Policy says NVIDIA websites honor GPC by turning off Performance, Personalization and Advertising cookies. build.nvidia.com shows the NVIDIA cookie banner with Reject Optional.
limits: Covers website cookies, not API calls. Whether build.nvidia.com reads GPC was not tested; banner was seen but not clicked.

where: Privacy Center
what_it_does: People with an NVIDIA account (including Developer Program) or a newsletter email can opt out of 'sales' and 'sharing' of information they provided for interest-based ads by entering that email.
plans: NVIDIA account holders and email newsletter subscribers
limits: Cookie-based sharing needs a separate opt-out on each website.

control: NVIDIA Accounts (exercise your data subject rights)
where: Privacy Center
what_it_does: Account holders and email subscribers can use the Privacy Center to exercise privacy rights, including erasure; others email privacy@nvidia.com. Deletion, not an opt-out.
limits: API trial personal data is handled under the NVIDIA Privacy Policy (Terms Section 3.1). No way to delete specific prompts was found.

where: Privacy Policy
what_it_does: NVIDIA says it usually transfers and stores personal data in the United States, using Standard Contractual Clauses and the Data Privacy Framework.
limits: No region choice for hosted API endpoints was found.

control: Ensure your data isn't used for model training (NIM page statement)
where: NIM microservices page > Start Prototyping for Free (NIM API endpoints on DGX Cloud)
what_it_does: NVIDIA's product page says data sent to its hosted prototyping endpoints is not used for model training.
limits: Marketing statement with no setting. Conflicts with API Trial Terms Section 3.3 and the playground notice, which say inputs and outputs may improve AI models.

where: Settings > Data controls
what_it_does: Switch that decides whether your new conversations can be used to train OpenAI models. On personal plans it also covers Codex tasks.
plans: Services for individuals; page names Free, Plus, Pro (Go not named here)
limits: Default inferred from opt-out wording. Rating a reply with thumbs up or down can still put the whole chat into training. Codex 'Include environments' setting is separate.

control: Do not train on my content
where: OpenAI Privacy Portal
what_it_does: Request-based alternative to the in-app switch; opts the account out of training on new ChatGPT conversations and Codex tasks.
plans: Services for individuals (Free, Plus, Pro named)
limits: Portal page did not render in my session, so only the help article was checked. Either this or the switch is enough.

control: Include your audio recordings / Include your video recordings
where: Settings > Data Controls, under Improve the model for everyone
what_it_does: Lets Voice audio or video clips be used for model training. Clips are not used for training unless you turn these on.
plans: Free, Plus, Pro in personal workspaces
limits: Voice transcripts still follow the main training switch. Shared clips may be reviewed by OpenAI teams. Clips already separated from your account may still be used after you stop.

where: New chat > Temporary; pick personalization before the first message
what_it_does: Keeps the chat out of history, creates or updates no memories, and excludes it from training while it stays temporary. Unpersonalized skips memory, custom instructions, and plugins.
limits: OpenAI may keep a copy up to 30 days for safety. Saving it makes it a regular chat. Release notes say Unpersonalized is the default.

where: Chat ••• menu > Delete; Settings > Data controls > Delete all chats
what_it_does: Removes one chat or all chats from your account view at once and schedules permanent deletion. This is deletion, not an opt-out.
limits: Permanent deletion within 30 days unless already de-identified or kept for security or legal duties. No restore. Library files need separate deletion. Archiving does not change retention.

where: Settings > Personalization > Memory
what_it_does: Stops ChatGPT from using remembered details to personalize replies. Turning off Reference saved memories also turns off Reference chat history.
