limits: Does not delete past chats. Limited safety use of context in rare high-risk cases continues. If model improvement is on, chats and memories can be used for training.

where: Settings > Personalization > Memory
what_it_does: Stops ChatGPT from using past conversations to personalize future replies.
limits: Info remembered from past chats is scheduled for deletion within 30 days after you turn it off. Original chats and saved memories stay unless deleted.

control: Delete and turn off memory (and deleting single saved memories)
where: Memory summary ••• menu; Saved memories controls
what_it_does: Deletes the remembered information shown in the memory summary and turns Memory off; single saved memories can also be deleted. Deletion, not an opt-out.
limits: Past chats stay. Deleting a chat does not delete a memory saved from it. OpenAI may keep logs of deleted saved memories up to 30 days.

where: Memory summary, when the option is available (or tell ChatGPT in chat not to use the information)
what_it_does: Reduces future references to a remembered detail without deleting the chat, file, email, or other source it came from.
limits: Shown only when available. Nothing is deleted.

where: Project ••• > Project settings > Memory (Default memory or Project-only memory)
what_it_does: Keeps a project's chats from using memories or chats outside the project, and keeps project information out of memory used elsewhere.
limits: Release note dated August 14, 2026. Shared projects always use it. ChatGPT Work is unavailable in such projects. Changes may take a few hours.

where: Settings > Personalization (web, desktop); Settings > Customize ChatGPT (iOS, Android)
what_it_does: Turns custom instructions off for all chats; you can also edit or delete the instructions for future chats.
limits: Earlier chats keep old instructions unless deleted. Page says instruction data is used to improve models, subject to the training opt-out. Plug-ins may receive relevant instructions.

where: Settings > Ads controls (also called Ad Controls)
what_it_does: When off, ads are still chosen from the current chat thread (plus basic context such as general location and language), but other chat threads, ads history, and ad topics are not used.
plans: Free and Go, where ads are available
limits: Ads still appear; general location and language still used. Not initially offered in EEA or Switzerland. No ads for accounts identified as under 18 or in Temporary Chats.

where: Settings > Ads controls
what_it_does: When off, past chats and memory are not used to pick ads; ads lean on the current chat thread.
limits: Page says that when ads personalization is on and Memory is on, ChatGPT may use memories and recent chats to pick ads; both are managed in Settings. Hiding, reporting, viewing, or clicking ads is not added to memory.

where: Settings > Ads controls
what_it_does: Clears ads history and topics so they stop being used for ads; chats are not affected. Deletion, not an opt-out.
limits: Data can take up to 30 days to be fully removed.

control: Change plan to go ad-free > Reduce message limits
where: Settings > Ads controls
what_it_does: Removes ads on the Free plan in exchange for lower usage limits and fewer tools.
plans: Free only; Go users must switch to Free or upgrade
limits: Only where ads are tested. Some tools such as image generation or deep research become unavailable. Paid ad-free route is Plus or Pro.

control: Hide ad / Report ad / About this ad / Ask ChatGPT
where: Three-dot menu on an ad
what_it_does: Dismiss or report an ad and see why it was shown. ChatGPT cannot see your ads unless you choose Ask ChatGPT to share one.
limits: An ad shared through Ask ChatGPT can be referenced later if Reference chat history is on.

where: Settings > Data Controls > Marketing Privacy (web); signed out: Manage Cookies or Your Privacy Choices footer link
what_it_does: Blocks sharing of cookie IDs, IP, hashed email or phone, and basic activity with ad platforms used to market OpenAI products on other sites.
limits: Covers OpenAI's own ads on other sites, not ads inside ChatGPT. A signed-out choice applies only to that browser. Article does not mention GPC.

control: Global Privacy Control (legally recognized opt-out mechanism)
where: US Privacy Policy, section 9, 'Your Opt-Out Rights'
what_it_does: Policy says you can opt out of targeted-advertising sharing with marketing partners by sending a recognized opt-out signal such as GPC. It says OpenAI does not sell personal data.
plans: Residents of US states with these privacy laws
limits: Policy does not say how GPC is detected or whether it reaches account settings or in-ChatGPT ads. No such sharing for users known to be under 18.

control: Cookie settings (Analytics and Marketing Performance cookies)
where: Cookie settings link on OpenAI sites; browser settings
what_it_does: Where local law allows, lets you choose which non-necessary cookies are used: OpenAI's own analytics cookie (__obi) and marketing-measurement cookies from LinkedIn, Google, Reddit, TikTok, Meta, Bing, Snapchat, and Impact.
plans: All site visitors, depending on jurisdiction
limits: Necessary cookies cannot be disabled. Choices are per device and browser. The cookie policy does not mention GPC or which choices are preset.

where: Links in OpenAI marketing messages
what_it_does: Stops marketing communications from OpenAI.

control: Privacy rights requests (know or access, delete, correct, appeal)
where: privacy.openai.com or dsar@openai.com; authorized agents and appeals via dsar@openai.com
what_it_does: Residents of covered US states can ask to access, delete, or correct personal data and appeal a refusal.
limits: Identity checks may be required; requests are refused if identity cannot be verified.

where: EU Privacy Policy, 'Your rights'; account tools, privacy.openai.com, or dsar@openai.com
what_it_does: Object to direct marketing and to processing based on legitimate interests, which the policy cites for model training; withdraw consent where consent is the basis.
plans: Users in the EEA, UK, Switzerland
limits: Policy says ads personalization for Free and Go users there relies on consent. It does not explain how objections to training are handled.

control: Remove personal data from ChatGPT responses
where: Privacy Portal > Make a Privacy Request
what_it_does: Asks OpenAI to stop certain personal information about you appearing in ChatGPT answers; open to people with or without an account.
plans: Under laws such as the GDPR
limits: Reviewed case by case against free expression and public interest; ID proof required.

control: Objection to processing of personal data by models (training data)
where: Privacy Portal or privacy@openai.com
what_it_does: People in certain places can object to OpenAI's models processing their personal information, including data gathered from the public internet for training.
limits: Rights may not be absolute; reviewed case by case. Separately, website owners can block training crawls by disallowing GPTBot in robots.txt.

where: Settings > Data controls > Location; device or browser location permission
what_it_does: Turns device location sharing on or off. On iOS and Android, you may be able to turn off precise location while still sharing approximate device location.
limits: IP-based approximate location is still used, and general location may go to search partners; no opt-out described. Parents can turn sharing off for linked teens.

where: Settings > Data controls > Information shared with apps
what_it_does: Review or change permission for ChatGPT to fill your name and email in restaurant booking flows; choices are allow once, allow for future bookings, or decline.
limits: Covers OpenTable and Yelp booking flows; Resy uses its own sign-in.

control: Always ask / Allow read actions / Allow low-risk actions / Allow all actions
where: Settings > Plugins (or Apps) > Permissions; per connected account settings
what_it_does: Sets when ChatGPT must ask before reading from or acting in connected apps. Always ask is strictest; Allow all actions removes prompts.
plans: Personal accounts with a plugin that includes an app
limits: Release notes and the Health article say the default is Allow low-risk actions if unchanged. Does not grant or remove app access. Allow all actions only per app or account.

control: Deny / Decline, Allow once, Allow low-risk actions, Always allow (approval card)
where: Approval card shown before a supported app action
what_it_does: Refuse or approve one proposed app action, or save broader approval for future low-risk or supported actions.
limits: Always allow is not offered to managed-workspace members or for actions needing extra safety review. Some sensitive actions are denied outright.

where: Settings > Plugins > select the app > disconnect
what_it_does: Stops future ChatGPT access to that connected app account.
limits: Enabled apps can receive chat context, memories if Memory is on, IP address, and approximate location. (That past chats using app data stay after disconnecting is stated in the Memory and Deleting chats articles, not on this page.)

control: Health permissions (Settings > Plugins > Health) / Remove account (medical records, Health > Accounts) / Disconnect (Apple Health)
where: Settings > Plugins > Health; Health > Accounts
what_it_does: Choose whether ChatGPT asks before using connected health data, or disconnect medical records and Apple Health so synced data is deleted.
default: Allow low-risk actions for new Health connections if the global Plugins setting is unchanged
plans: Free, Go, Plus, Pro in the U.S., age 18 or older
limits: As of September 2026 new connections inherit the global default, Allow low-risk actions. Synced data deleted within 30 days of disconnect. Health data not used for foundation-model training or ads.

control: Always ask / Auto approve / Always allow (cloud browser website access)
where: Settings > Cloud browser; per-site allow or block
what_it_does: Decides whether ChatGPT Work's cloud browser must ask before visiting a new website. Per-site allow or block choices override the general setting.
default: asks before each new website (page wording; matches Always ask)
plans: Paid plans except Free and Go (ChatGPT Work)
limits: Default is to ask before a new site. Site access is separate from approval of consequential actions. OpenAI does not recommend Always allow.

where: In the chat during ChatGPT Work cloud browser tasks
what_it_does: ChatGPT asks you in chat to confirm hard-to-reverse actions, such as confirming a booking or making a payment, before doing them.
plans: Paid plans except Free and Go
limits: Described as built-in; no setting described. Some tasks need a final step you complete yourself.

control: Take over (cloud browser) and secure sign-in form
where: Link or prompt in the chat during a cloud browser task
what_it_does: Take direct control of the remote browser. Credentials typed in the secure sign-in form go to the remote browser, are hidden from the model, and are not stored.
plans: Paid plans except Free and Go
limits: Signed-in sessions persist for later tasks until they expire or you clear browser data.

control: Browser data (clear all sites or individual sites)
where: Settings > Cloud browser > Browser data
what_it_does: Deletes the cloud browser's cookies, browser data, and signed-in sessions for all sites or chosen sites.
plans: Paid plans except Free and Go
limits: Clearing signs you out of those sites. Website information used in tasks follows your ChatGPT data controls.

control: ChatGPT agent (retired): watch mode, Take over browser, screenshot deletion
where: Legacy agent mode; help page now says ChatGPT agent is no longer available
what_it_does: Legacy safeguards: confirmations for high-impact actions, watch mode on some sites, takeover with no screenshots captured. Deleting a chat deleted its screenshots.
plans: Was Plus, Pro, Business, Enterprise, Edu
limits: Retired in favor of ChatGPT Work. Page says deleted chats and screenshots leave systems within 90 days, and calls Plus/Pro training 'opted in', both conflicting with other articles.

where: Settings > Security > Advanced security; per chat 'Turn off for this chat'
what_it_does: Cuts outbound network features to curb data leaks from prompt injection: cached-only browsing, no deep research or agent mode, no file downloads for analysis, limited live app access.
plans: Eligible personal accounts and self-serve ChatGPT Business
limits: Optional. Does not change memory, sharing, or training settings, and does not stop all prompt injection. Codex network access unaffected.

where: Scheduled page; Settings > Notifications > Manage tasks
what_it_does: Pause, resume, edit, or delete one-time, recurring, monitoring, and event-triggered tasks, including a Weekly finances update task that connecting a financial account may create.
plans: Free, Go, Plus, Pro (event-triggered tasks: Plus and Pro only)
limits: Deleting a task's chat only pauses the task and leaves its shared link. Notification type is set in Settings > Notifications.

where: Settings > Voice
what_it_does: Turn-by-turn voice that transcribes speech first; the audio is deleted after transcription unless you chose to share audio for training.
plans: Depends on plan, region, app version
limits: With Live or Advanced, audio clips (and Advanced video clips) are kept with the transcript for 30 days. Parents can turn off Voice for teens.

control: Background conversations setting, Start with Voice, mute, stop camera or Share Screen
where: Settings > Voice; in-call microphone, camera, and screen-sharing controls
what_it_does: Limit Voice running in the background, stop Voice auto-starting, mute the microphone, and stop live video or screen sharing.
plans: Video and screen sharing only in Advanced on iOS and Android
limits: Page names where background conversations are controlled but not the exact toggle label.

control: Computer history (Turn on, Pause, Exclude these apps, Exclude these websites, delete or clear)
where: ChatGPT macOS app: Settings > Integrations > Computer history; macOS menu bar
what_it_does: Optional activity capture for ChatGPT and Codex memories. Pause it, limit contributing apps and sites, delete items, or clear the last 10 minutes, hour, day, or all.
plans: Pro; Business and Enterprise only after an admin grants access
limits: Temporary event files kept up to 48 hours; memory files stay on the Mac unencrypted until deleted. OpenAI processes event files but says it does not train on them.

where: Device settings, contacts permission for ChatGPT
what_it_does: Optional upload of contact phone numbers, converted to hashes, to suggest people you know; you can withdraw contact access in device settings.
limits: Hashed numbers may be kept on OpenAI servers to match people who join later.
page_date: Updated: last month; Last Updated: April 27, 2026

control: Delete shared link / Delete all shared links
where: Settings > Data controls > Shared links > Manage
what_it_does: Stops future access to links for shared conversations or scheduled tasks. Shared conversation links are anonymous by default.
limits: Does not delete the original chat or task, or copies others saved. Task links survive chat deletion and need separate deletion.

where: Settings > Account > Delete; Privacy Portal > Delete my ChatGPT account
what_it_does: Permanently deletes the OpenAI account, ending access to ChatGPT and the API. Deletion, not an opt-out.
limits: Data deleted within 30 days, except limited data kept where law requires or permits. Does not cancel Apple subscriptions; may not pause or cancel active ad campaigns.

where: Settings > Data controls; or Privacy Portal
what_it_does: Request a copy of your ChatGPT data. An access right, not an opt-out.
limits: Not self-serve in Business, Enterprise, or Healthcare workspaces.

where: Settings > Account > Age > Verify age
what_it_does: Adults placed in the teen experience can verify their age; after verifying, OpenAI stops running age prediction on the account.
limits: Needs a live selfie and/or government ID sent to Persona, which deletes them within 7 days. Objections to age prediction go to privacy@openai.com.

control: Parental controls: Improve the model for everyone, Reference saved memories, Voice Mode, Image generation, Cloud browser, Codex network access, Quiet hours
where: Parent's Settings > Parental controls > Family members > teen
what_it_does: A linked parent can switch off a teen's model training, saved-memory use, Voice, image generation, Work cloud browser and network access, and set no-use quiet hours.
limits: These toggles default to Enabled; Quiet hours is off. Saved-memory default may differ by region. Parents cannot read teen chats.

where: Settings > Trusted contact
what_it_does: Optional: name one adult who may be alerted if reviewers find a serious suicide-related concern in your chats; transcripts are not shared.
plans: Personal accounts, adults 18 or older (19 or older in Korea, per page footnote); not in Voice; not in Business, Enterprise, or Edu workspaces
limits: Relies on automated monitoring and human review before any alert.

where: Settings > Personalization > Reference photos
what_it_does: Replace or delete the selfie saved for virtual try-on of clothing. Deletion control.
limits: Photos are saved for future try-ons once used.

control: Custom rules: Take action without asking / Take action if pre-approved / Ask before taking action / Hand off to you
where: Dot profile > Customize > Custom rules (mobile); Learn docs: Settings > Personalization > Custom rules
what_it_does: For a described action, choose whether your dot acts freely, acts only when you explicitly asked, asks first, or hands the step to you.
plans: Pro (not EEA, Switzerland, UK) and Business Premium; Enterprise beta
limits: Default rules exist but are not listed. Learn docs label option two 'Take action when you say so'. Rules cannot override built-in safety, Auto-review, or research limits.

control: Built-in approval requirements (approval each time, approval in advance, take over)
where: Applied automatically; Dots privacy FAQ, 'Actions, approvals, and control'
what_it_does: Built-in policies the dot is instructed to follow: for sensitive actions it may ask for your explicit approval (sometimes given in advance) or ask you to take over; password changes and money transfers require you to take over; purchases with cards saved on merchant sites require approval.
limits: Custom Rules can change the default approval behavior for supported actions but cannot remove core safety requirements, such as taking over to change a password. Approving one message is not ongoing permission. The dot can still make mistakes.

where: Automatic check before certain planned actions
what_it_does: Checks planned actions, such as sending an email, against your instructions, custom rules, and safety rules; may block, ask for approval, or stop.
limits: Custom rules cannot change it and required checks cannot be turned off. The FAQ links a Codex Auto-review policy page; no dots-specific setting found.

where: Dot profile > ••• menu > Pause
what_it_does: Stops your dot's work until you resume it.
limits: Learn docs say Pause stops only the current main task; delegated tasks and scheduled runs must be stopped separately. Stopping does not undo completed actions.

control: Stop delegated task (Activity) / disable or delete scheduled task (Scheduled)
where: Dot profile > Activity; Scheduled
what_it_does: Stop individual background tasks your dot handed off, and disable or delete its recurring schedules.
limits: Stopping work does not undo completed actions.

where: Dot profile > ••• > Reset, then confirm Reset
what_it_does: Deletes the dot with its conversations, saved memories, and scheduled tasks. The only way to delete the dot's own memories. Deletion, not an opt-out.
limits: Privacy FAQ: files, Codex threads, and ChatGPT chats it created remain, as do ChatGPT memories. Individual dot memories cannot be viewed or deleted.

control: Memory (ChatGPT memory setting shared with the dot)
where: ChatGPT Settings > Personalization > Memory; dot profile > Customize > Memory (mobile)
what_it_does: Turning off ChatGPT Memory stops memories and recent chat context flowing between ChatGPT and your dot.
limits: Does not delete what the dot already received. The dot's own saved notes are separate, and changing memory settings does not necessarily change them.

control: Improve the model for everyone (applies to dots)
where: ChatGPT Settings > Data controls
what_it_does: On personal plans, decides whether dot conversations, actions, delegated work, automations, and connected-app data used in chats can train OpenAI models.
plans: Personal plans; Business, Enterprise, Edu not used by default
limits: Proactive research and its notes are not trained on directly unless brought into an eligible chat. Human review may still occur, including for safety.

control: Plugin permissions and disconnect (ChatGPT Plugins tab)
where: ChatGPT Plugins tab; dot profile > Customize > Plugins (mobile)
what_it_does: Choose which apps the dot can use and whether it may read or also change content; disconnect an app to stop new access.
limits: Permissions are shared with ChatGPT, ChatGPT Work, and Codex. Disconnecting does not delete what the dot already learned; it may read connected apps proactively.

where: ChatGPT desktop app on that computer: dot profile > Computers > Your computer
what_it_does: Grants or removes the dot's ability to use files and work on your own computer; otherwise it uses its own cloud computer.
limits: When allowed, the dot can reach the computer from any messaging channel and use your local browser if its cloud browser is blocked.

where: Connect your computer to the dot, then allow in device settings
what_it_does: The dot can use your computer's camera, microphone, or screen only after you connect the computer and grant the ChatGPT app device permission.

where: Reply STOP to a text from your dot
what_it_does: Stops outgoing text messages from your dot.
plans: Limited beta for Pro users in the US
limits: Texting runs through a third-party provider. STOP does not delete conversations; use Reset.

control: Activity review, Take over / Return control
where: Desktop app: dot profile (In progress, Scheduled, Completed); Computers
what_it_does: Review ongoing, scheduled, and finished work, open the dot's cloud computer, and take direct control of it when needed.
limits: Review only; no way found to delete single activity records. Privacy FAQ says the dot's context does not keep credentials, images, or screenshots.

control: Workspace admin enablement (dots beta) and custom-rule policy
where: Enterprise, Edu, Healthcare workspace admin settings
what_it_does: Admins decide whether members can try dots; the beta is off by default. Learn docs say a workspace can also disable custom rules.

where: privacy.openai.com or dsar@openai.com
what_it_does: Ask for access, correction, deletion, or a copy of personal data, even without an OpenAI account.
limits: Identity verification may be needed.

where: Slack DM or channels you add the dot to
what_it_does: By default the dot replies only to you; it engages others or monitors channels only if you tell it to. It checks permission before sharing private details.
limits: Adding the dot to a channel does not start monitoring. Set by instruction, not a toggle.

control: API data excluded from training unless shared (opt-in)
where: Default policy; Data controls in the OpenAI platform guide
what_it_does: OpenAI does not use API data to train or improve its models unless the organization explicitly opts in to share data.
limits: Stated as applying since March 1, 2023.

control: Share inputs and outputs with OpenAI (Enabled for all or selected projects)
where: Platform organization settings, data sharing page
what_it_does: Opt-in switch letting OpenAI use inputs and outputs from chosen projects to improve and train models; owners can turn it off anytime.
plans: Not offered to Enterprise or ZDR organizations
limits: Only organization owners can change it. Eligible orgs may get free daily tokens for shared traffic.

where: Platform organization settings, data sharing page
what_it_does: Opt-in sharing of evals and fine-tuning data from all or selected projects with OpenAI.
limits: Incentives: some free eval runs and discounted inference for shared reinforcement fine-tuning jobs.

control: Playground feedback sharing (enabled / enabled for selected projects)
where: Organization settings page
what_it_does: When enabled, members get a thumbs-down button in the Playground that can send the conversation, including uploaded files, to OpenAI feedback systems.
plans: API organizations, except accounts with Zero Data Retention (they cannot opt in to data sharing)

where: Settings > Organization > Data controls > Data Retention tab, after approval; org or project level
what_it_does: Keeps customer content out of abuse monitoring logs across API endpoints, with rare exceptions for image and file inputs.
limits: By default abuse logs may hold prompts and outputs up to 30 days. Needs OpenAI approval. Images flagged as possible CSAM are still kept for review.

where: Settings > Organization > Data controls > Data Retention tab, after approval; org or project level
what_it_does: Keeps content out of abuse logs and forces the store parameter to false on Responses and Chat Completions.
limits: Endpoints marked ineligible may still keep application state. Without ZDR, all queries use extended prompt caching. CSAM-flagged images still kept.

control: Private Retention with Private Safety Processing
where: Applied by OpenAI to approved ZDR or MAM customers, with written notice
what_it_does: If OpenAI makes a model ineligible for ZDR or MAM, content sits in encrypted logs but is excluded from human review unless law requires it.
limits: Under the separate Safety Retention mode, flagged content may be kept and reviewed by humans.

where: Request parameter on POST /v1/responses
what_it_does: Set store to false to stop OpenAI saving the generated response for later retrieval.
limits: When stored, data is kept at least 30 days. ZDR forces false. Responses attached to a Conversation persist until deleted, per the conversation-state guide.

where: Request parameter on POST /v1/chat/completions
what_it_does: Turns storage of Chat Completions outputs off when set to false.
default: on for new accounts (per migration guide)
limits: Migration guide says stored by default for new accounts; the API reference states no default and the data-controls table lists no stored application state.

where: Files API parameter; delete via API or dashboard
what_it_does: Auto-delete uploaded files after a set time, or delete files and Assistants objects yourself.
limits: Assistants, threads, and vector stores are removed 30 days after deletion; objects never deleted are kept indefinitely.

where: Project session storage setting; store on /v1/live/sessions
what_it_does: Session storage is off by default; when enabled, store: true keeps the session recording for 30 days for download or forking.
limits: No public endpoint to delete stored sessions. ZDR forces store false.

control: Data residency (project region or regional endpoint)
where: Choose a region when creating a project, or use a regional domain per request
what_it_does: Stores customer content at rest in a chosen region, and in some regions also runs inference there.
limits: System data such as account and usage data is excluded. Non-US regions need MAM or ZDR approval. Several regions store but do not process.

where: Organization setup with AWS KMS, Google Cloud, or Azure Key Vault
what_it_does: Encrypts application state at OpenAI with keys held in the customer's own key management service.
limits: Not supported for Assistants or vision fine-tuning.

where: Responses API web_search tool setting
what_it_does: Runs web search in offline, cache-only mode instead of live internet access.
limits: The web_search_preview variant ignores it. Docs mention it mainly for HIPAA and BAA eligibility.

where: Agents SDK environment variable, code, or per-run config
what_it_does: Stops the SDK from sending traces of model calls, tool calls, handoffs, and guardrails to OpenAI's Traces dashboard.
limits: Data already buffered still flushes after disabling. Source is OpenAI's SDK docs on github.io; platform docs confirm tracing is on by default.

where: RunConfig / VoicePipelineConfig; env var OPENAI_AGENTS_TRACE_INCLUDE_SENSITIVE_DATA
what_it_does: Set to false to keep model and tool inputs and outputs, or audio, out of traces while keeping tracing on.
limits: Responses spans still carry the response ID as metadata for official OpenAI endpoints.

where: Agents SDK tracing setup
what_it_does: Replaces the default exporter so traces go only to the destinations you choose and not to OpenAI's backend.
limits: add_trace_processor() keeps the OpenAI exporter. A failing redaction processor does not stop other processors from receiving data.

where: Agents SDK tool definitions; MCP server configs; HostedMCPTool tool_config
what_it_does: Pauses an agent run until a person approves or rejects marked tool calls; approvals can also be decided in code.
default: off for local ShellTool and ApplyPatchTool (needs_approval defaults to False); not stated for other tools
limits: Applies only to tools the developer marks. Malformed arguments fail closed to manual approval.

where: Agents API (beta): delete sessions and published artifacts
what_it_does: Delete agent sessions and artifacts you no longer need; otherwise session state is kept so work can continue.
limits: No Zero Data Retention support, even with a self-hosted sandbox; data residency in the United States only.

control: Agents API tracing (Logs > Agents) and trace export
where: Platform dashboard Logs > Agents; session traces export endpoint
what_it_does: Records model, tool, and subagent steps for each session turn. Exporting traces through the API must be enabled for the organization.
limits: No way to turn tracing off was described on this page.

control: require_approval and allowed_tools on the remote MCP server / connector tool (Responses API)
where: Responses API: remote MCP server and connector tool parameters
what_it_does: require_approval sets whether OpenAI asks for your approval before data is shared with a connector or remote MCP server ('always' or 'never'); allowed_tools limits which server tools are imported.
limits: Data sent to an MCP server then follows that server's own policies.

where: Account settings → Preferences → 'AI data retention' toggle
what_it_does: Stops your search data from being used to train Perplexity's AI models. Applies only to data collected after you opt out.
plans: On by default for Free, Pro and Max; Enterprise Pro and Enterprise Max data is never used for training
limits: Past training data cannot be deleted. Data is still processed for service, legal compliance and product improvement. Other help pages label it 'AI Data Usage'.

where: Settings → Memory
what_it_does: Stops Perplexity from drawing on your past questions and answers when writing new answers.
limits: Turning it off deletes nothing; delete past sessions from history to stop their influence. Incognito always turns it off.

where: Settings → Memory
what_it_does: Stops Perplexity from saving details from your sessions as memories for later answers.
limits: Turning it off does not clear existing memories. Memory content may be used to improve models unless AI Data Retention is off.

where: Settings → Memory → Manage memories
what_it_does: Lets you search, review and delete single memories or clear all of them.
limits: Deletion, not an opt-out. Perplexity may keep a log of cleared memories for up to 30 days.

where: Settings → Memory settings → Brain (Computer); admins: Organization settings → Memory → Enable Brain
what_it_does: Stops Brain, which runs in the background, from writing new knowledge about your projects, people and files into Computer's memory.
plans: Max and Enterprise Max (Research Preview, Computer)
limits: AI Data Retention does not cover what Brain writes; Brain's own toggle controls it. Existing entries must be edited or deleted separately.

where: Profile icon menu → Incognito
what_it_does: Starts private threads for sensitive queries that expire after 24 hours.
plans: not stated (page only notes that logged-out sessions are anonymous and expire after 14 days)
limits: Logged-out threads expire after 14 days. Another help page says incognito searches are never stored; Comet AI queries in incognito still reach Perplexity servers.

control: Delete all threads / Delete (thread, project, page)
where: Library (perplexity.ai/library) → ⋯ menu
what_it_does: Deletes all threads, a single thread, or a project or page. The action cannot be undone.
limits: Deletion, not an opt-out. Files are kept for 30 days by default; deleting the whole session removes its uploads.

where: Account settings (perplexity.ai/account/details) → Delete account (or Learn more at the bottom of the page)
what_it_does: Disables the account and permanently deletes all account and personal data; once complete it cannot be reversed.
limits: Deletion, not an opt-out. Completes within 30 days; signing back in before then cancels the request. Cancel any subscription first.

where: Account settings (perplexity.ai/account/details)
what_it_does: Emails you a download link with a copy of your data (self-serve right of access).
limits: Access right, not an opt-out.

where: GDPR Compliance help article; privacy notice contact form
what_it_does: Formal requests for rectification, erasure, restriction, objection and portability, including by a legal representative.
limits: Erasure deletes the whole account only, not chosen threads or dates. Requests to opt out of essential processing are refused.

control: Opt-out of Website Targeted Advertising (cookie consent pop-up)
where: Cookie consent pop-up on Perplexity web pages
what_it_does: Opts you out of cookie and pixel based targeted advertising on Perplexity websites.
plans: not stated (notice covers Perplexity websites, Comet and apps; it excludes Enterprise and API data where Perplexity acts as a processor)
limits: Saved per browser; repeat after switching devices or clearing cache. The notice lists identifiers and activity shared with advertising partners for targeted ads.

where: Browser-level signal (Privacy Notice → Your Choices)
what_it_does: Perplexity treats a GPC signal from your browser as a targeted-advertising opt-out where applicable law requires it.
plans: not stated (applies to GPC signals sent by web browsers)
limits: Applies to the current browser only. A conflicting manual choice on the site wins. Do Not Track is not honored. No 'Do Not Sell or Share' link found.

where: Mobile device settings menu
what_it_does: Limits SDK-based targeted advertising in Perplexity's mobile apps through your phone's own settings.
limits: No in-app toggle is described; relies on operating system controls.

where: Account settings → Personalization
what_it_does: Lets you opt in to sharing precise location for location-aware answers; leave it off to withhold precise location.
limits: An older settings page calls it 'Location' and says network location is used when unset; the privacy notice says general location comes from IP address.

where: Plugins → Installed (or Customize → Connectors where Plugins has not rolled out)
what_it_does: Disconnecting removes a connector's access everywhere it is used; uninstalling a plugin removes its skills but leaves its connectors connected.
plans: Plugins that include skills need a plan that includes Computer
limits: Recent change: connectors and skills are now managed on the Plugins page, rolling out gradually (older UI: Customize → Connectors). Enterprise members only get connectors enabled for their role.

control: Allow members to add custom connectors
where: Enterprise settings → Connectors → Connector permissions
what_it_does: Lets admins decide whether non-admin members can add their own remote custom (MCP) connectors.
limits: Admins should review and remove risky member-added connectors; only admins can share connectors organization-wide.

control: No UI label: confirmation prompt for local MCP tool calls
where: Perplexity Mac app with local MCP connectors (Plugins → Add custom)
what_it_does: When a request runs a local MCP server tool, the app asks you to confirm first.
limits: Described only for local MCP on macOS; no setting to change it is documented. The MCP must also be toggled on under Sources.

where: Organization Settings → Data and privacy → Data Retention
what_it_does: Admins set how long sessions are kept; sessions outside the window become inaccessible and are deleted.
plans: Enterprise orgs with 50 seats or more, or at least one Enterprise Max user
limits: Counted from last activity; out-of-window sessions are deleted within 7 days and cannot be recovered. Session file attachments are deleted after seven days anyway.

where: Organization Settings → Data and privacy → Data Retention
what_it_does: Admin setting listed under Data Retention that enforces Incognito Mode across the organization.
limits: The page lists the setting but does not explain its exact effect or which Enterprise tiers get it.

control: Reference search library / Reference saved memories (admin)
where: Admin dashboard → Permissions
what_it_does: Admins can turn off search-history referencing or saved memories for everyone; disabling saved memories deletes existing ones.
limits: If admins leave them on, members can still switch them off. Enterprise memory content is never used for training.

where: Organization Settings → Data and privacy → Audit Log Settings
what_it_does: Admins stream a real-time record of queries, agent steps (including Comet agent actions), answers and admin changes to their own webhook.
plans: Enterprise orgs with 50 seats or more, or at least one Enterprise Max user
limits: An oversight record for admins, not a user privacy control; entries include user email and IP address.

where: Computer → Automations dashboard (perplexity.ai/computer/automations) → task row's Actions menu, or the task's detail page
what_it_does: Pause or delete recurring tasks that Computer runs for you in the background in the cloud.
limits: Creating a task requires confirming a proposed schedule. Each run uses credits.

where: Perplexity desktop app → model selector (Hybrid) or Settings → Local Inference
what_it_does: Runs tasks with an on-device model. On Mac (Hybrid), a privacy gate can mask sensitive details, keep the step local, refuse, or ask consent before protected file data reaches the cloud; on Windows and Linux the app asks permission before sending anything to the cloud.
plans: Pro, Max and Enterprise (local models); supported hardware only
limits: For managed accounts, admins decide whether local inference is allowed (Windows, Linux) or set rules for what stays on device (Mac).

where: Android Settings → Apps → Default Apps → Digital assist app
what_it_does: Chooses which app acts as the phone's assistant; picking another app keeps Perplexity from acting as the device assistant.
limits: Android system setting described by Perplexity for setup; turning it away from Perplexity is implied, not spelled out.

control: No UI label: file deletion request form
where: Security and Privacy with File Uploads help article (form link)
what_it_does: Request immediate deletion of uploaded files or images from a session, project or organization.
limits: Deletion. Files are otherwise retained 30 days (7 days for Enterprise Pro); project and repository files follow their own retention.

where: Plugins → Installed, or the Health hub
what_it_does: Disconnect wearables, medical records and Apple Health; Apple Health only shares the data types you select on its permissions screen.
plans: Pro and Max subscribers in the US (phased rollout; iOS and web); Apple Health needs iOS and age 18+
limits: Medical records run through b.well and wearables through Terra. Health memories are deleted separately in Personalization.

where: Settings → Privacy and security → Comet Assistant
what_it_does: Allows or prohibits the Assistant from accessing browser history, navigating the web and interacting with sites; access can be paused anytime.
limits: Enterprise telemetry mentions a 'Personal Search' setting for history access; its user-facing label is not documented.

where: Settings → Privacy and security
what_it_does: Adds sites, such as your bank, that Comet must not use for AI actions, context or suggestions.

control: No UI label: integration approval prompt (e.g., Gmail)
where: Prompt shown when Comet needs another service
what_it_does: Comet asks for your approval before it uses another service such as Gmail.
limits: Described as behavior, not a setting. The page also says Comet never has access to passwords or payment data.

control: Allow this time only / Always allow / Don't allow
where: Prompt when an advanced agent or automation runs for the first time
what_it_does: Asks before an agent runs; you can allow it once, allow it always, or refuse.
limits: 'Always allow' suppresses future prompts; no way to reset that choice is documented.

where: Perplexity Library
what_it_does: Context from page content, history items or open tabs is stored up to 30 days, then auto-deleted; you can delete the thread sooner or remove the timer.
limits: The retention period is fixed, not user-adjustable; removing the timer keeps the thread.

control: Enable Comet to Control the Browser / Enable "Always Allow" option
where: Organization settings → Comet Setup → Assistant Permissions
what_it_does: Admins can stop Comet from acting for members, or remove the option to let it act without confirming each action.
limits: Domain-specific settings override these global settings.

control: Domain-Specific Assistant Permissions (Browser Control / Read Only / No Access)
where: Organization settings → Comet Setup
what_it_does: Admins set, per domain, whether Comet can act, only read, or have no access.
limits: Overrides global settings: a domain set to Browser Control stays usable even if the Assistant is disabled.

control: Enable Comet Access (Enable for specific members)
where: Organization Settings → Comet setup
what_it_does: Admins can enable Comet only for chosen members and disable it for everyone else.

control: IncognitoModeAvailability / GenAILocalFoundationalModelSettings / BuiltInAIAPIsEnabled (examples of MDM browser policies)
where: MDM profiles (replace com.google.Chrome with ai.perplexity.comet)
what_it_does: Admins apply Chromium policies, for example forcing or disabling Incognito, stopping local AI model downloads, or blocking built-in AI web APIs.
default: Unset (default): Incognito allowed, local GenAI model downloaded and used automatically, built-in AI APIs enabled
limits: The page says Comet supports 500+ Chromium policies, but its table lists 398. Descriptions are Chrome's text and some mention Google services, so effects in Comet may differ.

where: Comet Incognito window
what_it_does: After closing, Comet keeps no history, cookies, site data, form fills or passwords from the session.
limits: AI queries and needed context still go to Perplexity's servers; security logs remain; websites, employers and ISPs can still see activity.

where: Settings → Privacy and security → Delete browsing data
what_it_does: Deletes locally stored browsing data by time range and data type.
limits: Deletion. Clears local data only, not your Perplexity account or synced settings; downloaded files and saved passwords stay.

where: Settings → Privacy and security → Help improve Comet
what_it_does: Turns off sending crash logs and performance data used to improve stability.
limits: The page says reports are stripped of identifiers before leaving the device.

where: Settings → Privacy and security → Third-party cookies
what_it_does: Choose Allow, Block, Block only in incognito, or Block cookies after closing sites.
limits: Allowed by default for compatibility. Blocking may break social logins, embedded widgets and some payment flows.

where: Settings → Privacy → Blocking
what_it_does: Blocks intrusive ads and tracking scripts using open-source filter lists; can be switched off or given site exceptions.
limits: Site exceptions let chosen sites keep showing ads.

where: Settings → Privacy and security → Site settings
what_it_does: Set camera, microphone, location, notifications, clipboard and other site permissions to Allow, Block or Ask every time.

control: Sync (Create Sync / Join Sync, per-item toggles)
where: Settings → Sync
what_it_does: You create or join an encrypted sync chain; each data type, such as history or passwords, can be switched off and devices removed.
limits: Turning an item off stops new syncing but keeps local data. The privacy notice says Comet use with a synced account may record browsing history.

where: Settings (Inline Assistant option), or popup ⋯ menu → disable
what_it_does: Turns off the floating AI button that appears whenever you select text on a page or in a text field.
plans: not stated (page says it is currently available in the Comet browser extension; mobile support may vary)
limits: May not appear in Incognito, on blocked websites, or on some sites like Google Docs. Selections are processed by Perplexity under regular query policies.

control: Reference search library / Reference saved memories / Edit your saved memories
where: New Tab Page → Account → Preferences → Memory (Perplexity account settings)
what_it_does: Stops Comet from using past searches or saved memories, and lets you review or delete stored memories.
limits: Shared with Perplexity account memory; labels differ from 'Use search history' and 'Notes'. Agent actions are not stored in memory.

where: Settings → Search engine
what_it_does: Switching the default away from Perplexity limits or disables many of Comet's AI features.
default: Perplexity AI (implied: page says to keep Perplexity AI as your default and how to select it again)
limits: The page presents this as something to avoid, not as a privacy control.

where: Comet for Android, during task automation
what_it_does: Shows the step-by-step actions Comet took; blue screen edges show when AI is in control.
limits: Review only; no way to limit or delete action records is described. Tasks run only while the app is open.

control: Allow your interactions to be used to train our models
where: Admin panel (admin.mistral.ai) → Manage → Vibe → Privacy
what_it_does: Turn off to stop Mistral using your Vibe inputs and outputs, including uploaded documents, to train its models.
plans: Vibe: not opted out by default; Vibe (Teams): admins can disable for the organization; Vibe (Enterprise): opted out by default, opt-in set by admin
limits: Separate from the Studio/API toggle (MIS-03); opting out of one does not opt out of the other.

where: Mobile app Settings → Account → Data & Account Controls
what_it_does: Uncheck to opt out of Mistral's training program from the iOS or Android app.

where: Admin panel → Privacy (Mistral Studio and API)
what_it_does: Turn off to stop API calls and related data being used to improve Mistral's services.
limits: Opting out here does not opt you out of Vibe training, and the reverse is also true.

where: Rating buttons on Vibe responses
what_it_does: Giving feedback lets Mistral use your rating plus the related input and output to improve its models, on any plan.
limits: The help article advises not sending feedback if you do not want it used.

where: Request via Help Center or support; shown in Admin panel Privacy settings once approved
what_it_does: For approved pay-as-you-go customers, inputs and outputs of stateless API calls are not retained after the response is returned.
limits: Not available for Vibe Work or Chat, agents, libraries, conversations, batch files or the Files API. Approval is at Mistral's discretion.

where: User: organization name → Privacy → Personalization → Knowledge, or the Knowledge page. Admin: admin.mistral.ai/vibe/preferences → Tools → Knowledge
what_it_does: Turns off Knowledge Base, which saves and recalls details from your chats in the background. Admins can disable it for all members.
limits: Turning it off keeps stored entries; use 'Delete all knowledge' to remove them. Single entries are deleted by asking Vibe.

where: Organization name → Privacy (shown when Knowledge is on); admins: admin.mistral.ai/vibe/privacy or workspace Chat Settings
what_it_does: When off, Knowledge Base will not save sensitive details such as health, religion or sexual orientation, even if you ask.
limits: Turning it off does not delete sensitive entries already saved. Admins can lock it off. Credentials and government IDs are never saved.

where: Memories tab (Intelligence menu) → ⋯ → Memories in Vibe
what_it_does: Turns legacy Chat Memories on or off; memories can be edited, deleted, or cleared with 'Clear all Memories'.
plans: Legacy Chat; Enterprise may keep it during a six-month migration window
limits: Turning it off does not delete stored memories, which are kept for the length of the subscription. Being replaced by Knowledge Base.

where: Vibe Work (location in the app not documented)
what_it_does: Conversations excluded from your history, search, memory and model training.
limits: How to start it is not documented. The Vibe overview page (https://docs.mistral.ai/vibe) says Mistral logs only that a Temporary Chat happened, not its content, and that data may be kept where the law requires; the September 22, 2026 release notes say it is kept out of history and Knowledge Base.

where: ⋮ next to the conversation title → Delete → confirm
what_it_does: Deletes a whole conversation; you cannot get it back afterwards.
limits: Deletion, not an opt-out. Backend copies may be kept for policy enforcement or legal reasons; Team and Enterprise orgs may apply their own rules.

where: Admin panel account page → Danger Zone → Delete account
what_it_does: Permanently deletes your Vibe account after you retype your email address.
limits: Deletion; accounts cannot be recovered. Paid users must settle outstanding fees first.

where: admin.mistral.ai/account/export
what_it_does: Downloads all your Vibe data as stored at the time of the request.
limits: Access right, not an opt-out.

where: Cookie banner on first visit; 'Privacy Choices' link in the site footer
what_it_does: Accept or refuse analytics cookies (Google Analytics, PostHog) and partner marketing cookies (X, Meta) used to show ads on other sites.
limits: Strictly necessary cookies cannot be turned off in the banner. Browser settings are an alternative.

control: No UI label: IP-based location opt-out
where: User preferences in your Mistral AI Account (path not given)
what_it_does: Opts out of Mistral using part of your IP address to tailor outputs to where you are.
limits: Stated only in the privacy policy; no matching setting was found in the help center or docs.

where: Connectors page in the sidebar
what_it_does: Connect tools such as Gmail or Notion through OAuth only when you choose; disconnecting revokes access immediately.
limits: Admins can disable connectors org-wide. Connector data is never used for training. MCP connectors require an administrator.

where: In-chat prompt before external actions (Vibe Work)
what_it_does: Work stops for approval before anything that creates, modifies, sends, posts or deletes in a connected tool.
limits: 'Always allow' pre-authorizes that function for the session. Stopping a running action may not undo it.

where: Connectors → My Connectors → [connector] → Functions
what_it_does: Choose which connector functions may run without asking; choices are per user.
limits: Docs recommend keeping interactive (write) functions on manual approval.

where: Admin Panel → Administration → Connectors → [connector] → Permissions
what_it_does: Admins allow all tools, allow only selected tools, or block a connector for users in a Workspace.
limits: Applies to Vibe and Studio.

control: Work mode / Agents / Canvas / Code Interpreter / Deep Research / Image Generation / Memories / Thinking Mode / Web Search
where: Admin Panel → Administration → Workspaces → Workspace settings
what_it_does: Admins remove chosen Vibe capabilities for every member of a Workspace.
limits: Disabling removes the feature for all Workspace members.

where: Admin Panel → Administration → Workspaces → Workspace settings
what_it_does: Automatically deletes Workspace chats and their artifacts after 30, 90, 180 or 365 days, or never.
limits: Can only be stricter than the organization setting in Admin Panel → Vibe → Privacy. No user-level retention choice was found.

where: Admin Panel → Administration → Workspaces → Workspace settings
what_it_does: Admin switch that collects traces, token usage and error metrics from Workspace conversations into Studio Observability.

where: Admin company-wide controls
what_it_does: Admins can turn off Flash Answers, an optional fast-response feature, for the whole organization.

where: Sidebar → Scheduled
what_it_does: Pause or delete prompts that Work runs automatically on a schedule.
plans: Vibe Work (number of tasks depends on plan)
limits: Public Preview. Sensitive actions need 'Always allow' to run unattended; suggested schedules may appear based on recent chats and tools.

control: default / plan / accept-edits / smart-approve / auto-approve (Vibe Code agents)
where: Vibe Code CLI or VS Code (Shift+Tab, --agent, default_agent in config.toml)
what_it_does: Sets how Vibe Code asks before running tools, from asking every time, to read-only, to approving everything automatically.
limits: In programmatic mode without --agent, Vibe falls back to auto-approve. Smart approve is a classifier, not a sandbox.

where: Help Center GDPR article; 'Privacy Requests' form in the privacy policy
what_it_does: Request access, rectification, restriction, portability or objection to processing beyond the self-serve tools.
limits: Training objection is handled by the account toggle; other objections go through email unsubscribe links or the form.

where: Settings → Apple Intelligence & Siri
what_it_does: Master switch for Apple Intelligence in iOS 26. The guide shows how to turn it on, and its 'Turn off Apple Intelligence' section says to tap the same button next to Apple Intelligence in Settings → Apple Intelligence & Siri.
limits: The option shown depends on iOS version and earlier setup. Newer guides list per-feature switches instead (APL-02).

control: Summarize Messages / Summarize Message Previews / Summarize Notifications / Prioritize Notifications / Personalize Smart Replies / Suggestions in Voicemail / Show When Calling / Get Writing Prompts
where: Settings → Apps → [Messages, Mail, Phone, Journal], or Settings → Notifications
what_it_does: Turn off single AI features: message and notification summaries, notification priority, smart replies, voicemail suggestions, call context cards and journal prompts.
limits: This guide gives no single master switch; Siri AI is turned off separately (APL-03). Screen Time can also restrict features.

control: Try Siri AI (Beta) / Turn Off Siri / Use Siri Classic
where: Settings → Siri
what_it_does: Siri AI must be chosen with 'Try Siri AI (Beta)'; you can turn Siri off or go back to the classic Siri.
limits: Siri AI will not initially be offered on iOS in the EU; daily usage limits apply to server-based features.

control: Talk to Siri (Off) / Press Side Button for Siri / Enable Dictation
where: Settings → Siri; Settings → General → Keyboard
what_it_does: Stops Siri from listening or responding and turns off Dictation; turning off both deletes Siri and Dictation transcripts kept on the device.
limits: Only on-device transcripts are deleted this way; Apple separately keeps request history for up to two years.

control: Don't Allow Siri / Siri (Classic Version) / Siri AI (Beta) / Allow / Block (per Siri AI capability)
where: Settings → Screen Time → Content & Privacy Restrictions → Siri
what_it_does: Block Siri, allow only classic Siri, or block Siri AI capabilities such as Image Creation, Sensitive Topics or Explicit Language.
limits: Options shown vary by Siri version; can also be used as a parental control.

control: Writing Tools / Image Creation / Intelligence Extensions (Allow / Don't Allow)
where: Settings → Screen Time → Content & Privacy Restrictions → Intelligence & Siri
what_it_does: Block Writing Tools, image creation features and third-party AI extensions such as ChatGPT.
limits: Documented in the iOS 26 guide; newer Siri AI restrictions are in APL-05.

where: Settings → Apple Intelligence & Siri → ChatGPT (per legal page)
what_it_does: Turns the ChatGPT extension on or off for Siri, Writing Tools and visual intelligence; nothing is sent to ChatGPT unless it is enabled.
limits: Signed out, OpenAI must not store or train on requests; signed in, OpenAI's policies apply and it may train. Newer guide path: Settings → Siri → ChatGPT.

control: Confirm Requests (legal page: Confirm ChatGPT Requests)
where: Settings → Siri → Extensions → ChatGPT
what_it_does: When on, Siri asks before sending your request to ChatGPT; turning it off lets Siri send requests automatically.
limits: Not available with Siri AI, where you must ask ChatGPT explicitly before a prompt, photos or files are sent.

where: Settings → Siri → ChatGPT (after turning off Use ChatGPT)
what_it_does: Stops Siri from suggesting ChatGPT when you make a request.
limits: Not available with Siri AI.

control: Improve Siri & Apple Intelligence / Improve Siri & Dictation
where: Settings → Privacy & Security → Analytics & Improvements (also on Mac, Watch, HomePod, Apple TV, Vision Pro)
what_it_does: Opt-in that lets Apple store and review samples of Siri, Dictation and Translate audio and transcripts; the Siri AI version also allows training foundation models.
plans: Improve Siri & Apple Intelligence for Siri AI users; Improve Siri & Dictation for others
limits: You are asked at device setup or first Siri use. On an Apple Watch set up for a family member it is off and cannot be changed.

where: Settings → Privacy & Security → Analytics & Improvements
what_it_does: If on with Siri AI, Apple may store all Siri and Dictation interactions, including Siri app conversations, to improve Siri and train Apple foundation models.
limits: Kept up to two years; reviewed samples may be kept longer. Not tied to your Apple Account, but Apple may link rotating IDs within a conversation.

where: Settings → Privacy & Security → Analytics & Improvements
what_it_does: Opt-in; if on, Apple may use privacy-preserving techniques on aggregated trends, including content Apple Intelligence processes, to improve Apple Intelligence.
limits: Apple says it does not collect individual user data or content this way.

control: Apple Intelligence Report (legal page: Apple Intelligence & PCC Report)
where: Settings → Privacy & Security → Apple Intelligence Report
what_it_does: Keeps an exportable log of requests your iPhone sent to Private Cloud Compute for a chosen window; choose Off to disable it.
default: last 15 minutes (the guide marks this as the default; Apple's legal page says you turn reporting on)
limits: Guide offers last 15 minutes (marked default) or last 7 days; Apple's legal page says you turn reporting on. Report may be empty after changing duration.

control: Learn from this App / Learn From App Clips
where: Settings → Siri → App Access → [app]; Settings → Siri → App Clips
what_it_does: Stops Siri from learning how you use an app or App Clips to make suggestions.
limits: Guide says suggestions are on by default; a per-app default is not stated separately. The legal page path is Settings → Siri → Apps.

control: Suggest Apps Before Searching / Allow Notifications / Show in App Library / Show When Sharing / Show Listening Suggestions
where: Settings → Siri → Suggestions
what_it_does: Limits where proactive Siri suggestions appear: search, notifications, App Library, the share sheet and listening suggestions.

control: Highlight to Search / Automatic Visual Look Up
where: Settings → Siri
what_it_does: Controls automatic web searches when you highlight in Siri camera mode or screenshots, and automatic identification of objects in screenshots.
plans: Highlight to Search: Siri AI only
limits: Visual Intelligence can send highlighted objects to third parties for results.

where: Settings → Siri → Responses
what_it_does: Leave it off to keep Siri asking you to confirm before it sends a message.
limits: Options vary by Siri version. No general approval setting for other Siri AI app actions was found.

where: Settings → Siri → Apps → [app name]
what_it_does: Controls which third-party apps can work with Siri requests and send contextual data to Apple.
limits: When Siri acts in a third-party app, that app's terms and privacy policy apply.

where: Settings → Privacy & Security → Location Services → Siri; System Services → Suggestions & Search
what_it_does: Stops sending your device location with Siri requests and for location-based Siri Suggestions.
limits: Apple may still estimate location from your IP address.

where: Settings → [your name] → iCloud → Saved to iCloud → See All → Siri
what_it_does: Stops Siri settings and personalization from syncing across your devices through iCloud.
limits: The effect on Siri app conversation sync is not stated.

where: Settings → Privacy & Security → Speech Recognition
what_it_does: Chooses which apps may use Siri for transcription, which can send audio to Apple.

where: Settings → Siri → Siri & Dictation History
what_it_does: Deletes the Siri and Dictation transcripts stored on your device.
limits: Deletion, not an opt-out. Apple keeps request history on a rotating random ID for up to two years and may review a subset; reviewed items can be kept longer.

where: System Settings → Apple Intelligence & Siri (or Siri)
what_it_does: Deletes Siri and Dictation request history (audio and transcripts) tied to a random identifier and less than six months old.
limits: Deletion. Needs an internet connection and does not change your audio-sharing choice.

where: Settings → Siri → Keep Conversations
what_it_does: Sets how long the Siri app keeps conversations; under shorter options, older ones are permanently deleted.
limits: The guide names 30 days and 1 year as options; the full list and default are not given. Conversations sync across devices.

where: Siri app → touch and hold a conversation → Delete (or Select for several)
what_it_does: Deletes one or several Siri app conversations.
limits: Deletion, not an opt-out.

where: Home app → More → Home Settings → Apple Intelligence
what_it_does: Turns off Apple Intelligence alert summaries in the Home app, which replace multiple alerts with one summary.
plans: Homeowners and admins of the home
limits: Turning off Apple Intelligence in Settings also turns this off. Homeowners can change or turn off Apple Intelligence Reports.

where: Home app → More → Home Settings → Apple Intelligence (or per camera)
what_it_does: Controls AI captions describing activity on HomeKit Secure Video cameras.
plans: Eligible iCloud+ users; homeowners and admins
limits: When on, footage with detected activity is sent to Private Cloud Compute for captions; cameras without it analyze only on device.

where: Settings → Privacy & Security → Apple Advertising
what_it_does: Opts your Apple Account out of interest-based ads from Apple's ad platform in the App Store, Apple News, Stocks and the Apple TV app, on any device you use.
limits: Contextual ads still appear. Covers Apple's ad platform generally, not Apple Intelligence specifically.

control: Allow Apps to Request to Track
where: Device privacy settings (path not given in the policy)
what_it_does: When off, third-party apps cannot ask to use the advertising identifier to track you across other companies' apps and websites.
limits: Device-wide; not specific to Apple Intelligence.

where: Settings → Search
what_it_does: Stops Apple from storing your search queries to improve Search.
limits: Searches made through Siri are still kept if Improve Siri & Dictation is on.

control: Report a Concern (separate choice to share with OpenAI or Google)
where: Report a Concern flow
what_it_does: Reports go to Apple and may be used to train its models; sharing a report with OpenAI or Google is a separate choice.
limits: Reports may be stored in a way linked to you for up to one year or as required by law. The page's opening line says the report will be linked to your Apple Account, while its details say only reports on certain Apple Beta Software Program features are linked and other reports use a random ID.

where: privacy.apple.com (sign in required)
what_it_does: Request access, correction, transfer, restriction or deletion of personal data Apple holds.
limits: Apple may refuse some requests, such as deleting records it must keep by law.

where: Settings > Galaxy AI (some models: Settings > Advanced features > Advanced intelligence)
what_it_does: Master switch that turns off cloud-based processing for Galaxy AI features, so only on-device processing is used.
limits: Samsung says settings that block server access limit the functionality of some AI features (Samsung US Newsroom, May 14, 2024, which is also the source of the alternate menu path).

control: Galaxy AI feature switches (example given: Call assist)
where: Settings > Galaxy AI (or Advanced features > Galaxy AI / Awesome Intelligence) > feature sub-menu
what_it_does: Turn off individual Galaxy AI features one at a time. Samsung advises restarting the device afterward.
limits: Page says signing in with a Samsung account automatically activates all AI features. Switch labels for each feature (Interpreter, Note assist, etc.) are not listed.

where: Settings inside Phone, Samsung Notes, Camera, Gallery, Samsung Messages, Samsung Health, SmartThings
what_it_does: Turn off specific AI features from inside each Samsung app's own settings.
limits: Page does not list which features each app exposes.

where: Support article, section 'Disable Galaxy AI features'
what_it_does: Samsung says some AI features may be built into the system and cannot be turned off.
limits: The affected features are not named.

control: Consent before first cloud-processed Galaxy AI use
where: Samsung account U.S. Privacy Notice > Information We Collect While Using Specific Services > Galaxy AI
what_it_does: Before first use of a Galaxy AI feature that sends data off the device, Samsung informs the user and asks for consent. Some apps offer an on-device processing option.
limits: Off-device inputs listed for Writing, Note, Transcript, Browsing and Photo assist and Creative studio. Minors notice says consent is sought 'where required by applicable law'.

control: No long-term storage or AI training on Galaxy AI personal data
where: Samsung Global Newsroom, 'Your Privacy, Secured: How Galaxy AI Empowers You...' (Advanced Settings for Advanced AI)
what_it_does: Samsung says personal data used by Galaxy AI is not stored long-term or used for AI training, whether processed on device or in the cloud, under any setting.
limits: Newsroom statement, not policy text. 'Long-term' is not defined. The US privacy policy separately allows AI training on US residents' personal information (SAM-08).

control: Samsung does not save AI input or output data
where: Samsung US Newsroom, 'The Knox Journals: Stay in Control of Your Security' (Advanced Intelligence settings footnotes)
what_it_does: Samsung states that, whether or not server access is allowed, it does not save user input or output data from AI features.
limits: 2024 newsroom footnote. Not found in the July 2026 privacy notices reviewed.

control: Use of US residents' personal information to train AI models
where: Samsung Privacy Policy > US Supplement > Additional Uses of Your Information
what_it_does: Samsung may use personal information about US residents to develop and train its AI algorithms and models.
limits: No specific opt-out is named. Data categories and consent basis are not stated. Broader than, and in tension with, SAM-06.

control: On-device Live Translate, Interpreter and Audio Eraser
where: Samsung Global Newsroom, 'Your Privacy, Secured: How Galaxy AI Empowers You...'
what_it_does: Samsung says Live Translate, Interpreter and Audio Eraser keep inputs on the phone rather than sending them to the cloud.
limits: Samsung UAE FAQ (2024-01-15) also says Live Translate uses on-device AI only. Language packs may need download.

where: Settings > Galaxy AI > Now nudge > Personal data intelligence (also Settings > Security and privacy > More privacy settings > Personal data intelligence)
what_it_does: Turns the on-device Personal Data Engine on or off. It learns from phone use to power suggestions in Samsung and third-party apps.
plans: Galaxy phones with One UI 8.5 or later, including the Galaxy S26 series and newer (Now nudge path)
limits: Samsung says analyzed data is deleted when this menu is turned off (samsung.com/us/galaxy-ai footnote 16). Second path and app picker are from a Samsung India help page.

control: Consent to share Personal data intelligence data with Samsung or partners
where: Settings > Galaxy AI > Now nudge > Personal data intelligence (note on page)
what_it_does: Data for this feature is processed on the phone unless the user consents to share it with Samsung or its partners for better recommendations.
plans: Galaxy devices with One UI 8.5 or later
limits: Exact consent label and partner list are not given.

where: Galaxy S26 launch release, Now Brief footnote
what_it_does: Now Brief recalls data from Gmail only if the user consents to Personal Data Intelligence's Gmail read permission.
limits: Settings path not given. Newsroom footnote only.

where: Settings > Galaxy AI > Now nudge > Personal data intelligence > Manage personal data
what_it_does: Manage stored personal details (name, phone, email, passport, pets, interests) that Now nudge can suggest when filling in forms.
plans: Galaxy devices with One UI 8.5 or later
limits: Page does not say whether removing an entry deletes it everywhere.

control: Personal Data Engine with Knox Enhanced Encrypted Protection (KEEP) and Knox Vault
where: Samsung Global Newsroom, One UI 8 security release
what_it_does: Personal insights used by the Personal Data Engine stay on the device in encrypted per-app storage (KEEP) backed by Knox Vault hardware.
limits: Engine runs only when Personal data intelligence is on.

where: Settings > Galaxy AI > Now nudge
what_it_does: Switch for proactive suggestions based on on-screen content, such as adding events, sharing photos, or recalling past chats and screenshots.
plans: One UI 8.5 or later (Galaxy S26 series and newer)
limits: Needs Auto suggestion on. Location suggestions need Location permission. Samsung account login required.

control: Content to include; Show Now brief while phone is locked
where: Settings > Galaxy AI > Now brief
what_it_does: Choose which content categories appear in the daily Now brief and whether it shows on the lock screen.
limits: Samsung account notice says some Now brief content is processed off the device, including by third parties.

control: Now bar categories; Media player; Current mode
where: Settings > Lock screen and AOD (or Lock screen) > Now bar > View more
what_it_does: Switches that pick which categories and live items appear in the Now bar on the lock screen.
limits: Categories vary by model and software version.

where: Call assist (exact menu path not given)
what_it_does: AI answers unknown calls and asks who is calling and why. Samsung says the feature must be turned on manually.
plans: Galaxy AI devices; varies by country and language
limits: US Galaxy AI page footnote 8. S26 release says manual activation only 'in select regions'. Feature description from Samsung Services Terms.

where: Settings > Security and privacy > AI assistant activity
what_it_does: Shows a timestamped log (last 24 hours or 7 days) of agentic tasks an AI assistant, such as Gemini, carried out in Samsung apps.
limits: Samsung India help page. View only; no switch to stop or delete logs is described. Covers only eligible assistant activity.

where: Bixby settings > Privacy settings
what_it_does: Opt in to keep Bixby audio for troubleshooting and review, including human review. A small share of pooled recordings is reviewed to improve and train Bixby.
limits: Audio kept linked to an identifier for 1 month, then de-identified and kept 1 year total. Consent applies to every device on the same Samsung account.

control: Audio deleted after command without review opt-in
where: Bixby U.S. Privacy Notice > Audio Recording Review
what_it_does: If the user does not opt in to review, Bixby audio recordings are deleted once the requested command has been provided.
limits: Covers audio only. Other Bixby data follows the general retention rule (SAM-22).

control: Bixby data deleted or anonymized within 45 days
where: Bixby U.S. Privacy Notice > How Long We Keep Your Information
what_it_does: Once Bixby data is no longer needed, Samsung deletes or anonymizes it, including backups, within 45 days, unless law or consent requires otherwise.
limits: How long data is 'needed' is not defined. No user-set retention period.

where: Bixby U.S. Privacy Notice > Information We Obtain
what_it_does: Bixby collects precise location only with separate consent, and the device notifies the user when Bixby tries to access location.
limits: Declining may limit some features. Samsung Privacy Policy states the same separate-consent rule for other services.

control: Location consent for Bixby web answers
where: 'Samsung Introduces the New Bixby in One UI 8.5' release, footnote 2
what_it_does: Bixby asks for location consent when a web answer depends on it. Samsung says the location is used only for that answer and deleted right after.
plans: One UI 8.5, select markets including the US
limits: Newsroom footnote. Exact prompt label not shown.

control: Bixby access to app content used by commands
where: Bixby U.S. Privacy Notice > Information We Obtain; Information Sharing
what_it_does: Bixby may obtain content from Samsung and third-party apps a command touches, including social media, email and messaging apps, and may share data with content providers.
limits: Scope depends on the command. No per-app limit for Bixby is described.

where: Settings > Advanced features > Bixby > Voice registration
what_it_does: Set or skip a wake phrase ('Hi, Bixby' or 'Bixby'), its sensitivity, waking while media plays, and voice-matching options.
plans: Galaxy phones and tablets with Bixby
limits: Can be set during Bixby setup or later. Multi device wake-up runs automatically on Bixby 2.0+ with no setting.

where: Bixby settings
what_it_does: Switch that lets Bixby take commands without the wake phrase at certain moments, such as when an alarm rings or a call comes in.
plans: Galaxy phones and tablets with Bixby

where: Settings > Advanced features > Bixby > Voice registration
what_it_does: Option listed among voice wake-up settings to delete voice recordings.
plans: Galaxy phones and tablets with Bixby
limits: Page does not say which recordings are deleted or whether server copies are included. Deletion, not opt-out.

control: Bixby wake-up voiceprint stays on device
where: Samsung Privacy Policy > US Supplement > Biometric Data Stored on Your Device Not Accessible by Samsung
what_it_does: Voiceprint data for a custom Bixby wake-up command stays on the device; Samsung does not receive, access or share it. Users delete it in settings.
limits: Samsung says it cannot delete this data for users.

where: Settings > Advanced features > Bixby > Leave Bixby
what_it_does: Removes the Bixby account and data from the phone and sends a deletion request. Bixby must be set up again to use it.
limits: Requires Samsung account sign-in. Removing the Samsung account from the phone also resets Bixby data. Deletion, not opt-out.

where: Settings > Apps > Bixby > Storage > Clear cache / Clear data; then Disable
what_it_does: Resets all Bixby data on the device and stops Bixby from launching from the Side or Bixby button.
limits: Bixby cannot be uninstalled. Effect on server-side data is not stated.

control: Side button > Long press; Digital assistant app
where: Settings > Advanced features > Side button > Long press; Settings > Apps > Choose default apps > Digital assistant app
what_it_does: Assign the side button long press to the Power off menu instead of an assistant, or pick which assistant app (Bixby or Google) is the default.
limits: Digital assistant app steps are from ANS10010644. Default button assignment is not stated on these pages.

where: Bixby general questions > 'Does Bixby support Incognito mode?'
what_it_does: Bixby Voice requires a Samsung account sign-in, and Samsung says it does not offer an Incognito mode.
limits: No Samsung-documented setting to stop saving Bixby conversations was found.

where: Phone: Settings > Privacy > Customization Service (Samsung account settings)
what_it_does: Turns off Samsung's profiling service that analyzes device, app, browsing, calendar and location data to tailor content and recommendations, and ads with separate consent.
plans: Samsung account holders (phones, tablets, Smart TVs)
limits: Notice frames it as consent that can be withdrawn. Turning it off does not delete data already collected. Menu path may change by model.

control: Customization Service data categories and supported services
where: Customization Service settings in Samsung account
what_it_does: Choose which data types (for example call and message history, browsing, location) the service may collect and analyze, and which Samsung services it supports.
limits: Location tracking within the service is opt-in. Third-party app usage data is used only if the user connects that app.

where: Samsung account > Data management
what_it_does: Request deletion of specific categories of data the Customization Service collected, without deleting the Samsung account.
limits: Deletion, not opt-out. May take about 30 days. All such data is deleted when the Samsung account is deleted.

control: Improve personalized ads with Samsung account data
where: Samsung account Settings > Security and Privacy
what_it_does: Allows ads tailored with Samsung account data plus Customization Service data such as app use, search terms and browsing history.
limits: Notice calls it a separate consent. With all optional ad features off, Samsung says you may still see generic Samsung ads that are not tailored to you (Samsung account U.S. Privacy Notice).

control: Improve personalized ads with precise location data
where: Samsung account Settings > Security and Privacy (path per Samsung account U.S. Privacy Notice)
what_it_does: Allows ads tailored to the device's precise location.
limits: Consent wording from the Customization Service notice; menu path from the July 27, 2026 account notice.

where: Samsung account Settings > Security and Privacy
what_it_does: Turns on Samsung marketing by email, notifications and online platforms, tailored with Samsung account and device information.
limits: With all optional ad features off, Samsung says ads may still appear but are generic.

where: Settings > Security and privacy > More privacy settings
what_it_does: Switch that allows Samsung to collect diagnostic data from the device to improve its services.
