limits: Data types are not listed. Google's separate 'Usage & diagnostics' setting sits in the same menu.

where: Samsung Keyboard > Predictive text settings
what_it_does: When on, Samsung collects typed words and may sync them through the Samsung account. Learned data can be cleared in Predictive text settings.
limits: Covers predictive text only, not Writing assist in the same keyboard.

where: Samsung Internet browser
what_it_does: Search history from Secret mode is not collected by the Customization Service, and Browsing assist's personalized answers are unavailable in Secret Mode.
limits: Second point is from Samsung Services Terms (posted July 27, 2026). Secret mode is a browser mode, not a Galaxy AI setting.

control: Do Not Sell or Share (Opt out of Targeted Ads)
where: US Privacy Rights Portal (samsung.com/us/privacy/rights, form served from privacypost.sea.samsung.com) or 1-800-SAMSUNG
what_it_does: Request that Samsung stop selling personal information, sharing it for cross-context ads, and using it for targeted ads.
limits: First-party personalized ads may continue unless device or account settings are changed; contextual ads continue. Requests are tied to identifiers (ad ID, PSID, cookie, email, phone).

where: Samsung Privacy Policy > US Supplement > How to Submit a Privacy Request
what_it_does: Samsung treats a browser opt-out preference signal as an opt-out of targeted advertising on Samsung.com, set per browser and device, processed automatically.
limits: Only Samsung.com is named; nothing for devices, Galaxy AI, Bixby or apps. Samsung does not respond to browser signals that fail state law requirements, which it says may include older Do Not Track signals. Not tested in this audit.

control: Do Not Sell Or Share My Personal Information (footer link); Cookie Preference Settings
where: Samsung.com US page footer and cookie banner
what_it_does: Footer link calls Samsung.com's TrustArc consent tool (per page code). The cookie banner says continued browsing counts as consent to cookies.
limits: Tool options were not viewed because the banner was not dismissed. California statement (Dec 31, 2023) ties GPC to Samsung.com cookies.

where: Samsung Privacy Policy > US Supplement > Ad networks
what_it_does: Samsung points US users to industry opt-out pages to opt out of ad-network personalized advertising.
limits: Third-party tools; cover only participating networks.

control: Opt out of sensitive data processing / limit use of sensitive personal information (request)
where: Samsung Privacy Policy > US Supplement > State Law Privacy Rights; California Consumer Privacy Statement
what_it_does: US residents may request to opt out of collection or processing of sensitive data; California residents may request to limit its use and disclosure.
limits: Subject to applicable state law.

control: Access, Delete, Correct, List 3rd Parties, Appeal (requests)
where: US Privacy Rights Portal; 1-800-SAMSUNG
what_it_does: Request a copy, correction or deletion of personal data, a list of third-party recipients (Oregon), or appeal a decision.
limits: Deletion, not opt-out. Exemptions apply, and deletion may end access to services.

where: account.samsung.com > My Account > Profile > Manage Samsung account > Delete account
what_it_does: Permanently deletes the Samsung account with profile, purchase history, subscriptions and uploads.
limits: Deletion, not opt-out. Family organizers must delete child accounts first.

where: Samsung account settings > Family > child's account > Allowed apps
what_it_does: Parents can block a child account's use of services such as Bixby, Galaxy Wearable, SmartThings or Samsung Members.
limits: Parent or Family group role required. Samsung also says Galaxy AI may be limited for minors in some regions.

control: Health data AI training consent (label not shown in notice)
where: Samsung Health U.S. Privacy Notice > How We Use the Information We Obtain
what_it_does: With the user's consent, Samsung may use Samsung Health data to develop and train its AI models.
limits: Samsung Health, not core Galaxy AI; Health assist is a Galaxy AI feature. The notice says consents for processing health information can be withdrawn at any time in the Samsung Health settings, but it gives no label or separate path for the AI-training consent. July 2026 news reports not verified.

control: User Content License over AI Input and Output
where: Samsung Services Terms and Conditions > User Content; Advanced intelligence
what_it_does: Users grant Samsung an irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free license to content they provide, defined to include Input and Output of advanced intelligence features.
limits: Applies to the full extent allowed by law. Terms also bar users from using the features or outputs to train other AI models.

where: Product > Trust and reliability > Data governance and privacy
what_it_does: Personal information (PII) that end users share with an agent is automatically encrypted and masked.
limits: No list of PII types or where masking applies (transcripts, traces, model calls). A June 2025 blog says PII detection and encryption apply by default.

where: Blog: From LLMs to enterprise-grade agents > Reducing error rates
